title: A Panthers Player Said He Had to Change His Life. Four Games Later, It's Working
full_text:
I don't think Princely Umanmielen had a bad rookie season. He played in 16 games, had 24 tackles and 1.5 sacks, and for a rookie, that's not exactly something I'd be worried about.
Umanmielen obviously felt differently.
He looked back at his first year and decided there were things he needed to change. And I'm not talking about adding another pass-rush move or spending a little more time in the weight room. He started looking at how he was eating, sleeping, recovering, and pretty much everything else he was doing.
“I had to change my life,” Umanmielen told Panthers.com.
That's a pretty big statement for a guy coming off his rookie season. When I first read it, I wasn't really sure what to make of it. Now that we're four games into this season, it makes a little more sense.
Panthers.com went into everything Umanmielen changed during the offseason . His diet changed. Sleep became more important. So did recovery and what he was putting into his body.
We've all heard the offseason stories before. Somebody lost weight, somebody added muscle and somebody is supposedly in the best shape of his life. I usually don't pay much attention to those stories until I actually see something different on Sundays.
Well, I'm seeing something different with Umanmielen.
He already has three sacks through four games. That's twice as many as he had all of last season, and he's gotten a sack in three of Carolina's first four games.
According to Panthers.com , the last Panthers players to do that were Brian Burns and Haason Reddick in 2021.
I'm not saying that puts Umanmielen in that category. Three sacks isn't enough for me to start doing that, but it's definitely enough for me to start wondering what this could turn into, especially when you go back to what he said about changing his life.
I know Umanmielen had already recorded sacks against Chicago and Cleveland, but the one against Detroit probably stood out to me the most.
Dave Canales actually thought Umanmielen was too fired up early in the game. He wasn't playing like himself, so Canales found him on the sideline and basically told him to calm down and trust that his opportunity would come.
“Just settle in, just do your job, your time is going to come,” Canales told him.
Later in the fourth quarter, there was Umanmielen getting to Jared Goff for a huge sack.
Maybe I'm reading too much into one play, but I liked that. A young player gets told he's trying to do too much, settles himself down, and then makes one of the biggest defensive plays of the game.
And really, that's kind of where I'm at with his season. I'm not ready to call Umanmielen a breakout player after four games. I've watched enough football to know three sacks can turn into three sacks through eight games pretty quickly.
But I've also watched him get to the quarterback in three of four games. I've seen him already double his sack total from last season, and now I know how much he changed, trying to make sure his second year didn't look like his first.
Maybe this keeps going. Maybe we look back in a couple of months and three sacks through four games was just a nice start.
Right now, though, I'm starting to believe Umanmielen when he says he needed to change his life.
Because something definitely changed.

title: Bryce Young Has a Secret Weapon Nobody Is Talking About
full_text:
If you asked me who Bryce Young's best target has been this season, I'd say Tetairoa McMillan. After watching him catch 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, I don't think I'd have to think about it very long.
Then I saw something from PFF that caught me off guard. Young has a 138.1 passer rating when targeting Chuba Hubbard this season, which ranks 14th among 152 qualifying quarterback-pass catcher combinations with at least 10 targets.
I'll be honest, Hubbard wasn't even close to the first guy I would've guessed.
I've written about Hubbard plenty this season, and most of the time it's been about the same thing: Give him the ball. I've wondered why Carolina has gotten away from the running game at times, and after Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, I probably won't stop talking about it anytime soon.
But I really haven't paid much attention to what he's doing when Young throws him the ball.
Hubbard has caught 10 of his 11 targets for 84 yards and two touchdowns through four games. It's only 11 targets, so we're not talking about a huge sample. Still, a 138.1 passer rating when Young goes his way is pretty hard for me to ignore. The EPA/play is highest when targeting Hubbard, too.
Maybe Carolina needs to find a few more ways to use him there. I'm not talking about turning Hubbard into a receiver or doing anything crazy. Get him the ball underneath, give him some room, and let him do what he does.
We just watched what can happen when Carolina gets Hubbard going against Detroit. The nice thing about using him in the passing game is Young doesn't have to make some difficult throw down the field for it to work. Sometimes it's just getting the ball out of his hands and letting Hubbard do the rest.
Young could probably use a little more of that.
That's where I started thinking about this a little differently, because Hubbard isn't really the story by himself.
Look at who Young has around him now. McMillan looks every bit like a No. 1 receiver through four games. Jalen Coker had eight catches for 138 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago, and Darren Waller has already shown he can give Young another option around the end zone.
Now Hubbard is sitting there as one of Young's most efficient targets.
I don't remember having this problem with Young before. For most of his career, we've spent our time asking whether Carolina had given him enough help. I know I've asked it plenty, and there were Sundays when it felt like Young had to make something happen even when there wasn't much happening around him.
I don't think we can say that anymore.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards and nine touchdowns through four games. He's playing better football, and I'm not taking anything away from what he's doing. But it sure helps when McMillan can go for 192 yards, Hubbard can give you something out of the backfield, and there are other guys Young can turn to when one of them isn't open.
That's a pretty big change from what we've watched around here the last few years.
I'm still taking McMillan if you ask me who Young's best target is. I'm not changing my answer because of one PFF number, especially after what McMillan just did against Detroit.
But seeing Hubbard's name that high did make me realize something. We've spent most of Young's career wondering if he had enough guys to throw to.
I'm not wondering that anymore.

title: Dave Canales Gave Up Something He Loved — It Might Be Saving the Panthers
full_text:
When Dave Canales announced before the season that he was giving up play-calling to Brad Idzik, I thought I understood why. Let Idzik call the offense and give Canales more time to worry about everything else that comes with being a head coach.
It made sense, but I was still mostly interested in what it would mean for Bryce Young and the offense. Four games later, I think I was looking at the wrong part of it.
Back in February, Canales explained why he was making the change in an interview with Panthers.com . He had gone back through the previous season and noticed things he was missing during games because he was so focused on calling the next play.
“Let's not wait until Monday, when I watch the film, to be able to help somebody,” Canales said.
Four games into the season, we're starting to see what he meant.
Canales admitted this week that he still misses calling plays. That's not surprising. He said the speed of making those decisions during a game is “really stimulating,” and it's pretty obvious he still loves that part of coaching.
But Darin Gantt of Panthers.com pointed out a couple of moments from the Detroit game that caught my attention.
Akayleb Evans was having a rough night. He had given up some plays, and Canales knew the Lions weren't going to stop coming after him. So he found Evans on the sideline, talked to him, and tried to get him ready for the next time Detroit came his way.
Canales had a similar conversation with Princely Umanmielen, whom he thought was a little too fired up early in the game and had gotten away from what he normally does. Canales told him, “Just settle in, just do your job, your time is going to come.”
Later, Umanmielen came up with a huge sack in the fourth quarter. He deserves the credit for making the play, but I think it matters that Canales noticed what was happening earlier and had the time to go talk to him. That's exactly what Canales was talking about back in February.
I've spent a lot of time looking at this move from the offensive side. Is Idzik a better play-caller? Is Young more comfortable with him? Why does the offense look so much better?
Maybe I've been asking the wrong questions.
Linebacker Bobby Okereke called Canales an “emotional intelligence savant” and said that giving up play-calling allows Canales to use that part of his personality more during games. We've heard plenty about how Canales relates to players since he got to Carolina. Now he actually has time during games to do something with it.
Canales can still have his hands on the offense during the week. He's part of putting the game plan together, and Idzik isn't running some completely different system. But once Sunday gets here, Canales doesn't have to spend the entire game worrying about the next offensive series.
The Panthers are 2-2, so I'm not saying they've suddenly figured everything out because Canales gave up play-calling. We watched Chicago score 59 points in Week 1. There's still plenty for this team to work on, and four games isn't enough to know how much this change will matter over an entire season.
But I keep going back to the question Canales asked when he made the decision in February: “Can I affect our whole team in a more positive way?”
I think we're starting to get the answer.
I thought giving up play-calling was mostly about finding out what Idzik could do with the offense. Maybe it was also about finding out what Canales could do as the head coach.

title: Bears Report Card for Week 5 Vs. Packers: Last in the NFC North Again
full_text:
After playing a quarter on Sunday — which seemed like much more than some members of the Bears secondary or their other backup quarterback played — third-string QB Case Keenum beat up one of the most overused phrases at Halas Hall in any given week.
He decided to talk about the team's "identity."
"This is a tough resilient group," Keenum told reporters at Lambeau Field. "We are fighters. We're a really good football team. I know it didn't show today. But gol-ly I think i know guys are going to come and get back to work, get their bodies back right, get their minds back right.
"It's a long season. There's a lot you find out about yourself at this point in the season, about you're becoming the team you're going to be. Your identity is forged, sometimes through fire. It was in fire today. It was in the fire today, so we will see what kind of identity we have coming out of the back end of this thing.”
Too often Sunday the Bears looked like their identity was what really does come out of the back end.
As a result, they are now in last place in the NFC North.
Chicago Bears fans already turning on Ben Johnson 😂😂😂 pic.twitter.com/GnqRXomvs1
At the risk of channeling everyone's inner Dennis Green, they are who we thought they were. Their identity was obvious long before Sunday. They're a running team, a ball-control team and they need to take risks on defense to make up for personnel deficiencies. When they don't have Caleb Williams, they're all struggling on both sides of the ball.
The deficiencies were apparent everywhere on Sunday and here are their grades for a throwback game in Green Bay — the kind you throw back and an effort similar to those games they would play in the bad old days at Lambeau when Aaron Rodgers was Packers QB.
A 3.4-yard average per carry made it quite apparent how much the Bears missed Kyle Monangai. Early on, some of the running lanes were there but they closed gradually and eventually the Bears abandoned the run anyway. Only nine rushes for 43 yards for D'Andre Swift as he made his rebound from his egregious game against the Jets. Sunday, the whole offense was egregious. The one rushing positive was Swift's 1-yard fourth-and-goal TD burst up the middle. It was a tough play to pull off. If only Swift had done that against Minnesota instead of fumbling in that game.
rome odunze fumble issue now? #dabears B U S T one of the worst chicago bears of my lifetime man pic.twitter.com/TYwsw0VE9J
Tyson Bagent's 27.4 passer rating places him first place for the Rex Grossman Sweepstakes this year (0.00). Bagent's two interceptions were similar, even if one was tipped. They were late, over the middle and his arm can't deliver that type of pass. Keenum didn't get great pass protection but at that point in the game it's difficult to keep the passer free of traffic because the defense knew he was passing. At least he didn't eat the ball and take a sack on the fourth-down interception he threw, the way Bagent did in Chicago against the Vikings. Another typically disappointing week for the Bears receivers, especially Rome Odunze.
This might be one of the worst passes I’ve seen a Bears QB throw and that says a lot pic.twitter.com/tuW2i63pTB
It would be easy to look bottom line and 2.7 yards per carry with 70 total rushing yards says they did a fantastic job. However, they gave up a key 10-yard run to MarShawn Lloyd and later a 23-yard run to Kaleb Johnson. If they could duplicate this effort the rest of the year they wouldn't mind it.
Bears defense lets Watson score with ease pic.twitter.com/kRKkGp19ze
Even Austin Booker's sacks of Jordan Love on consecutive second-quarter plays couldn't cover for a pass rush lacking much life. Montez Sweat was held without a penalty call on the first Packers pass of the game, and Green Bay then drove 91 yards to a TD. Dillon Thieneman allowed two long TDs and Malik Muhammad struggled once the Bears moved him outside after Tyrique Stevenson's hamstring injury. Those two rookies making mistakes are anticipated. Seeing Jaylon Johnson beaten twice deep and six Love completions of 31 yards or longer says they need to bring Kyler Gordon back this week full time even if their plan said to gradually work him into the mix.
Zavion Thomas finally broke a kick return for 61 yards but that 4.28-second speed didn't keep him from being caught from behind. He veraged a healthy 26.2 yards on his other five returns. Cairo Santos missing a 43-yard field goal just doesn't happen. The snap by Scott Daly was a bit high but it was easily a kick Santos normally makes blindfolded.
Packers WR Matthew Golden appeared to intentionally knock over a Bears coach on the sideline and Bears K Cairo Santos tried to trip him out of retaliation. (🎥: NFL on FOX) pic.twitter.com/wK4DqcuGs1
Ben Johnson's game plan probably wasn't the kind of problem the execution was, but it was Dennis Allen's game plan on the other side that really caused problems. Too many of their DB blitzes got picked up and the wound up exposing their young DBs to Packer big-play attempts. When the Packers really had no running game to speak of, it should have been much easier for the Bears to scheme up heat on Love in the passing game. They still couldn't do it without blitzing.
Luther Burden said this week the Bears wanted to make the #Packers quit. Zaire Franklin heard the comments. "He quit today, by the way. He didn't want to play anymore." pic.twitter.com/aA34RXZoFw
The final score doesn't say the Bears were in it at halftime but they really weren't not long after that. At least they didn't telegraph their weakness shutting down the running game because that's the way the Falcons will attack them next week.
Entire chat during @ChicagoBears Press Conference saying we suck and the season is over. "Bears Won't Make The Playoffs" ect ect We started 0-2 last year and had to get a couple of miracles to get to 3-2 This year we are 3-2 with our backup QBs starting 3 games. #Bears pic.twitter.com/sRQ9KDVDrT

title: NFL Insider: 'All Signs Point To' Caleb Williams Returning From Injury For Bears in Week 6
full_text:
If there's one thing clear after the Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers, it's that the Chicago Bears need Caleb Williams back.
After the debacle that was Tyson Bagent's showing on Sunday, all eyes are now on Williams, who is hoping to return for the Week 6 contest against the Atlanta Falcons.
On Monday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport laid out the situation with Williams and he said that "all signs point to" Williams making his return after a three-week absence.
"My understanding at the beginning of this whole thing was three to four weeks with a hamstring. He has missed three weeks," Rap said. "All signs point to Caleb Williams being back on the field this week for Chicago, which considering the way it went this past Sunday, would be quite good news."
Rapoport is basing that on all of the evidence we've seen since last week that shows Williams is, at the very least, very close.
Optimism for Williams' Week 6 return has been building up since Friday, when the Bears signal-caller took part in his first practice since he suffered the Grade 2 hamstring strain in Week 2.
After the limited session, Williams was given the questionable tag before being made inactive on Sunday. However, the bigger note was how Williams was working out on the field before kickoff and seemed to be moving around perfectly fine.
#Bears QB Caleb Williams warming up pregame vs. Packers at Lambeau Field. Williams is questionable (hamstring) today. @fox32news pic.twitter.com/Y5KO7NDNdW
We also know, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , that Williams is "pushing to play" this coming Sunday.
"Really good news for the Bears the other day, with Caleb Williams returning to practice with that hamstring injury," Garafolo said.
"Not good news for (Week 5), really for next week, because this is Williams starting to work his way back and pushing to play next week. That's what I am told by multiple sources here," Garafolo went on to add. "The team is going to see how he does through the course of the week, so we really don't know how this is going to go, but this is Williams trying to get back right on the timeline."
After the loss to Green Bay, even head coach Ben Johnson would not rule out Williams making his return against the Falcons.
"(Williams is) on track," Johnson said . "We'll see if that's Atlanta or after. I think it's going to be close."
Not hard to see why Rapoport is saying "all signs point to" Williams making his return in Week 6. Every key indicator tells us that.
Now, we wait for our next injury update on Williams, which could come from Johnson on Monday, or from the injury report on Wednesday.

title: Bears' Tyson Bagent Destroys His Trade Value Against the Packers
full_text:
Chicago Bears backup quarterback Tyson Bagent had an opportunity to cement his status as one of the league's premier backup QBs in the team's Week 5 clash against Green Bay.
Many expected him to do just that, as the Bears were favored by 1.5 points at Lambeau Field for the first time in 20 years. The experts also liked Chicago's odds of coming out on top.
Unfortunately, Bagent fell well below expectations in the team's 31-7 loss. In fact, he had one of the worst passing performances we've seen from any QB over the first month of the season. Bagent completed only 12 of 21 attempts for 87 yards and threw two interceptions.
Bagent didn't even finish the contest, as he got benched for Case Keenum late in the game. While every QB has rough performances, this one feels especially consequential for a quarterback who wants to start in the league eventually. This might've been his last chance to start, with Caleb Williams progressing nicely as he returns from a strained hamstring he suffered in Chicago's Week 2 matchup against Minnesota.
Conversations surrounding Bagent's trade value have always been interesting. Many believed that he was one of the league's premier backup QBs. He showed a lot of promise in virtually every preseason opportunity he received.
That fact, combined with him still being only 26 years old, has led some to believe that they might be able to receive quality draft compensation for him if they decided to go that route. Ben Johnson even called him one of the league's 32 best signal-callers when asked about potentially trading him at the NFL Scouting Combine.
Ben Johnson doesn’t want the Bears to trade QB Tyson Bagent but acknowledges that they have to do what’s best for the team He believes Bagent is one of the best 32 QBs in the NFL pic.twitter.com/OwGJVVYr8M
However, that ship feels like it sailed today. Fair or not, there was always going to be a minimal margin for error in order for another team to take a chance on Bagent. He's not a former first-round selection like J.J. McCarthy in Minnesota. Bagent went undrafted in 2023.
Johnson surely developed his opinion through seeing Bagent in practice and the way he carries himself at Halas Hall. Other teams aren't privy to that information. All they can depend on is live game action. In the preseason, Bagent can sling it with the best of them. His turnover rate is far too high when the games start to matter, though.
Counting Bagent's four starts in 2023, he now has a career 3-9 touchdown-to-interception ratio. Penalties negated three more picks last week. Even if an injury strikes, he puts the ball in harm's way far too often to be considered a viable starting option for another team.
This conversation was probably not going to be reignited this season. Williams might be back next week, but hamstring injuries can be tricky. The re-injury risk alone would be enough for them to keep Bagent around, regardless of how well he played (or any offers they received) in his absence.
He's only under contract for one more season, though. The 2027 campaign will be his last in Chicago, and some theorized Keenum's strong showing against Philadelphia might be enough validation to send him to the highest bidder this offseason.
The asking price just went down considerably, though. Would anyone even be interested in trading for him? Certainly not as a viable starting option. A trade would only make sense now if Chicago wanted to get his contract off the books a year early.

title: How Noah Sewell’s PUP Return Restructures Bears LB Depth Chart Post-Edwards Injury
full_text:
The Chicago Bears lost middle linebacker T.J. Edwards on Sunday to a hamstring injury during a 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers . It's currently unclear how long Edwards will be on the shelf.
Noah Sewell's reactivation from the reserve/PUP list on Saturday after recovering from an Achilles tear couldn't have come at a more opportune time for the linebacker room. Sewell suffered the injury during Week 17 of the 2025 season against the San Francisco 49ers. Santa Clara, California, claimed another major injury last December.
Sewell stepped in at the Sam linebacker spot after D'Marco Jackson stepped into the green-dot play-caller spot for Edwards in Week 5. Devin Bush also saw increased opportunities in the box.
Jackson had four tackles, with two of them coming unassisted. Sewell had one assisted tackle in his return to action.
Those two are the keys to the post-Edwards injury depth chart.
Now is the toughest part for Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen. He needs to play a balancing act with Sewell's recovery and the ability to field the most competitive defense possible amid a 3-2 start.
Chicago is tied for last place in the division and still have no clear timetable on Caleb Williams' recovery. Neither Tyson Bagent nor Case Keenum inspired much hope for the offense against Green Bay. Bagent has been unimpressive for several weeks now after having throwing four interceptions against the New York Jets and having three brought back for penalties. Keenum is 38.
There's no time to waste. If Sewell can suit up, he has to take as many snaps as he can get. The defense needs to be a strong suit until Williams is fully healthy. Especially otherwise.
In 13 games played last season, Sewell had 59 total tackles, a forced fumble, and 6.5 stuffs at the line of scrimmage. Sewell helped establish a strong identity against the run last year. He'll reprise that role in 2026.
Jackson owns a 53.1 grade against the run. Jackson is far stingier in coverage, though. Both he and Bush will need to play major roles in the passing game.
Edwards struggled against the run, grading out as a 46.2 in PFF's metrics. That ranked No. 71 of 74 qualified linebackers.
Allen needs to lean in on using Sewell on early downs to prevent opposing attacks from moving the chains and establishing rhythm.
As for Jackson, his responsibilities expand ten-fold. Jackson was signed as a special teams player but has been asked to do more by the coaching staff.
Jackson is now an every-down player whose coverage abilities will help cover a secondary that also took injury losses on Sunday.
Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson left the game with a hamstring injury as well.
Allen has been hit with plenty of injuries before. 2025 was a rough year for the Bears defense health-wise.
Allen will have to do it again.

title: Bears Week 5 Stock Report: Tyson Bagent Leads 4 Crashing, Austin Booker Among 4 Rising
full_text:
A team just cannot play worse than what the Chicago Bears put on tape against the Green Bay Packers in Week 5.
Absolutely nothing went right for Chicago on Sunday. The defense started looking more like we expected it to this season and the offense saw putrid quarterback play throughout the contest.
We know things can change quickly in the NFL, and the Bears are a perfect example of that. In the span of a week, they went from riding high to full-blown crisis mode on both sides of the ball.
You can tell just how badly things went by the fact that three of the guys who saw their stocks rise didn't even play on Sunday. Check out who those players are and the ones who saw their stock go down in our Week 5 stock report below.
Remember when there were reportedly teams around the NFL that were interested in trading for Bagent? So much for that.
The Shepherd product was downright awful in Week 5, with the fourth-year signal-caller completing just 57% of his passes for only 87 yards and two interceptions. Bagent has now failed to throw any touchdowns over two games.
If Caleb Williams doesn't play in Week 6, the Bears should turn to Keenum, who, quite frankly, wasn't any better in his quarter of action. We'll give Keenum a pass, though, as he came into a terrible situation in the fourth quarter.
After what we saw out of Bagent and Keenum on Sunday, it's now more important than ever that the Bears get Williams back this week.
Thankfully, there's a chance that happens. Williams got on the comeback trail on Friday with a limited practice, and he was spotted doing some rehab work before the game.
Then, after the game, head coach Ben Johnson left the door open for Williams to possibly return in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons.
"He's on track," Johnson said . "We'll see if that's Atlanta or after. I think it's going to be close."
Just a guess, but we think Williams makes it back in Week 6.
One of the few bright spots in a horrifically bad game, Booker had a pair of sacks, five tackles, three tackles for loss and four run stops.
With four sacks this season, Booker now leads the team, and he is just one half of a sack away from his career-high. His contribution will be even more important in Week 6 if Dayo Odeyingbo doesn't play after getting hurt on Sunday.
Muhammad had his worst game as a pro, allowing six receptions on six targets for 124 yards and a passer rating of 118.8 while playing 29 snaps on the boundary and 11 in the slot, per Pro Football Focus .
While he does get a "stock down" designation, we're not going to panic about the rookie yet. It's just one game and Muhammad has been Chicago's best cornerback by a mile this season.
With how badly the secondary got torched on Sunday afternoon, Bears fans are ready for Gordon's return more than ever.
Getting Gordon back in the lineup will push Muhammad to the outside, where Tyrique Stevenson and Jaylon Johnson should be in a competition for the other starting spot on the boundary with how poorly Johnson has played this season.
Gordon thankfully appears to be close, as he has logged all full practices the past few weeks. After what we saw in Week 5, we expect to see Gordon activated off the PUP list in Week 6.
We got pretty much what we expected out of Johnson on the ground in place of an injured Kyle Monangai: nothing.
Johnson carried the rock five times for six yards, which reminded us of the fact that he's just never going to be anything more than a special teams contributor in Chicago. If Monangai misses another game, we'd like to see either Zavier Scott or Salvon Ahmed spell D'Andre Swift.
With Johnson struggling to provide an adequate two in the one-two punch in Chicago's backfield, it only reminded us more of just how effective Monangai can be on the ground.
Monangai's turf toe injury could sideline him multiple weeks, and based on the fact that he didn't practice at all last week and was spotted in a boot suggests that might be more likely to happen than not.
What we can say for sure is that the Bears need Monangai back after he has proven to be their most consistent back in 2026.
Johnson's downfall needs to be studied. This just can't be the same guy who used to be an elite NFL cornerback.
PFF only credited Johnson with giving up two catches on three targets for 48 yards, but he should be guilty of more.
It was Johnson who was caught napping while Christian Watson streaked down the field for his second touchdown catch of the game. PFF blamed Dillon Thieneman for that, but the rookie literally had to cross the field just to try and make a play.
Jaylon Johnson did his best pic.twitter.com/SNHtGJWWv4
One play before that, Johnson got beat for another big pass play that would have been a touchdown if it wasn't negated because of a penalty. Then, Matthew Golden beat him rather easily for a 36-yard reception later in the contest.
As if all that wasn't enough, Johnson got trucked badly on MarShawn Lloyd's touchdown run.
There is no doubt about it, Johnson is heading toward getting cut next offseason.

title: Caleb Williams' Status Not Bears' Only QB Question After Blowout Loss
full_text:
The only thing more elusive than Green Bay receivers on Sunday was Bears coach Ben Johnson when talking about whether Caleb Williams would be ready to return against Atlanta in Week 6.
"He's on track," Johnson said. "We'll see if that's Atlanta, or after. I think it's going to be close."
No sense giving the Falcons a head start on what to prepare for, because if it isn't Williams what is there really to prepare to face? The Bears backup quarterbacks were that bad in Sunday's 31-7 loss to the Packers.
Johnson said the approach will be like last week.
"We'll do the same thing we do every week," he told reporters after Sunday's loss. "We'll talk as a staff, we'll recap this game, and we'll make a decision going into next week on what's best for us."
As bad as the final score sounded, the Bears were still very much in it at halftime despite the opportunity given away with the first interception quarterback Tyson Bagent threw on a tipped ball to Xavier McKinney. Bagent had only 54 yards passing at the half, though.
Johnson had every bit of opportunity to pull his starter on the day at halftime or even a bit later with hope Keenum could rally them.
Ben Johnson on when it was time to Bench Tyson Bagent: “It was after the Second Interception.” Ben is PISSED 😭 pic.twitter.com/EF7pkH0Sq8
The Bears actually had the ball back at their own 10 in the final 1:22 of the second quarter and with three timeouts, trailing only by a touchdown, they could have made it a game. They went nowhere, Bagent was sacked and then when the Packers started the second half a 53-yard TD pass to Christian Watson by Jordan Love over Dillon Thieneman made it a two-TD deficit.
And stillJohnson wouldn't bench Bagent. Finally, he did it in the fourth quarter when the verdict already seemed sealed.
Tyson Bagent was a great story, loved rooting for the dude. He played so bad today that I am having flashbacks of Crag Krenzel I wish fans were able to talk about a player having a bad game without only saying “He sucks” “he has a noodle arm” ect Where is the real football…
"We felt like we wanted a little spark there," Johnson told reporters.
At that point they needed a bolt of lightning rather than a spark.
"Tyson just could never feel like he got in a rhythm here today. we'll look at why that was the case," Johnson said. "The second interception happened and we felt like lets give Case a chance out there and see if we get different results."
Once again, I think Ben Johnson is a dummy for starting Tyson Bagent over Case Keenum… I caught a lot of flack from Bears fans for this take last week, but I still believe I’m right. Should’ve stuck with the hot hand. pic.twitter.com/jp2pv6Dti1
What was somewhat curious — or perhaps not — the Bears had Case Keenum talking to reporters at the podium in the postgame interview room while Bagent was accessed in the locker room by a handful of reporters. Usually the starter gets the podium treatment.
Were they communicating something about Keenum being ahead of Bagent now in case Williams isn't ready to go next week? Has Bagent dropped to No. 3?
"You would definitely not want to be benched in a game like this, especially with the opportunity that I've been blessed with," Bagent told CHGO afterward. "But at the end of the game these things happen.
Tyson Bagent has helped Caleb Williams through his work ethic, preparation, knowledge of the playbook, film study, attention to detail, and ability to recognize defensive schemes, helping Caleb develop the mental side of quarterbacking. Go Bears #nfl #chicagobears pic.twitter.com/S4Uc2teZ8r
"I've got to play better and, like I said, I've got to look in the mirror and got to see where I can continue to get better, because there's a lot of things still even this far into my career that I can still get better at."
In honestly, Keenum was barely better than Bagent in terms of actual production, even though he threw for 108 yards in one quarter of play on 11 of 19. They turned it over on three of his four possessions, once by interception.
Stop trying to make Tyson Bagent a thing… He’s not an nfl caliber QB
"We'd get something going and then put ourselves in a tough spot," Keenum said. "That was kind of the name of the game today."
The interception Keenum threw was on a fourth down when they would have turned it over on downs if he didn't force it into coverage.
Who is worse at their job - Tyson Bagent or Jaylon Johnson?
Afterward, Keenum was focusing his attention on his friend and young teammate, Bagent.
"You don't last very long in this league if you don't know how to get back up when you've got your ass kicked," Keenum said. "That's just the way it is. There's really good players, really good coaches, really good teams, and if you last long enough it's just a matter of time at some point you get your ass kicked. "And it's not about that. It's about how you respond the next day, the next week and every day after that. I expect him to respond like he knows how to and he can."
Bears fans have to hope it just won't be until the distant future because Williams' return could be the next game.
There’s no chance Tyson Bagent has any trade value. The coverage of him in Chicago has always been strange but that’s basically over at this point. #Bears

title: Ben Johnson Explains Decision to Bench Tyson Bagent in Bears' Loss to Packers
full_text:
One week after he led the Chicago Bears to a convincing win over the New York Jets in Week 4, the wheels came completely off for Tyson Bagent in the Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
Bagent was not anywhere near as sharp as he was last week, with the fourth-year signal-caller completing just 12-of-21 passes for 87 yards and no touchdowns to two interceptions.
After three putrid quarters from Bagent, head coach Ben Johnson had seen enough and decided to bench Bagent for Case Keenum, who didn't fare much better.
Following the contest, Johnson said he decided to bench Bagent after his second interception in the third quarter and said he was looking for a spark from Keenum, which Chicago didn't get.
"We felt like we just wanted a little spark there," Johnson said of the decision. "Tyson just could never feel like he got in a rhythm here today, and so we'll look at why that was the case. The second interception happened, and we just felt like let's give Case a chance out there and see if we get different results."
“It was after the Second Interception," Johnson said of when he decided to pull the plug on the Shepherd product.
That second interception came in the third quarter, when Bagent threw a bad pass to Colston Loveland. The first interception was even worse, as Bagent threw to a clearly covered Luther Burden before McKinney picked that one off, also.
Keenum entered the game in the fourth quarter, but he didn't even come close to changing Chicago's fortunes. Not only did Keenum toss a pick, he also lost a fumble.
In all, Keenum was 11-of-18 for 108 yards, so he actually out-produced Bagent in one quarter, although he was obviously throwing a lot more often with the Bears down big.
After what we saw on Sunday, it's hard to have any confidence in either Bagent or Keenum. What is clear is the Bears need to go with the latter after Bagent's debacle in Week 5.
The hope, of course, is that neither one will be needed and Caleb Williams will make his return to the field . Johnson didn't close the door on that happening after the loss to the Packers.
"He's on track," Johnson said . "We'll see if that's Atlanta or after. I think it's going to be close."
Williams showed progress last week with a limited practice Friday , and he was getting in some rehab work before kickoff on Sunday, so Johnson isn't kidding when he says Williams is close.
The sense of urgency to get Williams back on the field has just been raised by a significant amount after the loss to Green Bay. We fully believe Williams is going to play next Sunday, but that's just a prediction and nothing has been confirmed yet.

title: Bears, Packers Trade Costly Injuries in Ugly Chicago Loss at Lambeau Field
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were the unluckier team during an ugly 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on Sunday.
Both franchises come out of this game with potentially substantial injuries, though.
Chicago lost linebacker T.J. Edwards to a non-contact hamstring injury. Edwards was originally questionable to return but was quickly ruled out in Week 5 . With Edwards out, D'Marco Jackson took over primary play-calling and communication leading duties for the defense. Noah Sewell took over on the strong side. Sewell just returned from the reserve/PUP list on Saturday.
Those weren't the only losses for the Bears either. Defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo, corner Tyrique Stevenson, and safety Cam Lewis all left the game, too. Odeyingbo had a quadriceps injury, Stevenson also had a hamstring issue, and Lewis had a hip issue.
Meanwhile, Green Bay lost defensive tackle Javon Hargrave to an Achilles tear. Hargrave's availability was in question coming into this contest , but will now miss the rest of the year once he has season-ending surgery.
Packers head coach Matt LaFleur confirmed Hargrave's injury and service during the postgame press conference, saying "It doesn't look good."
Hargrave joins a long list of Green Bay defenders with long-term absences. The Packers had just lost linebacker Edgerrin Cooper to a season-ending Achilles issue last week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Green Bay also lost receiver Skyy Moore to an ankle injury and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste to a hamstring injury on Sunday.
This won't be the first time Ben Johnson and Co. have had to adjust to injuries.
Starting quarterback Caleb Williams has been out with his own hamstring issue, while top running back Kyle Monangai has turf toe. In the secondary, safety Coby Bryant is likely out for the remainder of the season, while nickel Kyler Gordon is just now working his way back.
Meanwhile, LaFleur and defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon have been going through it all season as well with the personnel losses.
EDGE Micah Parsons has been out since last December with a torn ACL and meniscus repair in his left knee. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele tore his patellar tendon in Week 2. Receiver Jayden Reed needs neck surgery. Running back Chris Brooks is out with an ankle injury.
These two NFC North teams appear to have a hex placed on their health this year.
From the looks of it, Gannon had the Packers' defense up to snuff against the Bears on Sunday.
On the other side, Dennis Allen needs to figure out how to continue keeping his defense cohesive as the injuries continue to pile up.
In 2025, the unit was able to lead the league in turnovers as a band-aid. This season, there's a higher baseline, but the injuries piling up could complicate that.
Chicago has had a strong start defensively, ranking in the top 10 across many categories before Sunday's disastrous showing against Jordan Love and the rest of Green Bay's offense.
Allen must continue to instill a "next man up" philosophy to sustain the defense as the offense looks to reintegrate its banged-up pieces.

title: Bears Succeed Against Packers Only at Proving Caleb Williams' Value
full_text:
The return of Caleb Williams can't come fast enough.
Williams appeared on the verge of a return for Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons during pregame warmups Sunday at Lambeau Field, and after the Bears went down early, then couldn't rally against the Green Bay Packers in their 31-7 loss, the need to get him back became entirely apparent.
The Packers realized something other Bears opponents haven't, and that's the way the Bears are winning is with ball control while they have had to use backup quarterbacks. So Packers coach Matt LaFleur wanted to control the ball instead of attacking. His problem is he has no running game and he found a way to do it with a short passing game enough early to let the Packers build a 14-0 lead. Game, set and match.
The Packers did such a good job of keeping the ball away from the Bears in the first quarter without a running game that they thought they'd try another maneuver in the second half. They left the bag with the game balls in the locker room at halftime. It only worked for a few seconds, but no need to worry. They only had Tyson Bagent to overcome.
Tipped and picked by Xavier McKinney! @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RhgsGoEbmk
Bagent is not better than some of the starting quarterbacks in the NFL as the Bears have maintained. He's not even better than some of the best backups. His floaty throw over the middle got picked off by Xavier McKinney in the first quarter after coaches and Bagent himself had warned all week about the Packers safeties.
That led to the 14-0 deficit and for all intents and purposes the game had ended. He threw another interception later in much the same manner and finished 12-of-21 for only 87 yards.
HOPPER INTERCEPTION pic.twitter.com/tqg1HBWDSc
Once the Packers' had the lead, they appropriately trashed their ball-control tactics and went deep after the Bears' rookie defensive backs, Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad. They were even able to victimize veteran Jaylon Johnson a few times.
With the comeback king inactive, Bagent was only capable of handing off in a running attack suddenly tremendously ineffective with Kyle Monangai out injured. Bagent is 0-3 in road starts for his career and seven of his nine interceptions came in road games.
After that game… I’m giving Caleb Williams 75M a year Talk about the ghost of Bearsmas past with Tyson Bagent starting I might even give him more #Bears
Backup quarterbacks can only do so much, whether it's Bagent or 38-year-old Case Keenum, who played the fourth quarter and led three drives ending in turnovers. Keenum was 11 of 19 for 108 yards with an interception.
If you want to grate some cheese at Soldier Field or Lambeau, it has to be with Williams playing.
Fortunately for the Bears, Williams' return appears close at hand. It will need to be because the Falcons play ball control very well and they do it with an actual running game, not a passing game.

title: 3 Winners and 4 Losers From the Bears Week 5 Blowout Loss Against Green Bay
full_text:
Nothing went right for the Chicago Bears in their 31-7 loss against the Green Bay Packers today. It was as demoralizing of a defeat as you will ever see, and both teams now sport 3-2 records.
Despite coming into the contest with all the momentum in the world and the experts fully on their side , they fell completely flat on both sides of the ball. It was actually much easier to sift through the lousy performances to find winners than it was narrow down the losers from the game.
Which players stand out as the most significant on both fronts?
The Packers' defense hasn't shown much promise this season, but they had their best performance today. Following a promising performance (aside from turnover-worthy plays) against the Jets, Tyson Bagent looked like an inexperienced backup quarterback playing in a hostile environment. In fact, he was downright terrible.
His two interceptions were completely unacceptable. First, he forced a pass to Luther Burden III blanketed in double coverage, rather than taking the wide-open checkdown to Colston Loveland. His second was potentially even more egregious, as he didn't even see the defender sitting directly in the passing lane.
Bagent eventually got benched early in the fourth quarter for Case Keenum. He unfortunately tarnished any opportunity the Bears would have to trade him for quality draft capital in the offseason.
Austin Booker was easily the best player on Chicago's defense today. He brought down Jordan Love for two sacks in the span of three plays to end the first half, and nearly got to him a handful more times throughout the contest. Green Bay's makeshift offensive line had no answers for him.
Booker now has four sacks over the first five games. He's enjoying a pretty substantial year-three leap. You could make a case that his performance was the only real positive performance today.
Rome Odunze is coming off one of the best performances of his career . Unfortunately, he failed to build on it. He dropped a pass over the middle on a third-down in the second quarter (it was a tough catch, but it hit him square in the hands) and fumbled the ball midway through the fourth.
To Odunze's credit, nothing, and I mean absolutely NOTHING, went right on offense. Odunze's fumble was one of five turnovers. Odunze had a chance to stop the bleeding, though. He (literally) fumbled away that opportunity.
Rookie receiver Zavion Thomas finally showed some promise in the return game. He nearly broke a much-needed touchdown early in the fourth quarter before Green Bay's return unit brought him down after a gain of 61. Who knew it would only take six kick return attempts to get him going? Chicago's defense should play like this more often if they want to get the most out of their third-round pick.
Thomas took his lone rushing attempt for 11 yards on an end-around. He also hauled in his only target for 11 yards. It really didn't take much to stand out as one of Chicago's biggest winners today.
Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson has lost his touch. The rough start to his season continued against Green Bay, and today's performance might've been the worst of his career. After getting run over on the goal line for Green Bay's second touchdown, he gave up 40+ yards on back-to-back plays early in the third quarter.
The first was negated by an offensive pass interference, but that doesn't change the fact that Johnson got beat on the play (against undrafted rookie J Michael Sturdivant). Christian Watson then beat him for a 53-yard TD on the next play. Johnson got completely left in the dust. He might be a cut candidate in the offseason if his early performances are a sign of things to come.
D'Andre Swift was the Bears' lone bright spot on the offensive side of the ball. The veteran running back rebounded strongly after a rough performance against New York, finishing the game with nine attempts for 43 yards and Chicago's lone touchdown.
There was an obvious disparity between him running the ball and backup Roschon Johnson running the ball. The latter, who finished the game with five attempts for six yards, consistently fails to find running lanes when they're there. The former shows flashes whenever he gets any room to operate.
Simply put, Green Bay didn't need a running game today. I'm going to try to avoid Jordan Love's passing chart at all costs this week. He was hitting throws all over the field, and they were occasionally wide open. It's been an overwhelmingly positive season for defensive coordinator Dennis Allen's unit after a rough Week 1 performance, but today's game couldn't have been worse.
Packers head coach Matt LaFleur clearly came out on top in the schematic battle against Allen. They'll be licking their wounds this week and will be extra motivated to bounce back next week against Atlanta.

title: Joe Burrow Reflects on Dominant Play in One Area During Bengals Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' backs were up against the wall coming into Week 5. After back-to-back losses, it felt that a loss to the winless Miami Dolphins would have sparked even more uncomfortable conversations around the team.
It wasn't the cleanest performance, but the Bengals got back in the win column with a 31-24 victory over the Dolphins. There are certainly some things that need to be cleaned up, however, quarterback Joe Burrow was on his A-game.
After his impressive performance on Sunday, Burrow spoke with the media and was asked specifically about his effectiveness in the red zone.
"Our receivers did a good job of finding space. We didn't get a ton of man coverage, but when we did, we made them pay," Burrow explained. "We had good field position most of the day, and I think for the most part we took advantage of it. But we had some dumb mistakes, and we got to get those fixed if we want to be a great team."
Three of Burrow's four touchdowns on Sunday were in the red zone. Like Burrow stated, if a team is going to give this offense good field position for the majority of the game, the unit has to make them pay. That's exactly what Burrow did.
Along with their red zone success, the Bengals converted 69.2% of their third down conversions. Extending drives is the name of the game, and this offense will bruise any defense if they can stay on the field.
This offense can be the most dynamic unit in the league. They proved that on Sunday. But there is still a lot to clean up before they take the field again in two weeks.
In particular, running back Chase Brown had some struggles hanging on to the football. The Bengals running back had two fumbles on the day.
Waiting for the Bengals out of the bye week is the Baltimore Ravens, who picked up a dramatic win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football. With the Bengals already suffering a loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, the game against the Ravens will be pivotal for the AFC North race.
Early bye weeks are brutal, but a reset at this point in the season may not be such a bad thing for a team that has already seen injuries to key players.

title: Zac Taylor Praises Toughness of 2 Bengals Offensive Stars After Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
After dropping two straight games, the Cincinnati Bengals found themselves in a must-win scenario when they took on the winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday.
In one of the hottest games played in the month of October, the Bengals put the past in the rearview, beating the Dolphins 31-24.
Was it a pretty game? No. But no team should ever apologize for winning a game in the NFL. It was a total team effort, and thankfully the Bengals' offense was near full strength.
During postgame comments with the media, Bengals head coach Zac Taylor spoke about the toughness of wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who suffered injuries in the team's Week 4 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
"Hats off to them. They wanted to play, and Ja'Marr had to clear protocol on Saturday. His mindset all along was, 'I'm playing,'" Taylor stated. " Now I hadn't seen him on the field enough to know. I appreciate him saying that, but I need to see him do it in practice, and he did. For those guys to go out there and make plays that they did for us is a big time. I don't ever question that."
Chase had to exit last week's game against the Jaguars after a dirty hit concussed him. For Higgins, it was an adductor injury that had him coming into the game with the Dolphins feeling less than 100%.
Both receivers made an impact on Sunday's game, but it was Chase who showed no signs of dealing with a head injury. The Bengals star receiver made an unbelievable touchdown grab on a 45-yard dime from Joe Burrow in the third quarter.
Chase finished Sunday's game leading the Bengals in receptions with six and receiving yards with 77. As for Higgins, it was a little bit of a quieter day. The seventh-year receiver finished the game with two receptions and 22 receiving yards.
With a bye week coming up, it's nice to see that two of the biggest concerns on the injury front got through Sunday's game. The goal now is to rest and gear up for a long stretch of games thanks to drawing an unfortunate early bye week.

title: 6 Winners and 3 Losers From Bengals' 31-24 Win Over Dolphins
full_text:
In a game that did not feel as close as the score indicated, the Bengals beat the Dolphins in Miami 31- 24 to improve to 3-2 on the season.
Here are six winners and three losers from the Bengals victory over the Dolphins.
Battle stepped up in a major way after his struggles last week. After calling out Malik Willis' tells as a quarterback early in the week, Battle delivered on the confidence he displayed with two key interceptions.
The secondary consistently limited Willis' options, making him force throws outside of his comfort zone. This kind of bounce-back performance is the exact one that Battle needed after a week filled with criticism.
Lawrence committed two costly back-to-back penalties to extend the Dolphins opening drive. The first happened on a field goal attempt where the referees called him for roughing the center, with the second coming directly after for holding.
The Bengals have found their return man for the foreseeable future. Meyers returned the opening kickoff for 81 yards, setting up a Mike Gesicki touchdown to take a seven point lead in only three plays. Despite his mistake later in the game where he accidentally stepped out of bounds on a kickoff deep in Bengals territory, Meyers has earned enough faith from the coaching staff to feel secure.
All has not changed the Bengals offense as much as many had hoped so far. Now after he had an opportunity to make that impact, it is fair to wonder if he will at this point. After committing a bone-headed penalty that negated a short kickoff, All had a fumble that Miami nearly recovered if not for the defenders toe hitting out of bounds.
Perine at this point looks to be the most trustworthy runner the Bengals have in their backfield. He caught a six-yard touchdown from Joe Burrow in the second-quarter, and gained more opportunities following a horrendous Chase Brown fumble in the red zone.
Perine finished with 16 touches for 78 yards, a touchdown, and an average of 4.9 yards per carry. After this performance, Zac Taylor has to dial up a more balanced attack between Brown and Perine as the former has been largely ineffective this season so far.
As mentioned above, Brown lost a fumble in the first-half in the red zone and failed to make any true impact as a ball carrier. He finished with 16 touches for 60 yards and 3 yards per carry. Brown has done little to show he is deserving a big extension with the Bengals in a contract year.
Burrow controlled the game from from start to finish. He finished the game with four touchdown passes and 23 completions for 190 yards, and looked as poised as ever. This is the performance everyone should expect from Burrow against a lesser opponent.
Mafe got to Willis often in the backfield and forced the Dolphins quarterback to make hasty decisions, and even got home for his 3rd sack of the season. He also hit Willis while throwing to force an interception early in the second-quarter. Mafe continues to look like the young ascending player that the Bengals wanted when they signed him in the offseason.
Allen had a critical strip-sack late in the fourth quarter that the Bengals recovered. The turnover gave the Bengals the chance to take a 31-18 lead late in what ended up being a one score margin of victory. He now has three sacks on the season and has played exceptionally in the role of a pass rusher.

title: 'Mr. Reliable' - Bengals RB Samaje Perine States Case for Bigger Role in Backfield
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals run game looked a lot different Sunday afternoon in Miami.
And in more ways than one.
Coming off last week’s historically bad performance, the Bengals not only upped the volume and the efficiency of the rushing attack, but they also leaned heavily into backup running back Samaje Perine on the way to a 31-24 victory against the winless Dolphins.
The Bengals had a season-high 31 rushing attempts, with Perine leading the team in both carries (14) and yards (68). He also caught a pair of passes, including a 6-yard touchdown that gave the Bengals the lead for good with 11:51 left in the second quarter.
Perine’s 4.9 yards per attempt were much better than Chase Brown’s numbers, which saw him carry 13 times for 39 yards.
“I think he was finishing an extra 2 or 3 (yards),” head coach Zac Taylor said of Perine. “Got a lot of confidence in Chase. Sometimes you got two great backs that you've got trust in. That's just the way it can go sometimes, and I don't think there's anything wrong with that.”
Brown has struggled to get going this season, and the heavier volume for Perine on Sunday could lead to more of a split load after the team returns from the bye week.
Perine’s 4.86 average Sunday was the fourth highest of his Cincinnati career in a game in which he had at least 10 carries.
“I think I am effective whenever my number is called, whenever I need to be,” Perine said. “As the game goes on, I feel like I do become a stronger runner, just because if the defense has been out there for a long time, I feel like I'm wearing on them a little bit.
“I'm a bigger back, so they don't want to hit bigger backs that often,” the 5-foot-11, 240-pounder added.
“I wouldn’t want to try to tackle him,” Bengals center Ted Karras quipped.
Perine’s 14 carries against the Dolphins are tied for his third most in a game as a member of the Bengals.
In back-to-back weeks in 2022, the year before the team drafted Brown, Perine had 22 carries against the Chiefs and 17 against the Titans.
And Sunday’s workload came on day that goes down as the hottest road game in Bengals history and hottest October game ever at Hard Rock Stadium, which opened in 1987.
“I feel fine,” Perine said. “A little tired. Dehydrated. But I feel decent.”
Overall, the Bengals finished with 32 passes and 31 rushes, although two of those were kneel downs by Burrow after the Dolphins’ last-ditch onside kick attempt failed.
That output comes after Taylor and quarterback Joe Burrow both extolled the need for a more balance in the wake of last week’s loss to the Jaguars.
It helped that the Bengals jump out to an early lead and were up by 14 at halftime and eventually led by 18.
“That's just the way the game was played out,” Taylor said of the heavier reliance on the running game. “They're trying to give you some underneath stuff and let you run the ball a little bit, when you're in the gun there. You got to take advantage of it and get some yards there. And take advantage of the shots when you get the favorable looks for them, which we did with (the touchdown to Ja’Marr Chase).
“Eventually, they got to come up if they're going to be in those shells, come up and make a play. I thought they did a great job. They're well coached on defense. I thought their guys tackled well and they gave us a run there. They made it hard.”
Had it not been for Perine’s effectiveness, the Bengals may not have been able to lean into the run as much as they did.
Part of the self-scouting that will go on during the bye week will no doubt involve discussions on whether to make Perine a bigger part of the rushing attack.
It sounded as though Burrow would be in favor of it with the praise he heaped on Perine after the game, both for what he brings in the run game and pass game.
“He's just Mr. Reliable, and he has been my entire time here since he's been on our team,” Burrow said. “You can count on him to fall forward and get us an extra two. You can count on him to win against the linebacker in coverage. He's such a valuable piece for us and certainly doesn't get enough credit for it.
“Downhill,” Burrow added when asked why Perine is such a good fit for the offense. “We count on him a lot in protection too on third down to go not just block linebackers, sometimes defensive linemen as well. And I feel really confident that if I get it to him in space on third down, he's going to go make it happen for us. He's just such a valuable piece for us.”

title: 'Not Good Enough All Around' - Joe Burrow Aiming Higher After Bengals Road Win Over Miami
full_text:
Joe Burrow got a win in the NFL on Sunday, but it didn't seem like it from his reserved press conference. He drove home the mistakes Cincinnati made multiple times in a 31-24 result over the now 0-5 Miami Dolphins.
Cincinnati is entering its bye week with another massive divisional game on the horizon against Baltimore.
Committing untimely penalties and sputtering out on three punting drives could be a losing recipe on the road again October 25.
"I think just not good enough all around," Burrow said. "Team-wide. I think if we want to be the team that we think we're going to be, we got to be better than that ... Our receivers did a good job of finding space. We didn't get a ton of man coverage, but when we did, we made them pay. They made a good play there on the last third down. We had good field position most of the day, an I think for the most part we took advantage of it. But we had some dumb mistakes, and we got to get those cleaned up if you want to be a great team."
It marked the 10th time in Burrow's career he's tossed four-plus touchdowns in a game (14th time with a 126-plus passer rating), but he's more worried about the big picture and clearly wants to keep moving forward and not dwell on any milestones like that.
He had big praise for the stars gutting through injuries to come back and make plays like Ja'Marr Chase and more did today.
"You see what number one can do whenever the ball's in the air," Burrow said about the crazy 45-yard TD catch and touching on his toughness. "Obviously, unbelievable play, but we don't want to take it for granted. But we're used to it at this point, you know. That's football, man. That's football. When you have great players that want to be great and want to be there for the team, that's what it's all about."
Cincinnati flies back tonight and disbands for a few days this week before getting back to it for the final two-thirds of the season.

title: 'Dead Tired' - Bengals, Zac Taylor  Navigate Fall Heat to Get Back on Track Entering Bye Week
full_text:
Zac Taylor's Bengals team worked its way through record heat in Florida today to get on the winning side of a 31-24 result entering the bye week.
Cincinnati is 3-2 on the season after taking on the Dolphins during a real-feel game of 104 degrees at kickoff (hottest in Hard Rock Stadium history). The big-time heat may have caused a few more of the controllable penalties and final-drive malaise to cut the score closer, but they are 3-2 entering a few days off.
They are still last in the division due to tiebreakers, but it was a huge win. According to RotoWire, No team in the past 10 seasons has started 2-3 and made the Super Bowl.
"Nothing really at this point in October gets you ready for this heat," Taylor said. "I mean, somebody told me it started as the hottest game here in October history, which I can attest to. I've coached here for four years, and pregame; I was worn out. And so our players fought through that.
"Yeah, I told them. I made that statement to them because I know they're dead tired right now, and I didn't want them to think that's just in their mind. They're like, 'What's wrong with me?' It was a hot day, and they battled through it, and they found a way to win. And I don't discount that at all."
Cincinnati got a strong, surgical-type day from Joe Burrow (190 yards, four touchdowns, 126.3 passer rating). Still they only posted 4.9 yards per play to Miami's 5.2.
He fed the offense the right way after a week of injury questions all over, while Jordan Battle had the team's first multi-INT game since 2023 to keep Miami under 25 points.
It wasn't clean, but a win is a win in a league as tough and closely competitive as this one.
"There are a lot of frustrating things on our end. We had two personal fouls. We fumbled twice in the red zone. We caught a kickoff on the four-yard line. We had a penalty on a field goal that led to a touchdown. Gave them four points. Gave up over 200 yards rushing," Taylor said. "So, plenty to clean up. The bye hits us at a great time. I know these guys are worn out. We've had some down to the wire games last three weeks.
"I know how hot this one was today. So the bye week comes at a great time for us to be 3-2. These guys will regroup. We know who we are today. There are a lot of things we have to clean up to be better when we go to Baltimore in two weeks."
Cincinnati gets an extended rest period before returning to practice for Baltimore game planning.

title: Joe Burrow Leads Bengals to Much-Needed Win Over Dolphins: Instant Takeaways
full_text:
The Bengals beat the Dolphins 31-24 on Sunday in Miami. Cincinnati never trailed in the contest, maintaining a double digit lead for most of the second half.
The Bengals are 3-2 on the season following the victory. They ended a 2-game losing streak and are back over
Here are our top takeaways from the Bengals' win:
Burrow was outstanding on Sunday. He completed 23-of-32 passes for 190 yards and a season-high four touchdowns. He found Mike Gesicki on Cincinnati's first possession for a 4-yard touchdown.
He connected with Samaje Perine on a 6-yard touchdown to give Cincinnati the lead for good. Tanner Hudson snagged Cincinnati's third touchdown of the game and then Ja'Marr Chase had one of the best catches you'll ever see in the third quarter to put the game out of reach.
Chase made a one-handed grab for a 45-yard touchdown. Watch the play here .
Chase led the Bengals with six catches for 77 yards and a score. Erick All had three receptions for 25 yards. Tee Higgns had two catches on four targets for 22 yards. Burrow completed passes to nine different players on the roster: four tight ends, two running backs and three wide receivers.
The Bengals leaned into their rushing attack on Sunday. Samaje Perine led the way with 14 carries for 68 yards. He also had two catches for 10 yards and a touchdown. Chase Brown had 39 rushing yards on 13 carries and three catches for 21 yards and a fumble.
Overall, the Bengals leaned into their shotgun running attack and were able to move the ball on the ground. Cincinnati finished wth 119 rushing yards.
Battle mentioned Malik Willis had a "tell" when throwing the ball. He took advantage of that and had two interceptions. He also had six tackles and two passes defensed.
The Bengals' defense responded well for most of the game after giving up a touchdown on the Dolphins' first possession. Battle has three interceptions on the season.
The Bengals forced a third turnover late in the game when they knocked the ball away from Willis. Jonathan Allen recovered to secure the victory. The Dolphins scored a touchdown in the final minute to cut the lead to single digits.
Evan McPherson made his 22nd consecutive field goal in the fourth quarter. That's a new franchise record, breaking Shane Graham's record (21 straight). McPherson is 9-for-9 this season and has been as good as any kicker in the NFL this year.
The Bengals desperately needed a win after back-to-back losses. There are plenty of things to clean up, from penalties to fumbles—especially in the first half, but Cincinnati went on the road and got a much needed win ahead of the bye week. They showed they could run the ball, their defense forced turnovers and Burrow played well without turning the ball over.
This Bengals team has a chance to be a real contender in the AFC. They have flaws, but there's a lot to like about this group.
The Bengals are on a bye in Week 6. They play the Ravens in Baltimore on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET.

title: 3 Biggest Problems in Browns Loss Sunday vs. Jets
full_text:
Sunday was a rude reminder that the ebbs and flows of the NFL can make you feel like you’re on top of the mountain or in a deep valley.
The Browns came in at 3-1, on fire after a primetime divisional win against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and they were quickly put out by the rain in the Meadowlands.
New York outlasted Cleveland 17-12 in a wet, sloppy game all around. The young aspect of this team showed up in a big-time way, and while they have pulled out three games in a row in the fourth quarter, these struggles were too much to overcome.
In total, today Cleveland rushed for 96 yards on 24 carries; 40 of those yards came from Deshaun Watson, and Quinshon Judkins rushed for 44 yards on 14 carries (3.1 YPC). Even though Judkins is coming off an injury, he has still not been able to crack over 4 yards per carry through the first five games.
The run-blocking has not been up to par with the pass-blocking, as Cleveland ranked 30th in the league in run-block win rate (70%) coming into the week , and 17th in pass-block win rate (49%). Hopefully Judkins is healthy also after leaving the locker room in a boot, but the run game needs to be better in order to win these close games.
The Browns were able to force two lost fumbles, along with two more fumbles that were recovered by New York, but unlike last week, they could not do anything with the ball when they got it.
The fumbles that Cleveland took away came in crucial spots also, the first coming with the Jets threatening inside the Cleveland 15-yard line with under six minutes to go in the third quarter, where Quincy Williams forced the ball out, and Ronnie Hickman was there to recover. The Browns then went three-and-out on three run plays and punted it right back to the Jets.
The second fumble taken away came with 4:20 left in the game, after the offense was finally able to find the end zone and take their first lead of the game, 12-10. Cleveland needs to close the game out at this point; if they’re able to get a couple of first downs or just eat up some clock and flip the field, it will be a win for the offense.
But what do the Browns do? They take just 21 seconds off the clock and are forced to punt; Corey Bojorquez then mishandles a high snap, and New York gets the ball at the Cleveland 23-yard line.
The weather was obviously a huge factor in this game, as we saw many fumbles by both teams, along with lots of dropped passes. In total, though, the Browns mustered up 198 yards: 102 passing and 96 rushing.
Watson threw for 155 yards, but was sacked eight times for a loss of 53 yard s, which is subtracted from the team’s total passing yards.
Watson was sacked six times over the past three wins, but him going down eight times today was a mix of bad protection and him trying to extend plays with his legs.

title: I’m Most Concerned About This One Thing With the Browns Through Five Weeks
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns still have work to do.
After beginning the 2026 NFL regular season with a strong 3-1 record, the Browns returned right back down to reality.
On Sunday, Oct. 11, the Browns fell to the New York Jets on the road from MetLife Stadium by a final score of 17-12. While they entered the game as underdogs, that public perception became apparent as the offense struggled to get anything going.
"It comes down to making the other team play their best. And I don’t think we did that today," head coach Todd Monken said postgame.
The weather conditions in New Jersey certainly played a role in making such issues obvious, but there is a major concern following the organization.
And unfortunately, it hasn't gone away week after week.
For the first time since becoming a member of the Cleveland Browns, starting quarterback Deshaun Watson looks like a mobile quarterback. He is routinely moving around in the pocket, scrambling to pick up extra yards and connecting with receivers downfield on the run.
He finished Sunday's loss to the Jets with 15 completions for 155 yards and one touchdown.
However, he was sacked a whopping eight times and wasn't able to convert on third down 12 total times. With Watson being consistently pressured by the Jets' defense, they made the Browns' offensive line look abysmal.
“It’s coaching. It’s playing, it’s getting the ball out of our hands. It’s protection," Monken said when asked about the high number of sacks. "It’s all the above … We all gotta take a big freaking bite of this.”
4th and long and deshaun watson is stopped for a 1 yard gain pic.twitter.com/COpZ6QGehE
Now, on the season, Watson has been sacked 19 times.
In the Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on the road, he was sacked five times, before the offensive line somewhat turned things around as they held the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers to just two sacks each.
Either way, with a less mobile quarterback, the Browns' line would likely be giving up even more sacks than the statistics show.
There are players who are obviously looking the part, most notably rookies Austin Barber and Spener Fano, elevating a position group that went through extensive changes in the offseason, but there are still plenty of improvements needed to be made.
And it isn't just Watson who is struggling due to the offensive line's inability to provide ample room to move.
The Browns' go-to rusher out of the backfield, Quinshon Judkins, has had an eye-poppingly slow start to the season.
He carried the ball 14 times on Sunday, rushing for just 44 yards, an average of 3.1 yards per carry. On the season, his total numbers see him with just 221 yards on 73 carries, with him finding the endzone just once. He is barely averaging north of 3.0 yards per carry.
If the Browns truly want to be a multi-dimensional offense, that ability to establish both the rushing and passing game comes from the line's protection.
“You’re going to put yourself in that position when you can't run the football," Monken continued when asked about the high sack count. "We weren't able to run the football today. We were behind the sticks the whole day and we made a few plays, some (to) get back on track and some third downs that gave us a chance...
"But we were never comfortable calling it or playing. And that's not a recipe for success.”
Monken: “You’re going to put yourself in that position when you can't run the football. We weren't able to run the football today. We were behind the sticks the whole day and we made a few plays, some (to) get back on track and some third downs that gave us a chance, but we were… https://t.co/drjFJxMPvG
Moving forward, it simply needs to be better. Not just for Watson, but for Judkins and the rest of the running back room, too.
The Browns return to the field on Sunday, Oct. 18, for a Week 6 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens at 1:00 p.m. EST.
And with hopes of maintaining the top spot in the AFC North, they'll have to make that one big change.

title: The Browns Have 3 Major Issues That Could Derail Their Season
full_text:
After the Cleveland Browns lost to the New York Jets 17-12 in week five, one thing is very clear about this team: They do not have what it takes to perform like a top team in the league.
The Browns need to clean up some aspects of their game and stop getting cute with the football.
Browns' Head Coach Todd Monken is in his first-ever season as an NFL Head Coach.
With some of the play calls and decisions the Browns made in a very winnable loss to the Jets , that lack of experience was very clear.
While the rain played a big factor in the matchup, mother nature is not the one with the headset on calling plays from the sideline.
It seemed as if everything Monken learned about play calling for Deshaun Watson through the first four weeks was thrown out of the window.
Rather than simple screens or quick passes, Monken tried to go for longer developing plays that ultimately failed miserably against New York's strong pass rush. In the game, Watson was sacked eight times.
Monken needs to realize he is no longer calling plays for Lamar Jackson, but Deshaun Watson.
At the end of the first quarter, KC Concepcion was ruled out with a concussion after a dirty hit from Jets' safety Minkah Fitzpatrick.
Without their first-round rookie, you would think Monken would focus the playcalling on trying to target the NFL's rookie receiving leader, Denzel Boston, or reliable tight end Harold Fannin Jr.
Instead, Boston and Fannin combined for only 11 targets throughout the entire game, while guys like Isaiah Bond and Jerry Jeudy split 14 targets.
As the head coach, you have to be able to recognize those guys who are able to make big plays and then find ways to get them the football.
Once again, Deshaun Watson is not a top-tier quarterback who will win games for you. While he may make some nice plays, offensive production heavily depends on the skill positions making plays themselves.
Carson Schwesinger forces a massive turnover, @Browns ball! @CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FQHcn2V9Tc
With four minutes left to go in the game, the Carson Schwesinger strip-sacked Geno Smith. With the ball in Jets territory and the lead, you would think the Browns would try to drain the clock or maybe the Jets' timeouts. Instead, they ran the ball out of bounds and had back-to-back incompletions.
In that time, they only took nine seconds off the clock before the muffed punt from Corey Bojorquez. Clearly, it was that sequence that cost them the game just after taking their first lead.
Other than this moment, the Browns had multiple chances to make plays in a game they should have won.
If they can go back home next week, clean it up, and keep it simple, they will be in a much better spot trying to face off with the Baltimore Ravens.
