title: Browns vs Jets Week 5 Injury Report: Cleveland Without 2 Key Pieces Defensively
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have started the 2026 NFL regular season 3-1.
And while it seems like nothing can slow this team down, the recent injury report casts such a sentiment in doubt.
On Sunday, Oct. 11, the Browns are slated to take on the New York Jets at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, N.J., for what should be a fairly competitive contest. The Browns and Jets aren't the league's most prominent teams, especially with how young and raw they are, but they both have boom-or-bust potential.
Ahead of the showdown, the inactive list was announced , with Browns defensive linemen Mike Hall Jr. and Mason Graham stealing the spotlight.
#Browns inactives v #Jets : QB Taylen Green (3QB) WR Tylan Wallace TE Carsen Ryan DT Mike Hall Jr. C Parker Brailsford G Teven Jenkins DT Mason Graham
Both have been standouts on the line for the Browns this season, combining for 19 tackles, seven for a loss, six quarterback hits and five sacks. While many of those numbers skew in Graham's direction, his injury in last week's Thursday Night Football showdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers pushed Hall Jr. into a bigger role.
Fortunately, he did not disappoint.
But now, with both players banged up and out for Sunday's game, the Browns will have to dive into its depth with hopes of replacing such productivity.
On the line, the Browns are expected to deploy Maliek Collins, Adin Huntington, Chris Williams and Sam Kamara. Both Williams and Kamara were activated from the practice squad earlier in the week to fill Graham and Hall's voids.
"It's next man up. I think that's really what it is," head coach Todd Monken said earlier in the week when asked about the Browns' injuries. "That's why you have practice squad players and the ability to elevate them. It's going to take everybody on the roster, and that's why you're consistently trying to develop those players.
"So, when they get their number called, the expectation, the position, you're trying not to let that drop."
Outside of the defensive line, the Browns also are working through injuries on the offensive side of the ball.
Linemen Teven Jenkins and Parker Brailsford are both inactive, with Brailsford's reason being unknown. Jenkins, on the other hand, has missed much of the 2026 season due to a back injury. In his place, the Browns have turned to rookie Austin Barber, who has been one of the league's top first-year players.
Wideout Tylan Wallace is going to miss yet another game due to a knee injury, while tight end Carson Ryan stays off the gridiron due to a calf injury. Ryan was limited all week.
Both are not necessarily impacting the offense's capabilities much, but still, being without a few depth pieces will put more strain on the starters.
Quarterback Taylen Green rounds out the Browns' inactive report, as he will serve as the team's emergency QB.

title: Browns Trading for This Wideout Would Be an Unmitigated Disaster on Multiple Levels
full_text:
Over the course of the offseason, one common trade target mentioned in connection with the Cleveland Browns was current Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr.
Fast forward to Week 5 of the NFL regular season, and that move makes zero sense for the Browns, for a number of reasons.
Here are the three main ones:
There’s no question Thomas is a talented wideout. His rookie season back in 2024 was actually pretty phenomenal, catching 87 balls for 1,282 yards and 10 scores, leading to a Pro Bowl nod and a fourth place in voting for the AP Offensive Rookie of the Year Award.
Then, something changed. Thomas just stopped being a critical part of the Jags offense, once Liam Coen was promoted from offensive coordinator to head coach last year. His numbers took a nosedive, with only 48 catches for 707 yards and two scores all last year, while former sixth rounder Parker Washington’s role grew exponentially.
This year, Thomas hasn’t found a way to reinsert himself back into prominence, and is currently not only standing behind Washington and Jakobi Meyers in receptions, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, but also has one less score than rookie sixth rounder Josh Cameron, who the team seems to really like. And that’s not even mentioning that tight end Brenton Strange has been more involved in the offense, as well.
Thomas’ snap count is also falling at an alarming rate. After starting out at an 80 percent of offensive plays as a rookie and 78 percent in his sophomore season, it currently stands at just 47 percent.
Drops have become a big issue for Thomas, and that’s something the Browns really don’t need, especially after Jerry Jeudy’s deeply disappointing 2025 season.
Second-rounder Denzel Boston is arguably the leading candidate for Offensive Rookie of the Year honors so far this season, and first-rounder KC Concepcion has been almost as good. Together, they’ve reenergized the Browns’ receiving to the point where Jeudy has become somewhat of an afterthought, sparking debate on whether he should actually be traded, too.
Cleveland looks set up nicely for the future with the trio of Boston, Concepcion and tight end Harold Fannin Jr., along with the expected development of Isaiah Bond. For a team that just a mere six months ago had no clue on who could be their WR1, they came away from the 2026 NFL Draft with two solid candidates.
Another prominent name from the 2024 NFL Draft, Marvin Harrison Jr., is currently being shopped around in Arizona according to multiple reports . Even if Harrison’s numbers as a pro are even more underwhelming than Thomas, there might be some logic in trading for him, as his ceiling is still considered much higher.
While Harrison has been generally viewed as a wideout capable of doing it all with a pretty complete array of tools, Thomas is now more or less considered just a deep threat receiver, who’s best trait is creating some space underneath for others to exploit.
However, don’t expect Cleveland to make some noise in the Harrison front, no matter how attractive it might be. For the right price, swapping Harrison for Jeudy on the Browns’ current roster looks enticing . In real life, Cleveland might be better served not getting into a bidding war with other clubs for Harrison’s services, no matter how much untapped potential there still might be lying around in there, somewhere.
The Browns have a good thing going on with their current core of young talent from the last two drafts, and giving up too much capital for Harrison or Thomas when you’re expected to need it down the road for a new quarterback doesn’t make sense.
If the Browns are going to be players before the trade deadline, they should be targeting the offensive backfield , defensive line or defensive backfield . Wide receiver is just not a position of need for this team anymore.

title: A Struggling Rushing Attack Means the Browns Should Make This Trade
full_text:
Through the first four weeks of the 2026 NFL regular season, the Cleveland Browns are 3-1.
Owning the top spot in the AFC North , and having downed the in-division Pittsburgh Steelers, all while starting quarterback Deshaun Watson seems to be finding his footing again, things are looking up for a team that won just eight combined games the last two seasons.
But even though the team is winning games, pushing themselves to that next level and legitimately contending in the playoffs is going to be tough.
However, if they can bolster this one position in particular, the Browns' chances of being a more dynamic offense are greatly improved.
Here is one big-time trade the Browns should make before the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline:
The Tennessee Titans are arguably one of the league's most intriguing sides because not only do they have a good chunk of talent, but that talent is young. While the pieces aren't aligning as well as many expected them to, the Titans still do have a bright future ahead.
In order to capitalize on the youth movement, though, as losses continue to end up on their record, the front office could be inclined to move on from some of the more established pieces on the 53-man to free up opportunities for youngsters.
And Pollard, who is approaching 30 years old, could be a piece the front office is willing to deal. He is also r umored to be on the trade block , yet not fully confirmed.
Tony Pollard is a likely trade candidate from the Titans after their 0-4 start. Pollard is on a $6.7 million expiring contract, which many contending teams can absorb. Tennessee will only be able to net a Day 3 2027 pick for their starting running back. pic.twitter.com/AaMBitIcvc
Currently, behind Pollard are running backs Tyjae Spears and Nicholas Singleton, both of whom are 25 years old or younger.
While Pollard is obviously performing well to begin the year, rushing for over 200 yards and one score , his dual-threat capabilities have been lost in Tennessee's offense. While obviously being a good rusher, Pollard's biggest impact can come in the passing game, where he thrived in Dallas.
He has nearly 1,800 receiving yards across his eight-year career.
The Browns could be willing to swap Dylan Sampson and a 2027 fifth-rounder, or just toss in a few picks, for Pollard, bringing an experienced back to Cleveland to be paired with Judkins.
Potential trade candidates to monitor, per @AdamSchefter : Marvin Harrison Jr. Jerry Jeudy Tony Pollard Khalil Mack Josh Sweat
In his rookie campaign, Sampson became heavily involved in the Browns' rushing attack late in the season due to an injury to Judkins. However, he never quite found a role that seemed sustainable long-term. Like Pollard, he was good in the passing game, but heading into 2026, injuries have kept him off the field.
Looking for a change of pace and a new face to bring some energy back to the running back room, landing Pollard could be exactly what the Browns need to take some weight off Judkins' workload. The 29-year-old has topped 1,000 yards in each of the last four campaigns, bringing consistency to an offense that is looking to build it.
The Browns have plenty of youth on the offense, and while that is a good thing, in the short term, pairing them with a veteran like Pollard could be a great fit.
Would you trade Jerry Jeudy to the Titans for Tony Pollard? Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay proposed the two teams swap players to help bolster areas of weakness on each roster. "No other Browns back outside of starter Quinshon Judkins has garnered more than six carries or eclipsed… pic.twitter.com/aXaVm1VTie
With a chance to see the rushing attack break out of its dry spell, the Browns return to the field on Sunday, Oct. 11, in a Week 5 showdown against the New York Jets.

title: 5 Storylines for Week 5 Against the New York Jets
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns head to New York rested and ready to improve their record to 4-1.
The Browns have had ten days off after their win on Thursday Night Football and fans are eager to watch them prove that they belong in first place. The Jets enter the contest at 1-3, but have played a couple of close games. The matchup will be rain-soaked, and there are plenty of storylines to keep an eye on.
Watson has had his good plays and his bad plays, en route to three straight game-winning drives. The offense is waiting for him to avoid the quarter-long stalls. Some of his quarters have been reminiscent of his Houston Texan days, and other quarters have reminded fans of what they have been watching since he has been a Brown.
The Jets are seventh in the league in passing defense, and Watson will have to limit his turnovers when the rain starts to come down. Watson being able to get first downs throughout the game will be telling in how the offense can look moving forward.
Judkins has had better production in the past two games than the first two. However, it is still not good enough to keep up with the winning ways. The offense has to be able to move the ball on the ground, which may be especially important in tomorrow’s inclement weather. The Jets are in the bottom 10 in rushing defense and the Browns have to take advantage.
Todd Monken has had an extended week to plan and practice a running attack for Sunday. This could be the week Judkins revs up and gets close to 100 yards.
Denzel Ward and Garrett Wilson will face off against one another in New York. The defense has played a lot more man coverage, and Ward will try to shut down his fellow Buckeye when lined up on the right side of the ball. This matchup is more than just a fun storyline, but it could determine the game.
Geno Smith is first in the NFL in completion percentage thanks to the help of Wilson. Smith has a 77% completion percentage when targeting him. Ward has been one of the best man-coverage cornerbacks in the league, and if he can shut down the Smith-to-Wilson connection, then the Browns have a great chance of leaving the Big Apple with a win.
The defensive line will be without two of its best interior linemen , Mason Graham and Michael Hall Jr. The defensive line was thin in the preseason, and the Browns signed a couple of ends late in training camp. Last week it did not seem to matter who was in the rotation, as they consistently got in the backfield. They will have to disrupt Smith quickly to get him off rhythm and stagnate the offense.
The Jets will be missing star running back Breece Hall and the defensive line cannot let the backups get open holes to control the ground game on a wet afternoon.
Special Teams Coordinator Byron Storer has drastically turned the unit around in one offseason . They have covered kicks well and the return game has been productive. Last season, the Browns lost to the Jets by giving up both a kick and punt return for a touchdown. This will be a great measuring stick of how improved the unit is from last season.
This game is sandwiched in between two divisional games, but these storylines against the Jets are just as important.

title: 3 Biggest Injury Concerns For Browns Heading Into Sunday's Matchup vs. Jets
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are looking for their fourth straight win as they head to MetLife Stadium to take on the New York Jets on Sunday, but a few injury concerns remain.
Cleveland lost two of its defensive tackles in the Browns' Week 4 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mason Graham left in the first half and did not return, while Mike Hall also got injured but returned. However, Hall didn't practice all week, raising three injury concerns that could hurt the Browns this weekend.
Graham will not play against the Jets due to an MCL and ankle sprain. The second-year defensive tackle has had a strong start to the season, recording four sacks in his first three games, and the Browns will miss him up the middle.
While the Browns managed to win over the Steelers without Graham for the final three quarters, the Jets now have a week to prepare for his absence, which could hurt the Browns.
Hall left the field on a cart during the Browns' Week 4 game, but he returned and recorded a huge sack on Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers late in the third quarter, pushing Pittsburgh out of field goal range and forcing a punt.
Hall's injury didn't seem serious since he returned to play, but he's had almost eight days to recover and still hasn't practiced as of Friday. The Browns have already ruled him out for Week 5.
With Hall and Graham both out, defensive tackle like Adin Huntington will need to step up and take on a larger role than usual.
Sticking with the defensive tackles, the Browns will not have Davis available, as he hasn't played for them this season. The Browns signed Davis to a one-year, $2 million deal this offseason after he spent three years with the 49ers. However, the Browns placed him on injured reserve at the start of the regular season after he suffered a quad injury.
After four games on IR, Davis is eligible to return, and the Browns designated him to return on Tuesday, opening his 21-day practice window. But Cleveland did not add him to the 53-man roster, so he will still miss Sunday.
It seemed like Davis might be able to play, and now the Browns will be without three defensive tackles they expected to play significant roles this season.

title: Pros and Cons of Moving Any of Browns Quarterbacks in 2026
full_text:
At the current moment, the Cleveland Browns have four quarterbacks on the roster.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching in just over a month, it is likely one of them will be moved.
But who does Cleveland get rid of? Here are the pros and cons of moving each quarterback.
While many fans would be happy Deshaun Watson is off the team, the Browns would need a big offer to move their QB1 after his hot start to the season.
Outside of a happier fanbase, moving Watson would probably mean going all in on a quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft.
As for the cons, winning and offensive production would likely take a hit at first until the next man up is able to get comfortable in Todd Monken's scheme.
Overall, a Deshaun Watson midseason move is very unlikely.
A potential Shedeur Sanders trade was rumored after New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury.
Since then, those rumors have been shut down, and New York has found their new guy in J.J. McCarthy.
Browns aren't looking to trade Shedeur Sanders, per @RuiterWrongFAN . pic.twitter.com/UB35kUR2Hj
But let's talk about the pros and cons of moving Shedeur.
The only pro of moving Sanders is the potential for a good trade package in return. If Cleveland could get a higher draft pick, it might be worth it. But do draft picks outweigh the numerous cons?
Not only would the fanbase hate Sanders' departure, but the Browns would also mortgage a potential future QB option. Many people aren't realizing that the time currently being spent by Sanders as QB is great time for the raw talent to sit, watch, learn, and develop.
With the way the season has started, it looks like Coach Monken will be at the helm in Cleveland for multiple years. Additionally, with Deshaun Watson being 31 years old and in the final year of his contract, it is crucial that the Browns have a young backup developing now to take over in the near future.
If there's a quarterback that sticks out among the four, it's Dillon Gabriel .
Pros to moving Gabriel would be sending him to a place where he wants to be. Off the field, it has been pretty clearly seen through the media that Gabriel isn't very happy in Cleveland. To be fair, if you had to move to Cleveland from Hawaii during the winter season, you might not be the happiest either.
On the field, Gabriel performed very well in the final preseason game this year against the Patriots. In the first half, he threw for three touchdowns. Basing a trade on recency bias from that game, compared to his poor regular-season action last season, could haul in a better trade package for the Browns.
On the other hand, there are not many cons at all when it comes to moving the former Heisman candidate. The only thing that looks bad on paper is the fact that Cleveland used a third-round pick on Gabriel, just to get rid of him the following year.
Taylen Green is at the bottom because the Browns simply won't move him.
This is because any move to be made would have to be cutting the 2026 sixth-round pick.
Coach Monken has also talked about potentially using Green in specialized sets this season. Clearly, the former Arkansas Razorback is staying with the Browns.

title: Todd Monken Deserves More Credit For Launching Deshaun Watson Career Comeback
full_text:
After the conclusion of Week 1, many called for Deshaun Watson to be removed as the starting quarterback of the Cleveland Browns.
Fast-forward three weeks, and the Browns, still led by Watson, have won three consecutive games with fourth-quarter comebacks involved in each. And while the season opener was incredibly disappointing, it can be forgotten, with the Browns now 3-1 and atop the AFC North standings.
"I think in Todd Monken's mind, there's no week to week, month to month, that whole narrative has dissolved the way Monken wanted it to," - @TonyGrossi on Deshaun Watson's job security as QB1. pic.twitter.com/zMfvcafzkb
While Watson deserves an awful lot of credit, especially considering he now has 855 yards, a near-70% completion rate and six scores through the air, head coach Todd Monken deserves just as much praise and recognition for helping put him in position to succeed.
Watson is beginning to look like the quarterback Cleveland traded for back in 2022.
Watson's time in Cleveland hasn't had the greatest storyline surrounding it. He has been suspended, injured, ridiculed by the media and downright hated by the fanbase at times. Questions were asked heading into the 2026 season about whether or not the three-time Pro Bowler could ever be accepted as the starter.
But after working all offseason to beat out second-year signal caller Shedeur Sanders , he got his opportunity to do just that.
It hasn't always been pretty, but Monken has worked closely with Watson to make sure he can routinely improve and continue to stay under center week after week.
Cleveland columnist Terry Pluto echoed such a sentiment recently, adding that the two worked behind the scenes through tough video sessions to ensure Watson would make changes after the Week 1 disaster class.
"After the 34-10 loss to Jacksonville, Monken publicly stood strong with Watson," he wrote on Cleveland.com. "But the week before the game at Tampa, there were some very tough video sessions. I was told it was perhaps some of the 'hardest coaching' he’s had since coming to the Browns."
. @terrypluto credits Deshaun Watson's recent turnaround this season to Todd Monken's "tough love" in film review: "After the 34-10 loss to Jacksonville, Monken publicly stood strong with Watson. But the week before the game at Tampa, there were some very tough video sessions. I… pic.twitter.com/C4c7OWV66F
Obviously, such extra attention has worked wonders.
Since throwing for a measly 205 yards, one touchdown and one interception against the Jaguars, Watson has 650 yards, five touchdowns and one interception across the last three games. He has also brought his QBR up to a mark of 58.4, which is 18th in the NFL.
His best outing, a Week 2 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he passed for nearly 250 yards and two scores , resulted in high praise from Monken.
"I'm happy for Deshaun," Monken said following the Week 2 win. "I expected improvement and I expect continued improvement. There's a lot of football left in him. He just hasn't played in a while."
Terry Pluto of https://t.co/l4Q3F0Sn4e reveals the turning point behind Deshaun Watson's resurgence, as Todd Monken's tough coaching helped speed up the Browns quarterback's decision-making. "After the 34-10 loss to Jacksonville, Monken publicly stood strong with Watson. But the… pic.twitter.com/JbQJrqIEAA
At the time, that somewhat washed over, especially with plenty of other storylines occurring to take the spotlight. Now, though, those words seemed to reflect an important distinction that Monken recognizes: Watson isn't a quarterback who has lost his ability, but rather one who needed time to regain his rhythm and confidence.
Heading into a Week 5 matchup with the New York Jets on the road from MetLife Stadium, a lot of national eyes will be on the Browns.
The big question is: Has this three-game winning streak been a fluke, or is there legitimately something to be excited about in The Land?
And for Watson, he will look to continue silencing the doubts that surround his future in the league. Fortunately, he has Monken and the rest of the team on his side, with the hope that he can continue to lead the team to a fourth straight victory.

title: Ideal Cowboys 2027 Mock Draft Lands Prototypical DaRon Bland Replacement
full_text:
As the Dallas Cowboys aim to bounce back from last week's embarrassing effort at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , one thing remains clear: the defense is still in shambles despite all of the offseason efforts to improve the roster.
To be fair, the team has yet to field a healthy defense, and the secondary has been plagued by injuries, but former All-Pro cornerback DaRon Bland has been on the field and has been one of the team's biggest liabilities every week .
As the team searches for answers, there have been calls for the team to move on from Bland, who has been a perennial underperformer the past few years. That's why a new 2027 NFL mock draft from Pro Football Network will have everyone looking toward a brighter future.
In the latest mock, Dallas lands Clemson Tigers star cornerback Ashton Hampton , who is a "prototypical" cornerback who blends a perfect combination of size and ball skills.
The 2027 NFL Draft will be held from Thursday, April 29, through Saturday, May 1, at the National Mall outside of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C.
Let's take a closer look at what a player like Hampton could bring to the ailing Cowboys secondary.
Bland just hasn't been cutting it for the Cowboys since his blockbuster extension, and Cowboys Nation is desperate for the team to move on. Parting ways with Bland in favor of an exciting player like Hampton would be the kind of move to restore faith in the fan base.
"Bland has dealt with injuries and regression in play since his All-Pro campaign in 2023. Cobie Durant gives the Dallas Cowboys a new face in the secondary, but the cornerback room still has major question marks otherwise. The Cowboys had a lot of needs on defense, so you can’t fix them all in one year, but cornerback has remained a major weakness in 2026 ," Pro Football Network wrote.
"After a strong 2025 season, Ashton Hampton has arguably looked even better to begin 2026. He’s 6’-foot-2 and 200 pounds, using his prototypical build to jam receivers near the line of scrimmage and compete at the catch point. He’s a reliable form tackler who can hit hard as a downhill defender, and his mental trigger shows up well covering underneath."
A 6-foot-2 cornerback who can cover and play press coverage? One who excels physically and is not afraid to get dirty by helping against the run? You couldn't ask for a better player to plug into Christian Parker's scheme.
Last season, Hampton recorded 45 tackles, 9 passes defensed, three tackles for a loss, one sack, and one interception as a sophomore. This season, he has 15 tackles, an FBS-high 9 pass breakouts, one interception, and 0.5 tackles per loss in just five games.
His ability to make plays on the ball is only getting better, and he'd be a welcomed addition to the Dallas secondary. In the middle of Round 1, Hampton would be an incredible value pick.
Cowboys Nation can catch Hampton back in action on Saturday, October 17, at home against Charleston Southern. Kickoff is set for 12:00 p.m. ET on the ACC Network.

title: Cowboys & Jets Deemed Logical Trade Partners With Dallas' Need at Edge Rusher
full_text:
The more things change, the more they stay the same and the Dallas Cowboys are seeing that first hand.
After the total revamp of the defense this offseason, which included hiring a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker and making several changes to personnel, the Cowboys are no better off than they were last season.
One of the issues in Dallas is the inability to get sacks . Dallas is getting some pressure, but nobody seems to know how to finish, and that is routinely exposing an inadequate secondary.
As a result, edge rusher is going to be a major priority as we inch closer to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
With their need at edge rusher, the Cowboys are matched up as a possible fit for New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald, who was dubbed a possible trade candidate by Pro Football Focus' Bradley Locker .
"Possible Fits: Bears, 49ers, Eagles, Cowboys," Locker wrote.
"The Jets seemed to make future investments in the edge rusher position with David Bailey and Joseph Ossai this offseason, while Kingsley Enagbare has also played more than McDonald," Locker added. "The 27-year-old on a one-year deal should draw eyes for teams looking to better pursue the quarterback."
McDonald was the subject of trade rumors last year, and this year, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler believes he could draw interest on the trade market.
McDonald still has one year left on his rookie contract after 2026, so it's conceivable the Jets will be open to parting ways with him, especially with the recent investments they've made at the position that Locker pointed to.
McDonald has posted two sacks and 12 pressures through five games, according to PFF. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, those marks would rank first and third on the team.
McDonald has shown he's capable of impact sack production in the past few years, as he tallied 18.5 sacks combined in 2024 and 2025, with 10.5 of those coming in 2024.
We would prefer the Cowboys swing for the fences for an elite edge rusher, but we also know those guys don't grow on trees because teams are rarely willing to part with them.
McDonald would be the next-best thing for Dallas, assuming he can reproduce what he has put on tape the last two seasons.
Trade compensation will be based on what McDonald does between now and the trade deadline, but the Cowboys will probably be looking at a third- or fourth-round pick.
That isn't too bad when you consider McDonald still has one more year left on his contract. The Cowboys do not have their third-rounder in 2027, but they do have a fourth-round pick. Dallas sports both of those selections in 2028, though.
If things keep going the way they're going and McDonald is out there as the best option for Dallas on the trade market, we could definitely see Jerry Jones swinging a trade.

title: Updated NFC East Standings: Wild NFL Sunday Benefits Cowboys After Week 5
full_text:
Week 5 started brutally for the Dallas Cowboys as they lost embarrassingly to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football. That dropped them to 2-3 on the season, and considering how poorly they performed on both sides of the ball, that loss was especially deflating.
Hope felt lost, but that changed a bit on Sunday. The Cowboys didn't play during the weekend , but things really went their way, as every other team in the NFC East had a game to forget.
With that in mind, let's take a look at the updated divisional standings as Dallas prepares to face the Green Bay Packers in Week 6.
Wow, what were the Washington Commanders thinking at the end of their game against the New York Giants?
Treylon Burks made a big play in overtime, moving the ball to the New York 39. That put the Commanders in field goal range, with 1:02 left on the clock. They then moved it two more yards on a run by Rachaad White, but took their foot off the gas with 55 seconds left.
Despite having no timeouts, Washington took its time snapping the ball. Once they did, Jayden Daniels ran around for far too long before going down. Once he did, there wasn't enough time to snap the ball , and the game ended in a tie. Now 1-3-1, the Commanders are all alone in last place.
It's hard to get over the loss to the Bucs, but the Cowboys are still alive in their division. The question is whether they can take advantage. They take on the Packers in Week 6, a team that just shocked the Chicago Bears. After that, they have a late-October meeting with the struggling Eagles. Hope has been fading, but they can turn things around in a hurry.
Right now, the Philadelphia Eagles have the tiebreaker over the Cowboys because they are 1-0 in the NFC East, compared to 1-1 for Dallas. They should be 3-2, however, after taking a lead against the Jacksonville Jaguars with eight seconds to play.
As was the case for the Cowboys against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 3 , that was one second too long. Ameer Abdullah returned the final kickoff 53 yards to the Philadelphia 39. That allowed Cam Little to drill a 57-yard field goal, handing the Eagles a shocking 19-17 loss. That's three losses in a row for the Eagles and their only wins are against the 1-3-1 Commanders and 0-5 Tennessee Titans. There's not much to be excited about when it comes to their work this season.
Washington let the clock run out on them, but the Giants did their best to lose this game as well. At the end of overtime, they had a missed field goal attempt from Dominic Zvada, his third of the game. They got the ball back, and were in field goal range again, but Cam Skattebo fumbled the ball away. They should have won after a 14-point comeback in the final quarter, but yet somehow walked out with a tie.

title: Cowboys Week 5 Stock Report: Malachi Lawrence Leads 3 Rising, DaRon Bland Among 5 Falling
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys had one of the uglier losses in recent memory on Thursday when they fell to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 24-16.
It was a terrible performance all around , as the Cowboys couldn't get much going on offense and the defense was its usual putrid self.
Despite the struggles, we did find three players who managed to improve their respective stocks going into Week 6. Meanwhile, we are highlighting five guys who hurt their stocks the most, although we could have named a lot more.
Now, our Week 5 stock report.
Speed has quietly put together three solid games in a row for the Cowboys. While he has only been targeted twice in that span, his coverage has been sticky, so no wonder teams aren't trying him.
The Cowboys may have found an unsung hero at CB in someone NOBODY saw coming: Ameer Speed. Over the last 3 weeks, he’s played 34 coverage snaps and been targeted just twice, allowing 1 catch for 8 yards. The numbers are impressive, but the film is even better. Speed looks… pic.twitter.com/pRJ3ezIFcm
Speed saw one target in Week 5 but didn't allow a completion.
If Cobie Durant is needed in the slot upon his return, the Cowboys should give Speed snaps over DaRon Bland.
Ferguson has proven unreliable this season, and in more ways than one.
In Week 3, he had the crucial fumble, and in Week 5 it was the brutal drop on a pass that went through his hands, off his face mask and into the arms of a Bucs defender. That play sealed Dallas' loss on its final offensive drive.
Adding to those issues, Ferguson has also struggled badly with blocking, which has only made his season look even worse. The Cowboys tight end needs to get his act together, and fast.
Pickens finally broke out on Sunday, with the veteran wideout reeling in season-highs in catches (nine), receiving yards (130) and touchdowns (one). It was only a matter of time before he exploded, and here we are.
Keep an eye on the status of CeeDee Lamb going into Week 6, as he's dealing with a quad bruise . That's not expected to keep him out, but if it does, Pickens could be in line for another big game.
When isn't Bland's stock falling? In fact, we're not sure it can even go lower than it is now.
Another abysmal performance was headlined by Bland falling on two separate plays, both of which led to crucial receptions. Then, there was his brutal drop on a potential pick-six that the old Bland would have caught and housed.
It doesn't appear the Cowboys are going to make a change with the veteran corner yet, but they desperately need to.
The rookie did something nobody else could in Week 5: finish off a pressure with a sack. Adding to that, Lawrence had two pressures in total to go along with a run stop.
The sack was the first of Lawrence's career and he's now tied for the team lead with one. It was a step in the right direction during a season in which the rookie has been mostly quiet.
Willams has been inconsistent, at best, this season and had a bad game in Week 5 after playing better in Week 4.
The biggest issue we saw with Williams was his failure to get off blocks, which assisted in the Buccaneers running wild on Dallas. Williams did have a few pressures, but he didn't turn either of them into even a QB hit, let alone a sack.
Williams' performance on Thursday did nothing to quell the idea he just isn't a good fit in the system Christian Parker is running.
Like Williams, Miller was a big culprit in the Cowboys' run defense struggles in Week 5. The Bucs kept running it at the veteran edge rusher, and he kept failing to set the edge. It's amazing the damage Miller did in just 10 snaps.
Miller posted one pressure, but of course he didn't convert it into a sack, and he has yet to take down the quarterback through five games. The Von Miller experiment is not working in Dallas.
Beating a dead horse here at this point, but this coaching staff just continues to frustrate us.
Head coach Brian Schottenheimer even admitted his play-calling wasn't good enough in the first half of Week 5, and we'd say that was the case the entire game and, really, the entire season.
As for Parker, he continues to have no answers for how the Cowboys can fix their deficiencies on defense and our faith in him is nil.
This is just a poorly-coached team, plain and simple, and we're not sure that's ever going to change with this current staff.

title: Cowboys Trolled By Bucs Rookie Who Grew Up Hating Team After Week 5 Loss
full_text:
Losing is tough on its own, but for the Dallas Cowboys, the sting typically goes well beyond game day. As the most visible franchise in the NFL, Dallas is a constant talking point, and there's no shortage of opinions when they lose.
They're trolled by media personalities , such as Stephen A. Smith, and picked apart by others, such as Colin Cowherd . That's been the case this week after suffering a surprising defeat at the hands of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football .
As if that wasn't enough to deal with, opposing players are also piling on. Following their upset over the Cowboys, rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter shared photos as well as a clip of himself tackling running back Javonte Williams. The post was tagged as Cowgirl Stadium, and captioned "How bout dem Cowboys."
Trotter, a second-round pick out of Missouri, had seven tackles with one tackle for loss during the Bucs' 24-16 win over the heavily-favored Cowboys. It was the first victory of the year for Tampa Bay, who got the job done despite being without star quarterback Baker Mayfield.
Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels got the start in his place, and looked like a seasoned veteran against the suspect Dallas defense. Tampa Bay's defense, on the other hand, shut down the explosive Dallas offense, holding them to their lowest point total of the season.
If the name Trotter sounds familiar to Dallas fans, there's a reason for that. The rookie linebacker is the son of former Pro Bowl linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Sr., who spent eight years with the Philadelphia Eagles through three separate stings (1998-2001, 2004-2006, 2009) and two with Washington. The elder Trotter was also with the Tampa Bay Bucs for one season in 2007.
Trotter made the Pro Bowl four times during his 11-year career, finishing with 914 tackles 12.5 sacks, 69 tackles for loss, and nine interceptions.
His father's ties to the Eagles are more than enough reason for Trotter to poke fun at Dallas, but he has another reason as well. His older brother, Jeremiah Trotter Jr., is in his third season with the Eagles. Trotter Jr. was a fifth-round pick out of Clemson and has developed into a valuable role player in the Philly defense.

title: Dallas Cowboys Week 5 Rooting Guide For Frustrated Fan Base
full_text:
The NFL season is a marathon, not a sprint. Dallas Cowboys fans know that as well as anyone as they spent much of the 2025 campaign running calculus to see if their team had a chance at making the playoffs.
This season could be the same as they recently fell to 2-3 with a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . There's no shortage of reasons to be discouraged following the loss, but the Cowboys have plenty of time to turn things around .

If Dallas continues to lose, their draft pick could become a premium selection. The only way that doesn't sting too much is if the Packers have a solid pick as well, which happens if they keep losing.

title: NFL Fines Two Cowboys For Week 4 Infractions, With One Deemed 'Major Foul'
full_text:
A pair of Dallas Cowboys are receiving fines for Week 4 infractions, the league revealed on Saturday.
According to the NFL, Cowboys cornerback Reddy Steward has been hit with a $5,583 fine for unnecessary roughness (hit on a defenseless player) during the Week 4 win over the Houston Texans.
In addition to Steward, wide receiver and kick returner KaVontae Turpin was also hit in the wallet with a fine worth $11,941 for unsportsmanlike conduct (taunting) last week.
Steward's infraction came in the third quarter at 10:57, when the Texans scored on a touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud to Nico Collins. Steward was flagged on for the hit.
Turpin's infraction came in the third quarter on the very next play when he ripped off a 32-yard kick return. Turpin was not flagged for taunting during the game, though.
Steward was one of 10 players to be fined for "major" fouls this week, and that amounts to a season-high for the league, according to The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .
Assuming both players don't successfully appeal, their fines will be donated to the Professional Athletes Foundation that supports former players, and the NFL foundation that offers aid for the health, safety and wellness of athletes across all levels of organized football, including youth football.
A total of seven Cowboys players have been cited for fines this season when we include Steward's and Turpin's. However, not every Cowboy has had to pay up.
Tight end Jake Ferguson successfully appealed his fine for what the league deemed was an illegal celebration and vulgar act in Week 2.
The NFL believed Ferguson imitated shotgunning a beer in the Week 2 win over the Washington Commanders, but the appeals officers rescinded the fine after Ferguson made the case that the celebration "was his Gatorade celebtration that he previously had done on multiple occasions in practice, as the team documented on social media," according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .
With the successful appeal, Ferguson avoided a fine worth $13,611.
Ferguson wasn't the only one to have a fine rescinded for what the league thought was a player simulating shotgunning a beer, as San Francisco 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk and Indianapolis Colts guard Matt Goncalves had the same result after their fines.
The NFL and NFLPA have since agreed that drinking celebrations are acceptable , so we won't be seeing players get docked for doing them from here on out.
The consensus was the fines for those celebrations were silly to begin with, as the NFL's major sponsor is Bud Light. Finally, the league has seen the error in its ways.

title: Despite Secondary Struggles, Cowboys May Have Found Hidden Gem From UFL
full_text:
One thing the Dallas Cowboys have done well is find talent from the spring leagues . They were able to land kicker Brandon Aubrey following his stint with the USFL, which is the same league where they discovered their kik returner, KaVontae Turpin.
This year, they have another spring league product making a name for himself, even though he's being somewhat overlooked. Cornerback Ameer Speed was originally a sixth-round pick for the New England Patriots in 2023. The former Michigan State Spartan bounced around the league, playing for the Indianapolis Colts, Chicago Bears, and Houston Texans.
In April, he signed with the Houston Gamblers of the UFL and caught the attention of the Dallas coaching staff. Speed made the initial 53-man roster and has appeared in all five games. His numbers are modest, just seven tackles on the year, but he's been getting more snaps over the past two weeks.
Speed had 23 snaps in the win over the Texans and 45 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. According to PFF, he was in coverage 31 times over those two games and was targeted just twice . He surrendered only one reception for eight yards. Against Tampa Bay, he was able to play blanket coverage , allowing no receptions, which is something the rest of the secondary can't claim.
When looking at Speed, the first thing that stands out is his size. Listed at 6-foot-3 and 215 pounds, Speed is built like a wide receiver and has no issues going toe-to-toe with the biggest players on the opposing team.
He also uses that size in run defense, earning a 74.8 in run defense through the first five games of the year.
The Cowboys have made comments about changes coming following their latest defeat. They already made a trade for Joey Porter Jr., which gives them a legitimate CB1. He missed the game against Tampa Bay due to an illness, but hopefully will be back in Week 6 against the Green Bay Packers.
Given the struggles of players such as DaRon Bland and Shavon Revel Jr, who were both graded in the bottom five by PFF against the Bucs, Speed should see the field more. Unfortunately, Jerry Jones refuses to admit that they made an error in signing Bland to an extension, so Speed will likely remain on the bench, despite outperforming others ahead of him on the depth chart.

title: Broncos Player Grades: Bo Nix's Slump Continues in Ugly Chargers Win
full_text:
The Denver Broncos decided to make a big change on offense, with Sean Payton taking the play-calling duties back from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb ahead of Week 5's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
That was an indication that Payton felt the play-calling, and not the execution, was the biggest issue, though his feelings may have changed after the Broncos turned in their worst offensive showing of the season against the Chargers, when you factor in the quality of defense they are playing.
Denver won 23-17 , but it was ugly at times.
The Broncos scored four times off the takeaways their defense generated, including a turnover on downs, which is a credit to Vance Joseph's unit. The Broncos' defense put together a solid game, though they weren't without their faults, putting the win on their shoulders to move to 3-2 on the season.
This week's player grades reflect Denver's horrendous offensive showing and strong defensive display, minus a few miscues. Let’s get into the grades.
Tillman earned Defensive MVP after having the biggest impact on his snaps. He picked up three pressures on only 10 pass-rush snaps, and leading the team.
Several other Broncos tied with two pressures, all with nearly twice as many pass-rush snaps as Tillman. His run defense was stout as well, which helped him earn Defensive MVP in this one.
The Broncos' offensive line has had issues, but not Meinerz. Even against the Chargers, the offensive line struggled in both phases , but not the All-Pro right guard. A guard can only do so much to carry an offense, but that doesn't stop Meinerz from trying every week.
Sean Payton’s post-game comments were telling . Something is wrong with Nix mentally. Somehow, someway, he needs to get out of his own head; otherwise, it could be a long season.
This is Year 3, but Nix isn't playing like a quarterback with 39 regular-season starts under his belt. He looks like he's massively regressed.
D.J. Jones | DL | Grade: 79.4
This was one of the better games from Jones in his Broncos career, and it highlights when and how he can be a great run defender. The Broncos' run defense had issues, but not because of Jones in the middle, where he was stout and closed multiple running lanes.
Brandon Jones | S | Grade: 77.2
This was a 2024-level performance by Jones, back when he looked like an elite safety. Alas, this was his first game like that since 2024. He flew around the field, both in coverage and against the run, without getting caught out of position.
Garett Bolles | LT | Grade: 70.1
Bolles has been solid to good all season long, and against the Chargers, he put on an outstanding showing. Yes, the Chargers are beat up defensively, but Bolles looked great and held the fort down, minus one holding penalty.
Mike McGlinchey | RT | Grade: 67.9
McGlinchey was my matchup to watch against the Chargers' pass rush , and he answered the call. He stepped up and put on a good game for the first time this season. With no pressures allowed and a good run-blocking game, McGlinchey showed his value; now he just has to sustain that level of play.
RJ Harvey | RB | Grade: 31.7
If the Broncos want Harvey to improve, he has to do so as a pass protector first and foremost. The run game is lacking with him, too, but he can be a passing weapon. But if his pass protection doesn’t improve and it's as bad as it was against the Chargers, he will become too much of a tell for opposing defenses, if he isn’t already.
Devon Key | S | Grade: 34.8
When you play a position that isn’t rotated and have to come in for an injury, it can be difficult to come in and play well. Key has done that before, but this time, stepping in for an injured Talanoa Hufanga, he didn’t play well. Hopefully, Key can be ready for Thursday Night Football if Hufanga misses time.
J.K. Dobbins | RB | Grade: 37.6
It looks like the injuries have finally caught up with Dobbins. Even with a few solid runs, he averaged just 3.8 yards per carry and spent most of the game under a 3.0 average. He doesn’t look bursty or explosive, and that's been paired with some terrible vision of late.
Jonah Elliss | OLB | Grade: 39.7
Elliss is a technical player, but he isn’t overly explosive or athletic for an edge rusher. Denver should look to play Que Robinson over Elliss, and after this season, consider moving Elliss to an inside linebacker and defensive play-caller role, as his brothers do with their respective NFL teams.

title: Sean Payton Had One Strong Message for Bo Nix After Broncos Beat Chargers
full_text:
Sean Payton's return to calling the plays didn't result in an offensive revival , but the Denver Broncos did beat the Los Angeles Chargers on the road, 23-17. It was Payton's first-ever win at SoFi Stadium as Broncos head coach.
“It was good enough to win, but there are still a number of things that we need to improve on," Payton said of his offense post-game.
It was barely good enough to win. Denver finished with 224 total yards but converted just 1-of-12 third-down attempts while going 2-of-5 in the red zone. Payton's return wasn't the quick fix to the biggest issue holding back the Broncos' offense: Bo Nix's Year-3 slump .
Despite having Payton in his ear and calling the plays, Nix still looked skittish and unsure in the pocket. With the exception of one 36-yard strike to tight end Evan Engram in the first quarter, Nix didn't push the ball downfield.
Nix seems like he doesn't trust his eyes. Everyone's got a theory on why the young quarterback suddenly looks so uncomfortable and unpoised, but it seems to be a between-the-ears issue.
Payton and his staff are trying to get to the bottom of it, but the veteran head coach had one parting message for Nix at the post-game podium: "Let it rip."
"I think, man, we as coaches, like I've said to him, I said, 'Man, you're the guy we wanted here. Let's go. You've done a ton of things well,'" Payton said of Nix. "But I think there's a lot that goes into that. It's important that, you know, in that old TV series The Bear , where they just said, 'Let her rip,' I want him to make sure that, hey, let her rip."
Payton isn't telling Nix to go be a fast-and-loose gunslinger. In fact, Nix believes his coach meant that he should trust his eyes.
“I think when a coach says ‘let it rip,’ it means trust what you see," Nix said post-game. "Right now, there’s just a little subtle piece of overall offensive execution that we’re still working towards, because at times, it’s there and we’re really good. At times, for whatever reason, the drive stalls."
Nix believes that a quarterback has to earn the right to "let it rip." It would seem that, by Payton calling on Bo to fire away, the Broncos' head coach believes he has earned the right — and, by extension, can be trusted to make the right decisions.
"I think there’s a lot of pieces that go into it, but... letting it rip is one of the best things that you can do as a quarterback," Nix said. "At the same time, you’ve got to sort of earn that right. When you do the preparation, you earn the right to react so that you can let it rip.”
Perhaps in his hesitancy as a passer, Nix is questioning himself and whether he's earned the right to "let it rip." Based on what we saw at SoFi Stadium, he's yet to fully embrace the let-it-rip mindset.
He went 16-of-27 for 123 yards and a touchdown. While Nix didn't throw an interception, he did fumble twice, losing one of them. That lost fumble came with the game tied and sparked an enormous momentum swing in the Chargers' direction.
The sudden change allowed L.A. to score immediately on the ensuing play with a Kimani Vidal 42-yard touchdown romp. The Chargers took a 17-10 lead at the bottom of the third quarter.
Thanks to some excellent clutch-time play by the Broncos' defense, Nix was given some additional opportunities in the fourth quarter, and while there were still some painful moments, the Broncos capitalized by punctuating their rather ugly offensive performance with 13 additional points.
Still, Broncos fans have gone from various stages of concern to — in some cases — outright panic over Nix's slump. That was clear enough from the comments on my X posts and the Mile High Huddle Podcast 's live chat after the game.
Although there's the distinct possibility that we could simply be seeing the ups and downs of a young quarterback still finding his way, it's hard to argue against the assertion that Nix has regressed. Myself, I wonder if Nix is truly over his broken ankle; the bone may be healed, but has his psyche caught up?
It sounds like Payton and his staff are trying to focus on the little things to get Nix rollling again in the bigger picture, starting with his feet.
"I would say this. I think the one area, obviously there's a lot been said about his feet. I think he's settling that down," Payton said of Nix. "I think it's important from a protection standpoint that early in games we provide that clean pocket so that clock doesn't get juiced up a little bit. I don't know what his dropback percentage was, but I think it was a little less tonight."
With Payton at the helm, the Broncos were more balanced offensively from a run-pass perspective, though it didn't lead to any big plays or obvious successes. Denver finished with 29 runs to 28 passes.
Nix's 27 attempts were a season-low, a reflection of Payton's drive to build a run game around his young quarterback, even if the returns on the ground weren't big. Fortunately, as is his way, Nix saved his best for when the chips were down, as the Broncos scored 13 fourth-quarter points on the back of three huge defensive stops.
When I say "his best," though, it's in relative terms. This was far from Nix's Week 3 fourth-quarter display.
"I think when we needed it down the stretch, there were some plays to be had. We got blitzed on [Courtland] Sutton's touchdown," Payton said. "We were hoping to get a certain coverage, but it was good because he's got a free rusher there."
We know one of the reasons Payton took back the play-calling was that he wasn't seeing a " championship " offense. Rome wasn't built in a day, but if Nix and the Broncos' offense took any steps forward in Week 5, they were extremely small.
You can point to Denver finally moving the chains for the first time this season on the opening drive as progress. The Broncos actually picked up two first downs on their opening possession, though it still ended with a punt.
The Broncos also led for most of the game, which has been another inconvenient and nagging storyline around this team through the first quarter of the season. That's progress, to be sure, but keeping it in context, it was by no means impressive.
Getting the run game over 100 yards on the day and staying balanced from a run-pass perspective was another step in the right direction, and the offense got points (13 to be exact) on each of the Broncos' takeaways. But I'm stretching to find the silver linings here, if you can't tell.
The Broncos took some small steps forward as a rushing offense in L.A., but they have a long way to go in terms of efficiency. Payton has been coaching in this league long enough to know that without a viable run game, a quarterback is often dead in the water.
That's especially true with a slumping Year-3 quarterback.
"I think after four weeks, there's a handful of things that collectively, and it starts with me, where it's like, all right, let's focus on these details," Payton said. "I think the byproduct helps the quarterback. Obviously, the hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball."
The Broncos have a lot to work on with very little time to do it. The Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday night showdown, so once again, there's no rest for the weary.
After the Seahawks game, though, the Broncos will get three extra days — known colloquially as a 'mini-bye' — to prepare for their next opponent. That will be the Broncos' first and only chance to catch a breath before their actual Week 10 bye.
In the meantime, any improvement Nix shows will have to be done on the hoof.

title: Broncos' Biggest Winners & Losers in 23-17 Victory Over Chargers
full_text:
But the Denver Broncos' 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers was about as ugly as it gets . The Broncos' defense did the heavy lifting, while the offense stunk up the joint for most of the game.
Those Broncos fans hoping Sean Payton's return to calling the plays would be an immediate cure for whatever is ailing this offense were not only disappointed — they're likely even more alarmed.
However, the Broncos found a way to get it done. In his first game back at the play-calling controls, Payton was able to notch his first win over the Chargers at SoFi Stadium as Broncos head coach, as his team moves to 3-2 in the standings.
As we sift through the aftermath of Denver's divisional win, let's break down the Broncos' biggest winners and losers coming out of this game.
Payton put a mountain of pressure on his shoulders by taking back the play-calling from offensive coordinator Davis Webb . The decision also added more pressure on Nix amid his slump, but I digress. Payton asked for the pressure, and by virtue of the win, eased some of it.
However, the Broncos' offense didn't look markedly different with Payton calling the plays against the Chargers. But after Justin Herbert was able to battle back into this game and take the lead, it wouldn't have been a big surprise to see the Broncos wilt and lose this game.
That's not what happened, though. Thanks to some clutch-time play by the Broncos' defense, Payton was able to get his first win over Jim Harbaugh at SoFi Stadium, and preserve the appearance that his decision to take back the play sheet was the right one.
Alas, though, the Broncos finished with just 224 yards of total offense. They only converted one third down on 12 attempts — wrap your brain around that — and went 2-of-5 in the red zone. Nothing was working.
In terms of progress, there wasn't much to point to on Sunday. However, the Broncos did get move the chains on their opening drive for the first time this season and led for most of the game. I'll take that as a silver-lining development amid the upheaval of Payton taking back the play-calling.
Make no mistake, though: this game only hammered home the reality of Webb being the scapegoat for Denver's shockingly impotent offense. Payton has his work cut out for him to truly turn this ship around.
Something is wrong with Nix. What it could be is anyone's guess, but he continues to look far from the quarterback he was in his first two seasons.
In L.A., Nix started on solid footing, delivering an efficient if unspectacular performance early on. He had one really nice 36-yard throw to tight end Evan Engram to help set up the Broncos' first touchdown of the day.
It was all downhill from there, though. As has been the trend this season, Nix looked timid and completely unpoised against L.A. He's not trusting his eyes or his receivers, and it's leading to a multitude of missed opportunities and three-and-outs.
Nix finished the day 16-of-27 for 123 yards and a touchdown. He didn't throw any interceptions, but he fumbled twice, losing one of them. That lost fumble created a massive momentum swing that allowed the Chargers to take the lead late.
Nix entered the 2026 season with seven career fumbles. He has five already through the first five games of this season — another microcosm of the meta issues plaguing the third-year quarterback.
When it comes to what's eating at Nix, theories abound. It's not the play-calling, though. That, we know. The only thing that makes any sense to me, at this point, is that his ankle is still bothering him.
The Broncos need to get to the bottom of the Nix situation, fast.
Jones had one heck of a game. He totaled four tackles, and picked off Herbert late to help ice the game.
Brandon Jones in the right place at the right time 🗣️ @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/iZZSY0BYw1
Earlier, Jones recovered a Charlie Kolar fumble forced by Talanoa Hufanga that led direcetly to the Broncos' first touchdown of the game. When Hufanga exited in the second half with an ankle injury, never to return, Jones did a lot of the heavy lifting on the back end of the secondary.
Lutz missed his third field-goal attempt of the season, a got-to-have-it 42-yarder with the Broncos' trailing 17-10 in the fourth quarter. He doesn't have the biggest leg, but inside of 45 yards, Lutz is usually reliable.
Not so this season. Special teams coordinator Darren Rizzi needs to get to the bottom of what's eating Lutz as quickly as Payton does with Nix.
I already mentioned him, but Engram was the Broncos' most effective pass-catcher on the day. He led the team with five receptions for 55 yards and came very close to scoring a touchdown.
Bo Nix drops it in the bucket to Evan Engram 🪣 @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AntTdNFDKs
Engram ran his routes well and when the ball went his way, he fought hard to pick up extra yardage. It was good to see the veteran tight end lead the team in receptions and yards.
Waddle posted his third game of the season with two or fewer receptions, finishing with two grabs on a team-high five targets for just 19 yards. He also had one rush for nine yards.
Despite showing his frustration on the sideline, Waddle's drop in the second half killed another dead-on-arrival drive. I was hoping that Payton's play-calling would lead to more consistent Waddle usage, but he and Nix continued to struggle getting on the dame page.
Given what Denver gave up to acquire Waddle from the Miami Dolphins, it's fair to consider him a big disappointment this season. Outside of his 138-yard Week 2 performance, he's been a dud thus far.
Bonitto entered this game with just one sack on the season, but he took down Justin Herbert twice. Bonitto gave L.A.'s depleted offensive line fits all game long.
Nik Bonitto breaks through and gets the sack 💪 @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SapZ5OhaCU
The Pro Bowl rush linebacker continues to show modest progress as a run defender, too, finishing with a season-high four tackles. However, he missed two tackles against the Chargers, so there's still plenty of room for improvement.
Right tackle Mike McGlinchey was especially bad, but the Broncos' entire starting five turned in another concerning performance. They were unable to create any push in the run game until deep in the fourth quarter.
The lack of poise and discipline from this unit has become alarming. From pre-snap penalties to holding fouls, the Broncos' offensive line was a major reason for the Broncos' lack of success on Sunday.
The O-line only allowed one sack on Nix, but he was pressured five times. This unit is another quandry Payton needs to get to the bottom of fast, especially given the amount of salary-cap dollars the Broncos have allocated to the O-line.
Lastly, the Broncos need to strongly consider sitting McGlinchey down and rolling with Alex Palczewski at right tackle. McGlinchey is highly paid, but he's become a liability.
Dobbins ran hard in this game, but with only a few exceptions, he didn't get much help from his O-line. Finishing with 68 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries, the veteran back turned in his best performance of the season against his former team.
J.K. Dobbins scores the first TD of the game 👏 @DENvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/2x4pE7u2qJ
It was great to see Dobbins notch his first touchdown of the season. His fourth-quarter running helped the Broncos battle back and win this game.
Like Dobbins, Sutton was able to score his first touchdown of the season, but he finished with just two receptions for 18 yards. He and Nix have not been able to get on the same page, which is another alarming symptom of just how bad this offense is, given the strong chemistry this duo forged over the preceding two seasons.
Sutton isn't fighting for the ball and coming down with it anymore. That used to be a hallmark of his game and why his quarterbacks — from Joe Flacco to Drew Lock to Teddy…

title: 3 Alarming Takeaways From Broncos' 23-17 Win Over Chargers
full_text:
It was frustrating, but the “Heart Attack Horsies” struck again, as the Denver Broncos managed to hold off the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium , 23-17.
Bolstered by an incredible defensive showing against a battered Chargers offense, Denver managed to sneak its way to a 3-2 start and keep pace in the AFC West. The Broncos' offense had several short fields to navigate and was in scoring position for the majority of the second half, but there were still a lot of issues.
We'll have film to watch tomorrow, but here are my three big instant takeaways from the Broncos' third win of the season.
Don't let the final score steer you wrong. Nix and the Broncos' offense were absolutely putrid against the Chargers.
Despite one long scoring drive in the second quarter that featured a fleeting look at a solid rushing attack, the Broncos couldn't execute in the passing game. Denver had five three-and-outs before the fourth-quarter scoring fest.
Outside of that long touchdown drive, Sean Payton's play-calling looked almost exactly the same as Davis Webb's in the first four games, with incredibly similar results. Webb was relieved of the play-calling duties last week, a scapegoat, it would seem.
Those fourth-quarter scores were all set up by Denver's incredible defensive play, including a strip-sack of Justin Herbert, a Brandon Jones interception, and a turnover on downs.
Denver had three fourth-quarter possessions starting inside the Chargers' 40-yard line and a fourth at their 41-yard line, so only coming away with 13 points is disappointing. Wil Lutz did miss a 42-yard field goal, but that drive started at the Chargers' 27-yard line, and the Broncos were only able to generate three yards.
That's not nearly good enough, especially with how poor and depleted the Chargers' defense was going into the game.
This was arguably the Broncos' worst offensive showing this year, and Payton called the plays. It's time for the offense to start executing on the field, and that's on the players.
But hey; at least Nix can now say he's defeated Justin Herbert head-to-head.
Even without all of the takeaways in the fourth quarter, Denver's defense played one heck of a football game. The Chargers had one long drive coming out of halftime and an explosive 42-yard touchdown run by Kimani Vidal in the third quarter, hot on the heels of a Nix lost fumble and a big momentum change, but that's pretty much it.
Denver has had tackling issues in the run game all year, and Vidal's touchdown was just another example to point to. But overall, Denver's run defense played well.
The Chargers may have finished the game with 155 yards on the ground, but outside of the Vidal touchdown, they only had 113 yards on 33 carries. That's 3.2 yards per carry.
54 of those yards came via Herbert scrambles. Omarion Hampton only had 33 yards on his 14 carries, and Keaton Mitchell finished with 11 yards on six attempts. You can't play it much better than that.
Even without Surtain, Denver's secondary was incredible. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine held it down on the boundary.
Abrams-Draine had an interception taken away due to his own pass-interference penalty, but otherwise went unnoticed for the majority of the game. He finished with three total tackles and broke up a pass.
Barron was awesome as a tackler in space and had a solid game in coverage as well. Having rarely seen the field to open the season, a lot of fans in Broncos Country were beginning to think that drafting him in the first round last year was a major mistake.
Barron gets to wave a finger in his doubter's direction.
The Broncos' secondary had a great day overall. Herbert only completed 14 passes on 24 attempts for 121 yards and a touchdown.
The veteran quarterback looked rattled at times and put his horrendous decision-making on full display, as best illustrated by his game-sealing interception thrown to Brandon Jones late in the fourth quarter. However, Herbert was playing behind a battered offensive line that played four rookies in place of starters, and he was without half of his receiving corps.
But good teams capitalize on such vulnerabilities. That's what the Broncos' defense did, sacking Herbert five times, taking the ball away thrice, and delivering Payton his first-ever win at SoFi Stadium as Denver's head coach.

title: 5 Dream Trades That Could Transform the Broncos
full_text:
NFL trade rumors usually don't heat up for another couple of weeks when we draw closer to the trade deadline on November 10.
And yet, this week alone, we've seen Philadelphia Eagles center offensive lineman Cam Jurgens traded and possibly Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr . Teams seem a bit more ready to get something done sooner rather than later if it means solving a roster problem.
Those selling might be more willing to admit they aren't quite ready to compete for a Super Bowl and need draft capital to get where they want to be. However, the Denver Broncos still have solid Super Bowl ambitions, so could they be in the market to make a big splash before the deadline — that one player to help them get over the hump?
The Broncos worked the phones ahead of last year's trade deadline and tried to make a deal with the Miami Dolphins for Jaylen Waddle. It didn't happen before the deadline, but the Broncos got their man in the offseason. Waddle is the most recent example of the Broncos' pre-deadline trade maneuvers.
If the Broncos really want to go big and find that one missing piece for the now and the future, there could be some opportunities to do just that, depending on whether they're willing to pay for the privilege.
Today, I'm breaking down five dream trade targets that would put the Broncos on much more solid Super Bowl footing. Keep in mind that these are dream trade scenarios. The likelihood of them happening is very low, so let's have some fun.
I can't think of a better player to add to this roster and really strike fear into the rest of the league than Simmons. Pairing Simmons with Zach Allen on the Broncos' interior, with Nik Bonitto and this edge-rushing group, would give this team the most feared defensive front in the NFL.
On top of his ability to get after the quarterback, Simmons is also an excellent run defender. He won’t fix all of Denver's problems on defense, but adding maybe the best interior defensive lineman in football would put the league on notice.
Simmons's contract is one of the biggest hurdles to making this a reality. The Titans just signed him to an extension, and they'd take on a big dead-money hit to trade him so soon. On top of that, the Titans would likely ask for something similar to Myles Garrett-type compensation.
That might not be in the Broncos' best interest for winning now and in the future.
Broncos Country has been pounding the table for a top-tier linebacker for years. The Broncos have made some attempts through the draft and free agency, but they either saw their target get drafted before their pick, or they got priced out of what they were willing to spend.
Maybe the Broncos' best option for an upgrade is through a trade. The Eagles seem willing to listen to trade inquiries right now. They're not fully committing to a rebuild yet, but if they lose another couple of games between now and November 10, I could see the Eagles taking more calls.
Sean Payton is very familiar with Baun, having drafted him in the third round back in 2020 with the New Orleans Saints. Baun didn’t have his breakout years under Payton, but I could see the Broncos head coach wanting to make up for lost time.
Baun has been a huge surprise for the Eagles and a big part of why they have been able to field a top-tier defense in recent years. He's 30 years old, but he doesn’t have a lot of wear and tear like so many linebackers of his age do.
Baun would also fit well into the Vane Joseph system as an aggressive downhill attacker who can also drop back into coverage. Baun might be the most realistic player to become a Bronco on this list, and I doubt it would cost an arm and a leg to get it done.
Perhaps an early Day 3 pick would close the deal.
Again, the Eagles seem like sellers at this time, and I could see Barkley added to the list of trade bait. He's heading into the back-nine of his career, which could mean the Eagles don't view him as part of their future plan.
Barkley is still playing at a very high level, averaging 5.5 yards per carry despite a shaky Eagles offensive line.
The Broncos' offensive struggles this season have been blamed on Davis Webb, but the poor execution is the biggest culprit. Running back is one position where an upgrade would do wonders for how everything else functions.
J.K. Dobbins doesn’t look healthy, RJ Harvey is more of a receiving option, and Jonah Coleman is on injured reserve until Week 7 at the soonest. Adding Barkley to this room would give the Broncos a back who can make something from nothing and force teams to respect the run game asa threat.
This is another situation where I don't think the trade would be too costly. With Barkley being 29 years old, I would guess a late Day 2/early Day 3 pick might be able to get a deal done.
Payne coming to Denver would probably not get people too excited. He had one great season a few years back and has been mostly average otherwise.
However, Payne would give the Broncos a very good run defender who could be added to the interior rotation. He can be streaky as a pass rusher, but there is no denying he is a force in the middle of a defense and does well holding his ground and locating the ball carrier.
Payne getting traded could also be a very realistic option. The Commanders are not looking great so far this season and he has an expiring contract.
Once again, the compensation would be overly pricey to acquire Payne — if the Broncos were of a mind to call Washington. He has a sizable cap hit, though, if he were to be traded, meaning the Broncos would likely want to rework his contract before making any kind of deal for him.
McBride might be the least likely trade of the five listed here. But the Broncos need some help on offense, and landing arguably the best tight end in football could elevate this offense.
McBride is one of the NFL's biggest matchup nightmares regardless of position. Throw in how he would instantly become a safety valve for Bo Nix and a weapon he could grow with over the next several years, and it's clear why McBride fits the dream scenario.
There would be hurdles to making such a trade possible. McBride just recently got paid, making it very difficult for Arizona to clear his contract.
Another big hurdle would be the compensation required to pry McBride off Arizona's hands. The tight end position is not usually considered high value, but he's such a game-changing player, I can't imagine he'd go for anything less than a first-round pick.
Are the Broncos willing to give up such premium draft capital for a non-premium position? The answer is likely no, but pairing McBride with Nix for the next several years would be a dream scenario.
The likelihood of any of these deals getting done is, again, very slim. Payton has never traded anything higher than a fourth-round pick at the deadline, and Broncos GM George Paton seems to be more inclined toward a seller's posture than a buyer's.
That said, the Broncos would be wise to make a move of some type ahead of the deadline. Maybe not Simmons, Barkley, or McBride big , but the Broncos have several positions that could use an in-season talent infusion.
