title: Chargers' Strengths Are Clear, but Broncos Can Exploit These Flaws
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers may be winless, but they still have plenty of talent.
However, the Chargers also have glaring holes that should be easy to attack. That's exactly what the Denver Broncos will be aiming to do at SoFi Stadium.
The question is whether the Broncos can execute well enough to exploit the Chargers' biggest weaknesses, while doing what it takes to neutralize the biggest threats L.A. poses. If the Broncos struggle to do either, this game will be much closer that it should be.
Leading up to this game, I've laid out two key matchups , my bold predictions , and the Broncos' sleepers to watch . Now it's time to examine the biggest threats the Chargers pose to the Broncos on both sides of the ball, as well as the vulnerable spots Denver can attack.
Quentin Johnston would have been the guy here, but after he was ruled out on Friday, I had to make an audible. Gadsden is a talented receiving tight end who can create mismatches against linebackers and safeties.
His role in the Chargers' offense hasn't been clearly defined, which could be a needed break for the Broncos, given their recent issues with tight ends, especially tackling them (see the Travis Kelce and George Kittle touchdowns).
Even so, the Broncos will have to be wary of the threat Gadsden poses. Vance Joseph will need to have a plan to account for Gadsden, especially given some of the plays the tight end made against Denver a year ago when L.A.'s offense was performing at a significantly higher level.
Strange has been terrible since entering the NFL, and this year has been much the same. He has been the weak link in the Chargers' run game, has allowed nine pressures, and has been called for four penalties.
Strange has been one of the NFL's worst guards to start the season. Even with the Broncos' defensive line featuring Zach Allen and others, this should be a game where Malcolm Roach or Eyioma Uwazurike shines.
Even if that doesn't happen, Allen is poised for another monster game. With the Chargers' offensive line so beaten up and missing three starters, the Broncos have no excuse but to win in the trenches. The opportunities for the big negative plays will be there against Strange.
The Chargers have a very underrated corner in Still. He has size, length, and athleticism that help him match up with almost any type of receiver.
Still's versatility is a boost, and he can take the ball away anytime you target him. Now, he isn't immune to giving up big plays, as he is a risk-taker when attacking the ball, so the Broncos can still look to his side as long as they're calculated.
Despite Still's ball skills, he's yet to notch an interception this year, with only four in his career (all in 2024), and only two pass breakups, both in Week 4.
Phillips is playing a lot with Denzel Perryman out, leaving a void at the second level of L.A.'s defense. Daiyan Henley is a great linebacker, but he is struggling to put out the fires Phillips creates while Perryman has been sidelined.
Now, Phillips is a lighter downhill linebacker, which creates openings in the run game, and he really struggles in coverage. Denver should look to isolate matchups on Phillips, especially with running back RJ Harvey, tight end Evan Engram, or a receiver, and hunt for opportunities that come at the beleaguered linebacker's expense.

title: Broncos vs. Chargers: How to Watch or Stream Sunday's AFC West Showdown
full_text:
It's been a wild week at Denver Broncos HQ.
Losses in the Sean Payton era are few and far between, so last week's defeat was enough on its own to create some drama as the Broncos fell to 2-2. Then Payton decided to take the play-calling from offensive coordinator Davis Webb , and that storyline has dominated the headlines , airwaves, and podcasts since Wednesday.
Payton took back the play-calling because he believes it's in the Broncos' best interest, but I can't help but wonder how much of the drama of this past week has taken the focus off this trip to face the Los Angeles Chargers. Hopefully, Payton's veteran experience is enough to keep the Broncos' on task because he's 1-5 against the Chargers since arriving in Denver in 2023.
The Chargers may be 0-4, but that only makes them more dangerous. Desperation can be a powerful thing, and despite all the problems the Chargers have had this season, Jim Harbaugh is also a veteran coach who knows what he's doing; he'll have his players locked in and hellbent on breaking the ice in the win column against an AFC West rival.
I expect the Broncos' offense to be better with Payton at the helm, and that includes Bo Nix, but they've yet to win a game at SoFi Stadium. Denver can't look past the Chargers at what's coming to Denver next week on Thursday night.
If the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, this AFC West throwdown is likely to be competitive. We've dropped our final Broncos-Chargers predictions and picks , and we'll be covering every single angle of this game leading up to kickoff, starting with all the info you'll need to watch the action, regardless of where you're located.
#Broncos television coverage map for Week 5 Those in BLUE will get #DENvsLAC in the CBS late window pic.twitter.com/AV9i45Efcu
Keep in mind, streaming this game locally requires a subscription to either YouTubeTV or Paramount+ .
With an NFL+ subscription, you can live stream local and primetime games on mobile and tablets. You also get NFL Network and live game audio. An NFL+ premium subscription includes NFL RedZone and full replays of games across devices.
The Broncos will be in their Summit White jerseys and pants against the Chargers. It's the same uniform combo Denver rocked on the road at SoFi Stadium last year, too.
Cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II and Riley Moss have been ruled out of this game . Everyone else is a full go.
With Surtain and Moss down, the Broncos elevated two cornerbacks from the practice squad . Rookie Brent Austin and Sean Fresch Jr. will be making their NFL debuts.
The Broncos have Jahdae Barron, Ja'Quan McMillian, and Kris Abrams-Draine healthy and available, but Austin and Fresch will be dressed and ready for action if needed.

title: Broncos Make Two Telling Roster Moves Ahead of Chargers Showdown
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are uncomfortably short on cornerbacks.
With starting cornerback duo Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) ruled out of Sunday's road game against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Broncos have three remaining cover corners on the active roster.
Unsurprisingly, the Broncos are elevating practice-squad cornerbacks Brent Austin and Sean Fresch Jr. to the active roster for Sunday's game at SoFi Stadium. In response to the injury bug taking a massive bite out of the Broncos' cornerback room last week, the team also signed veteran defensive back Ugo Amadi to the practice squad on Friday.
Amadi has been playing in the NFL since arriving as a Seattle Seahawks fourth-round pick in 2019, and while he has 85 games of experience, two days was not enough time to get him ready to be elevated for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
Austin and Fresch will dress, but beyond some special teams action, they're unlikely to see the field on defense unless an injury befalls Jahdae Barron, Ja'Quan McMillian, or Kris Abrams-Draine (knock on wood). I suppose there's always a chance Vance Joseph could call a dime package that demands four cornerbacks on the field, but time will tell.
Austin is an undrafted rookie out of Cal. He impressed in training camp, though his preseason play wasn't all that great.
The Broncos saw enough to want to keep the 5-foot-11, 180-pound Austin around on the practice squad. He's a feisty corner who's sticky in coverage and he fancies himself a bit of a ballhawk.
Fresch was signed in June on the heels of the UFL's season coming to an end. He went undrafted out of Rice University in 2025, and although the Kansas City Chiefs invited him to try out at their rookie minicamp, he wasn't signed.
Finding no NFL interest in his services, Rice essentially sat out his rookie season before signing with the UFL's San Antonio Brahmas, but that franchise soon folded, and he was drafted by the St. Louis Battlehawks.
The 5-foot-8, 181-pound Fresch went on to record 41 tackles (29 solo), two sacks, and five passes defensed in 12 contests, and earned All-UFL honors as a punt returner, which was a big reason why the Broncos signed him this summer. Fresch looked excellent as a returner, but I think even the Broncos were surprised by his chops as a cornerback.
We didn't see Fresch flash much in the preseason games as a cornerback, but he had several days of training camp where he landed on the 'Winners' list. He was ultimately waived at the final roster cutdowns, but immediately re-signed to the Broncos' practice squad.
The Broncos are in a precarious position. It's not just that two of their five active corners are injured — it also happens to be the Broncos' top two players at the position.
Surtain and Moss are among the NFL's top cornerback duos, so their absence is almost surely to be felt this week, especially against a quality quarterback of Justin Herbert's caliber. The onus falls on Barron and Abrams-Draine to step up and answer the bell.
Herbert is going to test both Barron and Abrams-Draine, but the one silver lining is that the Chargers are as banged up at wide receiver as the Broncos are at cornerback. The Chargers ruled out Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quad) on Friday, while Ladd McConkey (foot) is questionable.
McConkey did not practice this week, so even though he's listed as questionable, it would be a mild surprise if he suits up. Tre' Harris remains healthy and available, though, and he's L.A.'s leading receiver this season.
Beyond Harris, the Chargers have Derius Davis and Marquez Valdes-Scantling on the active roster, and Gary Jennings and Theo Wease Jr. on the practice squad, but neither was elevated for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
The Chargers will have three healthy receivers and tight end Oronde Gadsden II going against McMillian and the Broncos' backup cornerbacks. Hopefully, the Broncos' cornerback trio can hold up and stay healthy.
Barron is coming off an impressive performance in relief of Surtain. And it just so happens that Abrams-Draine's first career inteception came off Herbert. Optimistic harbingers, perhaps.
Herbert is dangerous, as all Broncos fans know, but his offensive line is decimated and missing three starters. If this isn't a get-right game for the Broncos' pass rush, I don't know what is.

title: Several Broncos Could Make History vs. Chargers
full_text:
The week following a loss is always rough, but this one has been especially tumultuous for the Denver Broncos.
Sean Payton stripped the play-calling duties from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb — a storyline that has dominated the headlines and conversation in and around the Mile High City for obvious reasons. Webb has taken the setback shockingly well and remains firmly behind his head coach and offense.
The pressure is now on Payton to turn the ship around offensively, but as a head coach for 20 years or so, it's not a burden unfamiliar to him. Now that the play-calling Band-Aid has been ripped off, Payton's focus turns to figuring out how to beat Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers in their house for the first time.
Since arriving as head coach in 2023, Payton is 1-5 all-time against the Chargers. His only win came last season in Denver as Harbaugh rested Justin Herbert and most of his starters.
So, the Chargers may be winless, but you can believe that Payton isn't looking past them. L.A. has his full and undivided attention.
Entering this Week 5 tilt, several Broncos have individual milestones or records within reach. Let's take a look, starting with the head coach himself.
Payton is currently tied with Knox for the 12th-most regular-season wins among head coaches in league history. A win over the Chargers would give Payton sole possession of No. 12.
That's a pretty cool milestone to reach, but Payton just wants to beat the Chargers at SoFi Stadium. If it results in him moving up the all-time rankings, that's a cherry on top.
With two passing scores against the Chargers, Nix would tie Brian Griese and Jake Plummer for the fourth-most passing touchdowns in Broncos history. Nix hasn't looked like himself this season, but each week he has a milestone or record within reach.
The reason for that? Oh yeah, lest we should forget: Nix's first two NFL seasons were the most prolific by a quarterback in NFL history. He's the only quarterback to ever pass for 7,500-plus yards and 50-plus touchdowns while winning 20-plus games through his first two seasons.
Most Broncos fans are well aware of that statistical singularity; I mention it only to remind everyone of what Nix is capable of — especially with Payton as his play-caller. And set the stage.
With one reception against the Chargers, Sutton would pass Ed McCaffrey for the fifth-most catches in team history. Through four weeks, Sutton only has nine receptions for 86 yards — which is normally a pretty good stat line for him in a single game.
Sutton is due for a big game. As I wrote on Thursday, I have a sneaking suspicion he'll end up being one of the biggest winners of Payton's decision to take back the play-calling.
Payton loves his big-bodied X-receivers and he loves Sutton. The Pro Bowler is about to be shown some big love by his head coach and quarterback.
If Waddle can get over 100 yards in L.A., he'll become just the fifth player in Broncos history to notch multiple 100-yard receiving games in his first season with the team — and the first to do so since 2014, when Emmanuel Sanders arrived in Denver.
With Webb at the controls, Waddle has posted two games with two or fewer catches. In Week 3, though, he had a huge 138-yard game, and then last week against the San Francisco 49ers, he scored his first touchdown as a Bronco.
Payton told his wife, Skylene, to draft Waddle on her fantasy football team. We're fixin' to find out why.
With one sack, Allen would become the first interior defensive lineman to total at least four sacks in each of the last six seasons. That's pretty cool.
Allen leads the Broncos with 3.0 sacks, and he's been one of the few stars on defense to consistently dominate in each game thus far. By the way, both Allen and linebacker Alex Singleton will record the 100th game of their respective careers on Sunday when the Chargers take their first snap.
If Lutz makes his first extra point on Sunday, he'll tie Bass for the second-longest point-after-made streak since 2015. Lutz has been Mr. Consistent in the extra point department.
Alas, Lutz's reliability as a field-goal kicker hasnt been great this season. He's 5-of-7 on field-goal tries — a mark he'll surely be looking to improve upon dramatically.

title: Davis Webb Just Showed Broncos Fans What He's Really Made Of
full_text:
Just as Sean Payton foretold, Davis Webb is taking this week's professional setback quite well.
Payton said Webb would be "fantastic" at the podium on Friday, and he was. The Denver Broncos' 31-year-old offensive coordinator admitted his disappointment in Payton taking back the play-calling duties , while reaffirming his ongoing commitment to the team and his support for his head coach in no uncertain terms.
“I think anytime that happens in any aspect of your life, job-wise, it is a little bit [disappointing]," Webb said on Friday. "But in the same breath, that’s the NFL. You get going. I’ve been a backup QB, been up and down before, and that’s kind of how it goes.”
Webb is only four years into his NFL coaching career. In January of 2023, Payton literally pulled him from the quarterback ranks and onto his new Broncos coaching staff within weeks of Webb starting in the New York Giants' season finale.
Webb knew what he was getting into when he accepted the offensive coordinator job and play-calling duties. He sized up the opportunity from every angle and came to terms with the possible outcomes.
“I have taught myself early to think about the best- and worst-case scenarios," Webb said. "If you’re OK with both, then take that job on… Nothing I can really do about it now except be the best teammate and offensive coordinator I can be. That’s what I’m trying to do.”
Again, Webb is no stranger to professional setbacks. That was essentially the life he led as an NFL quarterback: more of a journeyman backup than an established starter.
Payton himself went through a similar situation in 2002 with the Giants when Jim Fassel took the play-calling duties from him. A few short years later, Payton was the head coach of the New Orleans Saints.
"I think for him, there was a lot of empathy with our conversation because that did happen to him," Webb said of Payton. "We talked about that for a long time, but in the same breath, it’s a different situation as well."
Payton relinquished the play-calling duties for a reason; he genuinely values Webb's unique talent, and when he made the decision early this past offseason, he believed it would be in the Broncos' best interest. Alas, as the offense has suffered from brutally slow starts and a lack of rhythm, Payton's fingers inched ever closer to taking the play sheet back before he finally took action.
"I don’t think anyone wanted to go through this right now, but he’s excited to get the chance to call plays," Webb said of Payton. "I know he’s itching, and we’ll see how it goes.”
As the coordinator, Webb is still in charge of running the offensive meetings and "helping out the quarterback room." Again, he's disappointed to be relieved of the play-calling duties, but his disappointment is more about the Broncos' failure to launch offensively early this season.
Amid the upheaval of Payton's big decision, the Broncos have been game-planning for the winless Los Angeles Chargers . The imperative of going into SoFi Stadium and winning this game takes precedence over all the drama, for lack of a better term.
“I think it’s more just how we started off offensively [with his disappointment], but I’m excited to see how our team responds this week," Webb said. "We’ll try to get a team win against a divisional opponent. It was a long week in some ways, but in other ways, it’s back to work.”
So much goes into the art of calling plays in the NFL. It's not just picking and choosing the right plays to put in the game plan or to roll out in the first 15 to 20 plays of a contest.
It's about sequencing, adjusting, and all the while, calling plays that maximize personnel strengths while attacking opponents' weaknesses. And so much more.
Gut feeling has much to do with it in-game, especially once a play-caller has burned through the scripted first 15. That's where talent and experience intersect.
Along the way, Webb feels confident that he was able to speed up the Broncos' play-calling process to cut out the delay-of-game penalties and give quarterback Bo Nix more time to survey the defense pre-snap. It may have been hard to deduce from watching on TV or from the stands, but Webb believes the Broncos' offensive operation was increasingly cleaner by the week.
Would that it was also increasingly productive. Webb learned a lot about himself — valuable information that will serve him down the road as his coaching career progresses.
"I think I’ve learned a ton when it comes to sequencing, to play selection, to how we game-plan, to really how the players respond to it," Webb said. "So I think everyone’s got a hand in that, and we’ll see what happens.”
The young OC ultimately takes responsibility for the unit's failure to launch on his watch, but even Payton and veterans like Bo Nix and Courtland Sutton said that everyone's fingerprints are on it. Nix has not looked like his usual self this season, which is obviously a big reason why Payton is taking back the reins.
"We were so close in a lot of areas. I think in the San Francisco game, you can see a few plays that were very, very close to being successful," Webb said. "Same with the week before against the Rams. We just didn’t put a full game together consistently enough. I take responsibility for that. I’m the play-caller, but we all have a hand in this, and hopefully we can get going this weekend a little bit faster.”
As we learned from Payton on Thursday, everyone at Broncos HQ who touches the offense feels like they let Webb down, including Nix . There's no question this was a collective failure.
Webb and Nix have a close relationship, and that won't change with Payton taking back the play-calling and being the voice in the quarterback's ear on game day. Webb confirmed that it was Payton who broke the news to Nix.
“I think Sean might have done that to be honest with you," Webb said of Nix. "But again, like I told him, I’m going to be like I always have been in my mind and his mind: I’m all in for him. I’m all in for everybody in this offensive unit, and I’m going to do everything I can to make sure everybody’s in a position to be successful.”
Webb is a selfless leader. His comportment and remarks at the podium on Friday were impressive. He's as mature and insightful as he is talented and knowledgeable, and Payton still sees a head-coaching job in his protégé's future, though this week's setback may have reset the timeline — but you never know.
The Broncos will rally behind Payton as the play-caller moving forward, which is how it's been for 54 of the 58 games (counting playoffs) he's served as the head coach. Webb will do everything in his power to help the offense get over the hump and break through the obstacle that has been holding it back.
But if Webb is right, it won't take much longer for Nix and the offense to finally break out.
“Extremely, extremely close," Webb said of the offense. "I think there are a few things in the pass game that were close last week, a few things in the run game that were close last week. You can see the second halves of the Jaguars game, the Rams game. I mean, I just mentioned three good teams right there. "
As I wrote in my Winners and Losers article analyzing Payton's play-calling decision, Nix stands to gain a lot from working under his head coach's experienced hand. Payton shepherded Drew Brees into the Pro Football Hall of Fame and helped Nix become the winningest and most statistically prolific quarterback in NFL history through his first two years.
It really is a bummer for Webb, and for Payton and Nix, to be honest. They all wanted this arrangement to work out.
But the NFL is a production-based business, and while the Broncos have managed to beat two of the league's four best teams thus far, the offense simply hasn't looked like a Super Bowl contender.
"Kansas City was tough on everybody… So I think getting off to this start, being at 2-2 is not what we wanted, but it’s where we’re at," Webb said. "I think that a lot of teams in the NFL will be OK with…

title: Detroit Lions Grades: Offense Shakes Off Struggles, Mows Down Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions got off to a sluggish start in Week 5 against the Arizona Cardinals.
They went three-and-out on their first series, then gave up a touchdown to the Cardinals on their first defensive series. However, when the second quarter rolled around, their fortunes changed dramatically.
Pushed forward by some aggression offensively, the Lions scored on seven consecutive drives including 31 unanswered points at one time and wound up with an emphatic 45-21 win to move to 3-2 on the season.
Here are grades for each position group following the Lions' dismantling of the Cardinals.
Jared Goff was once again excellent for the majority of Sunday's game. He was sacked on his first two drop-backs, including on a safety blitz from Budda Baker that wasn't picked up, but was clean and efficient after that.
Goff made some tight window throws to Sam LaPorta and Jameson Williams to convert fourth downs, with the throw to Williams going for a touchdown. His first touchdown pass came on a well-designed concept that left LaPorta running uncovered up the right sideline.
The veteran finished 19-of-30 for 271 yards and three touchdowns, and now has 12 passing touchdowns and zero interceptions through five games. He became the second quarterback to have thrown 12 touchdowns and no interceptions through that time frame.
Jahmyr Gibbs helped spark the Lions' offense. After the initial fourth-down conversion to LaPorta, Gibbs rushed for 16 yards on the next play fueled by a push from several of his teammates. He'd punch it in two plays later, giving him the first of his two scores on the afternoon.
The Alabama product broke Barry Sanders' record for most touchdowns by any player under the age of 25, and will likely create some serious separation given that he doesn't turn 25 until next March.
Gibbs also had some valuable reps in pass-protection and had an overall thorough performance. He tallied 151 rushing yards and two scores on the ground, along with five catches for 56 yards as a receiver.
The Lions had some unique looks for their wide receivers in Sunday's game. There was a double reverse involving Amon-Ra St. Brown that turned into a screen, as well as multiple slot-screen looks for St. Brown.
Ultimately, the group was highly efficient throughout the game. Jameson Williams made his two catches count, as both went for touchdowns including a 39-yard scoring grab in the third quarter after he beat his defender deep.
St. Brown had 69 yards on six catches, while Isaac TeSlaa did not have a catch on two targets. In an unfortunate development, Tom Kennedy went down with a knee injury on a punt return and did not re-enter the game.
LaPorta was a huge spark for the offense in Sunday's game. After the team went three drives without a first-down, they finally broke through when LaPorta snagged a 12-yard reception on a fourth-down to move the chains and set up their first touchdown.
He'd reach the end zone on the next drive, as some clever play-designing from Drew Petzing left him all alone for a 38-yard touchdown on a fourth-and-1. LaPorta would finish with a game-high 88 receiving yards on five catches.
It was a tough start for Detroit's offensive line, as their first two pass plays ended in sacks. Budda Baker's blitz was well-timed and simply overpowered the outnumbered line, while center Juice Scruggs was to blame for the second sack as he was beat by former Lion Roy Lopez.
After that tough start, however, everything clicked for the group. They finished averaging over five yards per carry on the ground, and would allow just one more sack.
Rookie Blake Miller took some lumps, as he was whistled for two penalties, but delivered another reliable performance.
The Lions notched five sacks on Sunday, giving them 20 as a team which is the most in franchise history through five games. D.J. Wonnum led the charge with two sacks, both of which came at key points in the first half.
Aidan Hutchinson teamed up with linebacker Malcolm Rodriguez on a sack that forced a fourth-quarter turnover on downs, while rookie Skyler Gill-Howard and Alim McNeill teamed up for one to force a long field goal that was ultimately missed.
Detroit did some shuffling with their linebacking corps ahead of kickoff, with Devin White returning to the starting lineup. However, White suffered a forearm injury in the first half and is expected to miss significant time.
As a result, the Lions leaned on their depth. Jack Campbell had a team-high 11 tackles, and had good coverage on Trey McBride's touchdown where the tight end made an incredible juggling catch.
Elsewhere, Derrick Barnes had a sack and five tackles while Rodriguez was credited with a half-sack when he teamed up with Hutchinson.
Sunday was Detroit's best defensive game to date, and one of their top performers was cornerback Roger McCreary. The Cardinals went after McCreary early and often Sunday, and he finished the game with a team-high six passes defensed.
D.J. Reed had three tackles for loss amidst his seven solo tackles in Sunday's game. Rookie Keith Abney logged some snaps at the safety position, and recorded his first-career interception on the final play of the first half.
Detroit had some early miscues on special teams, as they were called for illegal formation on kick return and nearly had a punt blocked. However, they were outstanding in the return game with Tom Kennedy and Jacob Saylors notching some big returns.
Kennedy was replaced by Amon-Ra St. Brown as the punt returner when he exited, and St. Brown nearly had a disaster as he coughed up the ball on his first return. However, Tay Martin avoided the damage by recovering the fumble.
Jake Bates remained perfect on the year, connecting on a 46-yard field goal before the half and knocking through all of his extra points.
While the slow start took away the potential for a perfect showing for the coaching staff, it was their best schematic game through the first five weeks. Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing had a number of well-designed plays go for big gains, and defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard worked around a tough start to dial up a nice showing.
At one point, the defense had forced five-straight three-and-outs, which was a big development from weeks past. Sheppard seemed to be pulling the right strings throughout the game, which led to the success.
Now, the Lions get a week to recover and bounce back before two-straight divisional games that will be pivotal to Detroit's hopes of winning the division.

title: Everything Dan Campbell Said After Detroit Lions Defeated Cardinals
full_text:
Here is everything Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said to reporters, after defeating the Arizona Cardinals, 45-21, at State Farm Stadium.
The former NFL tight end took the opportunity to immediately give play-by-play voice Dan Miller a game ball.
Miller's wife, Cindy Miller, passed away, significantly impacting the organization and the roster.
“We'll start with this. This ball goes to Dan Miller and his family. It was hard to hear what they went through. It's been a tough road for Dan. This is for him. Salt of the earth, Dan is salt of the earth, and I know this has been hard. But now I know Cindy's (Miller) at peace, and we love you, Dan. So appreciate you. I'll open with that. The guys really responded in a big way. I thought our defense really got everything started; we attacked the run. I thought we were sticking in coverage. Very disciplined, minus a couple of plays there. I thought ‘Shep’ (Defensive Coordinator Kelvin Sheppard) and the staff did an outstanding job. The players really responded. They took it to heart. Tried to do all the little things right and we played with aggressiveness, and just really set the tone for the day. The offense fed off of that and once we found our rhythm, then the defense fed off of them and special teams, and I just thought it was a great team effort. We cleaned up a lot of the little stuff. It's not good enough; it's not. We're going to have to be a hell of a lot better when we play Green Bay coming out of the bye. But that was a step in the right direction. It got us to win number three going into the bye. I was proud of them.”
Sam LaPorta’s success on fourth down calls
“Yes, that was big, that was really big. Took it in the back of the head on a critical catch; that was a contested catch. That was a great job by (Lions QB Jared) Goff progressing through, we're going to  'Saint' (Amon-Ra St. Brown). I mean, he worked his way through it. The O-line gave him time and he found it, gave him a ball to make a play on and he went and made a play and then took a shot, held on to it. It was huge. That was really big. I thought the guys answered the bell and I thought we played pretty fearless today. That’s what we have to be able to do. That's our offense. I thought our guys really fed off each other. The O-line got going, and opened some holes, and then 'Jah' (Jahmyr Gibbs) started to come to life. He obviously made some of his own plays there once we got him started. (Sam) LaPorta was huge for us today. Jamo (Jameson Williams) was huge for us today. Those guys really stepped up and obviously 'Jah', in the run and pass game. Goff is just Goff. He's as good as they come. I’ve just been so impressed with the way he's played these five games here. I thought he's just gotten better every year, and here we are five in, and he's even better than last year. He's the real deal. Proud of these guys. I thought special teams played with some enthusiasm, some energy, which we were looking for. Our specialists did a heck of a job (Jack) Fox and (Jake) Bates. It was a good team effort; good team win.”
How important it was to play this game with a sense of urgency?
“I think the important thing is that you go all in no matter what you're going to do. Either it crumbles or they rise up, but you're going all in. You have to push your chips all the way in and you have to believe in it. We did, we applied a little pressure. Players really responded, did a great job, and they brought it to life here on Sunday. It's a good win. It'll be nice to be able to enjoy this on this flight home and for a couple of days here going into the bye.”
On getting their sense of aggression back
“Yes, it felt good. When you believe in your players, you believe in the matchups, and you feel your young players are growing. That's a lot of it. We have a young (team). Our right tackle is young, our right guard is young, our left guard is young. So when your O-line has some youth in it, they have to continue to grow and you have to be able to trust if we get certain looks, or we get a curveball, (or) it's 4th down. There's a lot that goes into it, and I really feel like they're growing. They did a heck of a job today. We picked up the protection really well. ‘Jah’ had a couple of critical pro protection reps that helped us on some of those downs. It helped, and as I said, once we get in a rhythm , we are hard to stop, and we were hard today to stop.”
On what impressed him most about the defense
“I just love the pass defense. ‘PDs’ (passes defensed), man. We got our hands on some footballs (and) we knocked some footballs down. I didn't feel like we were stressed. That's good to see. Roger (McCreary) wasn't perfect, but I thought Roger really played some sticky coverage today and I thought (D.J.) Reed played some sticky coverage. That was good to see us challenge some footballs on the back end and work in unison. We played sticky and then we got a sack. We closed the pocket in and made some huge plays there. Just to get that many 3-and-outs back-to-back-to-back, and then you answer offensively — that's the white squall. Here comes the massive wave that's coming at you, and it felt that way a little bit so that's good. We just have to get better there. We have to continue to do those things, play off of each other and be on top of the little stuff. Honestly, the couple of things we did get hit on — those are ‘mentals’ (mental mistakes). Those are ‘mentals’ and they can't happen. You can't play that good for that long and all of a sudden we get dirty eyes or we mess something up and we give up a 30-yard (play) and now they're in field goal range. It was better and I thought those guys answered the bell .”
Thoughts on playing more man-to-man coverage this week
“It helped today. You have to go by what opponent it is. We knew ‘85’ (Cardinals tight end Trey McBride), they were going to get him the football and he's a factor. They're going to target him and they're going to go to him. And then ‘14’ (Cardinals wideout Michael Wilson) is their other bell cow. He's a good receiver and he does it the hard way. He'll muscle you and wrestle you — that's what ‘85’ does too. They're pretty crafty guys so we knew we had to try to eliminate those two and it just felt like the right thing to do today. That was good. For what we did, the game plan, ‘Shep’ (Kelvin Sheppard) did a good job, players executed, and it was a ‘W.’"
On whether he felt like the team's back was against the wall this week which led to them being more aggressive on fourth downs and playing more man coverage?
“No I just felt like it was what was right for this opponent. Every week's a little bit different — we play man-to-man. We play man every game, it's just how much do you play it? Most teams play some man-to-man on third down no matter what you believe in. We opened it up a little bit today — a little bit more and reduced the variables of other things that can happen in zone (coverage) for this opponent and knowing what they had. When you do that and you do some of the things we did — there are guys who have one-on-ones in man coverage so you have to win. You have to win. You can take away guys — their best players or a best player — but somebody's still single and that player has to win. We won today.”
Update on the injuries to Lions LB Devin White and WR Tom Kennedy
“It doesn’t look good. I think Devin’s probably going to need surgery. It’s a broken forearm; it’s unfortunate. I hate it because he was doing some good things for us in this game. Then for T.K., it doesn’t look good. As far as anything short-term, we’ll know a lot more tomorrow. I think it could be a sprain somewhere in there, a pretty good sprain. Neither one of them are going to be around here for a while so I hate that. Both players have done a really good job for us. T.K., I really thought really hit it. We challenged him on hitting some of these returns. His first was outstanding and I thought his second one, he caught it, put…

title: 8 Winners, 3 Losers From Lions’ Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions looked to get back to their winning ways in Arizona. The Lions looked to rebound following a loss to Carolina in Week 4, squaring off against a 1-3 Cardinals team.
The Cardinals started with a strong defensive effort , sacking Goff on each of his first two dropbacks and scoring on their opening drive. However, it was all Motown after that, with the Lions up, 24-7, at half. The Lions kept their foot on the pedal after the break, and a garbage-time touchdown by Arizona gave the 45-21 final an ounce of respectability.
Here are the winners and losers from the contest.
Kennedy provided a spark during an underwhelming first quarter for the Lions, with a 22-yard punt return setting up the offense in Cardinal territory. His next return was not as far on the yardage, but also set the Lions up with the ball at midfield. Unfortunately, he was injured on the play. Kennedy did not return to the game.
LaPorta was the first player on the offense to wake up after an extremely slow first quarter, with the tight end recording 61 yards and a touchdown in the first half. His first catch of the game was on fourth down, giving the Lions their initial first down of the game.
The Iowa product would add a 38-yard scoring strike after the Cardinals got caught looking at a play action to Gibbs.
LaPorta was not done on the day, either, adding two more catches for 27 yards to finish as the leading receiver on the day with 88 yards.
Wonnum was part of the stout defensive unit that gave Jacoby Brissett and the Arizona offense fits. The first-year Lions defender had his second multi-sack game, taking down Brissett twice. On his second sack, it was a pure effort play. Wonnum got into the backfield for pressure, but was evaded.
The defensive end refused to call it a play and chased down Brissett for the sack.
Williams has had a solid start to the 2026 season, but was held out of the end zone in the receiving game. The former Lions first-round pick took that as a challenge, scoring in each half.
Both touchdowns were displays of Williams’ pure speed, with the wide receiver flying past his corner on a slant for the first and reeling in a deep shot on the latter.
Abney II has been in and out of the Lions lineup this season. This week, with Rock Ya-Sin out and Chrisitan Izien getting back to health, it was time for the Lions fifth-round draft selection to be in the lineup. Abney responded with a strong starting effort, and hauled in his first career interception on a desperation heave by Brissett to end the first half.
Gibbs had a lesser role than expected against Carolina, and that was not the case against Arizona. Sonic had 30 touches on the day, and topped 200 yards from scrimmage. The back was all over the field, showcasing his patience on multiple runs and cuts.
Gibbs saved his best play for last, cutting back across the entire defense on the goal line and out accelerating a corner for his second touchdown. That score also pushed him over 150 rushing yards for the day.
Goff had a highly efficient outing for Motown. After an extremely slow start, with the former top overall selection being sacked twice on his first two dropbacks, Goff responded with a four-touchdown game.
The Lions signal-caller threw for 271 yards and three scores, and added a sneak where Goff extended in the air for the score.
McNeill continued his strong start to the season with a half-sack on Sunday. The N.C. State product entered among the top 10 in the league in sacks, and it is clear that his dominant 2023 and 2024 form has returned.
McNeill was a difference-maker until his injury in 2024, and the 2025 season is a distant memory. With the half sack, McNeill has tied his 2024 total, which was achieved in 14 games.
On the second pass play of the game, Scruggs was completely blown off the ball by former Lions DT Roy Lopez. The former Texans offensive lineman stood no chance, and it was a bad rep that was part of a first quarter that saw Detroit finish in the negative for total yardage.
Reed found himself targeted more as the game wore on, with Roger McCreary putting in a strong effort of his own to dissuade Arizona from targeting him. The veteran was picked on, and it did not go well for Reed.
He allowed multiple first downs and catches to continue drives for the Cardinals.
Clark did not meet his standard on Sunday. In the second half, two of the big plays for the Cardinals offense, including a touchdown, came with Clark out of position. In both instances, the veteran defensive back threw his hands up in frustration. Perhaps it was a missed assignment by a teammate, but regardless, it was a bad look for a team leader .

title: Lions Provide Unfortunate Injury Updates on White, Kennedy
full_text:
While the Detroit Lions handled the Arizona Cardinals with ease Sunday afternoon, it was not all positive for Dan Campbell's squad in the desert.
It's because the Lions lost not just one but two players to game-ending injuries in their Week 5 tilt with the Cardinals.
Reports after the game indicated that Devin White left the locker room with his arm in a sling, while Tom Kennedy left on crutches with his right knee in a brace. Campbell provided grim updates on both players as far as their short-term status goes, with White expected to miss significant time.
"Doesn't look good. I think Devin's probably gonna need surgery, broken forearm," Campbell said. "It's unfortunate, I hate it because he was doing some good things for us this game. And then, TK, it doesn't look good as far as anything short-term. We'll know a lot more tomorrow. I think it could be a sprain, somewhere in there, a pretty good sprain. But neither one of them are gonna be around for a bit here, I hate that. Both players have done a really good job here."
White, who was active for the first time since Week 2, suffered a forearm injury in the final seconds of the first quarter. The game broadcast, televised on FOX, showed the veteran defender leaving the field on a cart, and he was later ruled out for the rest of the game.
Reserve linebackers Trevor Nowaske and Malcolm Rodriguez logged the majority of the snaps in place of White.
White, who was signed by the Lions less than a week into training camp this summer, has recorded 10 total tackles in three games with Detroit.
Then later in the first half, Kennedy suffered a knee ailment. It came on a 22-yard return in which his foot got caught in the State Farm Stadium turf and his right knee bent awkwardly.
"TK, I really thought hit it. We kind of challenged him on getting some of these returns. His first was outstanding," Campbell said. "His second one, he caught it and put his foot in the ground. He took it to heart, and I hate it for him that that happened. But, I don't think it's long, long-term. I think this is something that, we're gonna miss him for a little bit."
Initially, Kennedy was able to walk off the field on his own. However, after being examined in the blue tent, he was carted off to the locker room, and was eventually ruled out for the second half of the Week 5 matchup . He finished the contest with two punt returns for 33 yards.
The Lions are light on receiver depth, with only Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa and Tay Martin as the other options on the active roster. Detroit does have three receivers on the practice squad in Lawrence Keys, Lucky Jackson and Dominic Lovett.
St. Brown proceeded to replace Kennedy on punt return duties. He logged two punt returns in Kennedy's absence, amassing 36 yards, including 31 yards on his first return of the day.
Altogether, St. Brown compiled 105 all-purpose yards in the road victory for Detroit.
Next up for the Lions is their bye week, which will be followed by a pivotal NFC North matchup with the Green Bay Packers in Week 7.

title: Key Takeaways From Detroit Lions 45-21 Victory Over Arizona Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions entered Week 5 looking to get some much-needed momentum moving in their direction.
After a crushing loss to the Carolina Panthers evened their record at 2-2, the Lions traveled to State Farm Stadium looking to jump over the .500 mark ahead of their Week 6 bye.
Moving into their Week 5 matchup with Arizona, the Lions emphasized consistency after their performance fluctuated throughout the first four weeks.
"Yeah, any time you have a loss, you can't wait to get back to work and get back to the next game to get that taste out of your mouth," head coach Dan Campbell said in a pregame interview with Lions flagship radio. "At the end of the day, you've got to keep in mind that everything is about improvement, man. As much as you'd like to take these giant leaps, that's not how it works. The most important thing is the steady climb, and that's what we haven't done. We've done this teeter, this kind of roller-coaster. We've got to get out of that and begin to slowly climb every week and get better and better. It starts with Arizona."
Though they started slow, an emphatic second quarter resulted in a dominant 45-21 win for the Lions heading into the bye week. Here are takeaways from the team's win over Arizona.
The Lions elected to take the ball to start the game, but it was a non-ideal start. They went three-and-out, with the drive ending after Budda Baker blitzed untouched and sacked Goff on third-down.
Detroit's defense looked to have the Cardinals neutralized on their opening drive, forcing them into a third-and-11. However, Jacoby Brissett hit Kendrick Bourne for 22 yards to kickstart the drive.
Again, the Lions would force the Cardinals into a crucial situation as Brissett and company would face a fourth-and-1 from Detroit's 9-yard line. Rather than kick a field goal, Arizona dialed up some trickery as wide receiver Michael Wilson tossed the ball to Brissett after a reverse to pick up seven and a first-down.
Arizona would score on the next play, with Brissett hitting Teagan Quitoriano for a 2-yard touchdown to cap off the 14-play, 73-yard drive.
Detroit would go three-and-out on its ensuing drive, with former Lion Roy Lopez putting Detroit behind the sticks immediately with a sack of Jared Goff. They finished the first quarter with three three-and-outs, totaling negative-nine yards of offense in that timeframe.
While the Lions' offense struggled, the defense picked them up by forcing two straight punts to preserve the deficit at 7-0 through the end of the first quarter. After the second, the offense started to pick up steam.
Their momentum was sparked by a fourth-down conversion, as Goff hit Sam LaPorta for 12 yards and an additional 15 was tacked on thanks to a personal foul. After Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 15 yards with the help of his blockers, the Lions would call his number two more times and he reached paydirt to tie the game at 7-7 with 12:22 to go in the first half.
After stopping the Cardinals once again, the Lions caught a break when they were able to fall on a fumbled punt return by Amon-Ra St. Brown. Once again, they found themselves in a fourth-and-short after an unsuccessful challenge by Dan Campbell.
Once again, the Lions converted as Goff hit Sam LaPorta for a 38-yard touchdown. After a play-action fake, LaPorta snuck out wide open up the right sideline and strolled into the end zone to give the Lions the lead.
The defense came up big once again, forcing a three-and-out, and the Lions took advantage offensively. Once again, the Lions converted a pivotal fourth-down as they capped off their third scoring drive with a touchdown from Goff to Jameson Williams on fourth-and-4 from Arizona's 8-yard line.
Defensively, the Lions forced five-straight three-and-outs with D.J. Wonnum putting the exclamation point on the stretch with a third-down sack of Brissett. The Lions would tack on a 46-yard field goal from Jake Bates to take a 24-7 lead late in the first half.
Arizona was able to record a first-down on its final drive of the half, but another sack from Wonnum and the first career interception for Keith Abney II ended the half.
Wonnum with the third-down SACK pic.twitter.com/buiBiRTf7z
The Cardinals moved the ball quickly into Lions territory on their first drive of the second half, with Brissett connecting with Elijah Higgins for a 38-yard gain. However, Alim McNeill and Skyler Gill-Howard teamed up for a sack, and Chad Ryland's 53-yard field goal was no good.
Detroit's offense picked up right where they left off on the ensuing drive. Gibbs had a 10-yard run for a first-down, and then Tate Ratledge made a clutch fumble recovery after St. Brown lost the ball on a reception.
Facing a third-down, Goff dialed up a shot and connected with Jameson Williams on a 39-yard touchdown.
Jameson Williams TD! Second of day pic.twitter.com/lM0yP26n2E
Arizona would rally for their first points since their opening drive. Brissett rolled right and found Quitoriano for a 13-yard score, his second of the day, to make it 31-14 with 4:22 remaining in the third quarter.
However, the Lions snuffed out any momentum the Cardinals may have had by driving 74 yards in eight plays. They finished the drive out with yet another fourth-down conversion, this time a Jared Goff 1-yard quarterback sneak for a score. It was Goff's first rushing touchdown since the 2023 season.
The Lions have several players who logged significant accomplishments on Sunday. Most notably, running back Jahmyr Gibbs set an NFL record for the most touchdowns by a player under the age of 25 with his second rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter.
On a second-and-goal, Gibbs bounced off a tackle and reversed field, racing three yards into the end zone for the record-setting score. It capped off a 13-play, 79-yard drive and gave the Lions a 45-14 lead with five minutes remaining.
The Cardinals would punch in a late touchdown as Brissett hit Trey McBride, who made a terriffic juggling catch.
1.) Detroit Tigers play-by-play broadcaster Jason Benetti filled in as the Lions' play-by-play voice on the radio for Sunday's game. Dan Miller did not call the game after the passing of his wife, Cynthia .
"Our thoughts are with Dan right now, all weekend, and for the future, with the loss of his wife of 33 years, Cindy, a couple of days ago," Benetti said on Sunday's broadcast. "Dan is one of the most remarkable people I have met in my time in Detroit. One of the most sincere human beings you can possibly dream of. A fantastic voice of the Lions for more than two decades."
2.) Linebacker Devin White and wide receiver Tom Kennedy both suffered injuries in the first half. Both players did not return to the game. Amon-Ra St. Brown filled in for Tom Kennedy on punt return duties.
3.) Amon-Ra St. Brown made history on Sunday, passing Minnesota's Justin Jefferson for the most receiving yards in the first six seasons of a career.
4.) The 24 points the Lions scored in the second quarter were the most they've scored in a quarter since 2013.
5.) Wonnum set a new personal best with at least one sack in three-straight games.

title: Roundtable: Previewing Lions Week 5 Matchup Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Lions' Week 5 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.
1. How bad was the Kelvin Sheppard media session?
Christian Booher: I think the Sheppard press conference was one that he may look back upon and regret. To me, it just looked like he was unwilling to take some of the accountability for some of the struggles his defense has faced. Ultimately, when the group struggles, it falls on him as the coach, whether the calls were the correct ones or not.
Vito Chirco : It was catastrophically bad, and certainly didn't help out his case to remain the Lions’ defensive coordinator. The defense has been abysmal through the first quarter of the season, and his presser was nearly as bad. He likely needs the defense to come through with its best performance of the season in order to still have a job after the bye week.
Emmett Matasovsky: Personally, I see “bad” as a subjective term. From a fan’s perspective, it can definitely be viewed as an infuriating media session. However, if a defensive coordinator is going to back down due to the media or fans backseat play-calling, that coach likely is not fit for the role.
The statistics do not lie with Sheppard’s defense and the decision to blitz Bryce Young, but if a coach has made up their mind, there is a reason they went this far. Once again, I’ll circle back to my point that it can certainly be viewed as bad from a fan’s perspective.
2. Will the Lions be able to take advantage of Marvin Harrison Jr. not playing Sunday?
Booher : I still think the Lions will struggle against the Cardinals' passing game. Harrison is extremely talented, but for whatever reason it just hasn't worked out in Arizona. He'd caught just five passes all season leading up to this game, and while he's a big name, I don't think he's the biggest threat Detroit will be dealing with on Sunday.
Chirco : I believe so, to a certain extent. However, it's also important to note that Detroit will have its hands full trying to contain both Cardinals receiver Michael Wilson and tight end Trey McBride. So, while Harrison is out, Wilson and McBride are highly capable pass-catchers and will likely give the Lions’ secondary fits all Sunday afternoon. Subsequently, I still expect Detroit's defensive backs to experience their fair share of struggles vs. the Cardinals.
Matasovsky : Harrison Jr. being out is one less playmaker to worry about. That said, the Ohio State product is not showcasing his dominant form from college in the NFL. He is among the bottom of the league in separation.
However, if the Cardinals kept trotting him out, that implied either they had not given up on him, or he is better than the others in the organization. Sunday will help us find that out.
3. Will the Lions’ offense step up and score 35 points this week?
Booher : That's a lot to ask out of an offense to do week after week. They certainly have the talent to do it, but it's a lot to ask for a group to have to play at that level every single game. I think Drew Petzing will have some unique looks dialed up for his former team, but ultimately I think they come up just short of the 35-point threshold.
Chirco : I'm going to say no this week. Although Arizona hardly possesses a vaunted defense (29th in points allowed), I believe that Detroit's success on offense is going to run out a tad in this Week 5 contest. I still expect Lions signal-caller Jared Goff to have his fair share of success through the air. I just don't expect Drew Petzing's unit to produce 30-plus points.
Matasovsky : My prediction has Detroit with 37 points, so I will stick with yes, they will. The Cardinals have not been great so far, allowing nearly 27 points per game on average. The Lions' offense is highly potent.
The only way I see a drop-off is if the Lions struggle with a West Coast trip. Personally, I do not see that happening.
4. Is the bye week coming at the right time for the Lions?
Booher : I think so. Not only does it give them an extra week to get two important players back in Cade Mays and Brian Branch, but it also gives them a bit of a reprieve after having to deal with a lot of criticism over the first four weeks. If the defense struggles again Sunday, that noise will only get louder.
Detroit still has plenty to play for and the ability to contend and challenge for a division title, but I think having the bye week before starting their divisional slate will ultimately be beneficial for them.
Chirco : Yes. The defense needs to recalibrate and get back on track in the worst way, and hopefully the bye week will allow Detroit to do just that. Also, hopefully the Lions will get back a healthy and productive Brian Branch after the bye. That would definitely go a long way toward the defense improving its play.
Matasovsky : Considering the mounting injuries and the hope of Brian Branch returning to practice, yes. Considering the brutal international trip facing them, no.
Essentially, this is a short-term gain for the Lions to rest up and recover from some of their “next man up” defense. However, judgement on it will be reserved until two weeks after Munich.
5. Who will be the Lions' MVP on Sunday?
Booher : I think the Lions' MVP on Sunday will be Aidan Hutchinson. Hutchinson has been quiet for most of the last two games after a fast start to the season, and against a veteran in Jacoby Brissett who struggles against the blitz he could have a field day.
Chirco : I believe it will be Aidan Hutchinson. With the Cardinals’ injuries on the offensive line, I believe that the superstar EDGE will be able to wreak havoc against Jacoby Brissett all afternoon. And that should prove to be one of the difference-makers for Detroit in this Week 5 matchup.
Matasovsky : I do not see anyone slowing down Jahmyr Gibbs from getting his yards on Sunday. Gibbs will be the MVP with a 200-total yard performance. He had a less impactful outing than expected against Carolina, and I see that flipping around into a revenge game in the desert.

title: Lions Week 5 Inactives: Is First-Round DT Playing Against Cardinals?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have revealed their inactive players for their Week 5 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.
Entering Sunday, the Lions had already ruled four players inactive. Two of those players have not yet been added onto the active roster, as Brian Branch (Achilles) and Cade Mays (Wrist) both began their return to play windows this week after beginning the year on Physically Unable to Perform and Injured Reserve, respectively.
After Sunday's game, the Lions have their bye week before returning to action with a game against Green Bay in Week 7. Branch and Mays could both be on track to return for that game.
Players ruled inactive on Sunday include cornerback Rock Ya-Sin and offensive lineman Ben Bartch, who were both ruled out on the team's final injury report Friday with hamstring and foot injuries. For Bartch, it is the third consecutive week he's been ruled out.
Defensive tackle Tyleik Williams , who was ruled questionable on Friday with a foot injury after not practicing Wednesday and being limited on Thursday and Friday, is officially active and expected to start against the Cardinals.
Because the Lions only elevated one player, safety Jalen Mills, to the active roster from the practice squad this week, they needed to make four other players inactive. Those players include defensive linemen Ahmed Hassanein and Mekhi Wingo, tight end Jackson Meeks and safety Bishop Fitzgerald.
White is active after being marked as an inactive for the previous two weeks. He had played a starting role early in the season, but was demoted in favor of 2026 fourth-round pick Jimmy Rolder in recent weeks.
Signed in training camp after Rolder suffered an injury, White had a strong camp and impressed the coaches with his ability. However, after recording a total of nine tackles in the first two games, White appeared to fall out of the rotation.
Fitzgerald still has yet to make his Lions debut after the team signed him off the Pittsburgh Steelers' practice squad earlier in the season. He was signed after Avonte Maddox's season-ending injury in Week 2, but has yet to suit up for Detroit since arriving.
Tyler Conklin is also returning to the lineup after a two-week absence, as Meeks is out after playing a bigger role in that span.

title: Cynthia Miller, Wife of Detroit Lions Play-by-Play Voice Dan Miller, Dies
full_text:
Detroit Lions play-by-play voice Dan Miller has lost his beloved wife, Cynthia Miller, who passed away on October 10, 2026.
According to Griffin Funeral Home , "Cynthia ‘Cindy‘ Louise Miller, born on October 3, 1963, in Falls Church, Virginia, to Roy and the late Valerie (Weber) Biondi, was a woman whose magnetic personality, infectious humor, and welcoming spirit made everyone feel like family. Cindy was the beloved wife of Dan Miller, with whom she shared 33 wonderful years of marriage. She was the devoted and fiercely loving mother of Sammi (Brendan) Burdette, Rikki Miller, Tony (Viona Veseli) Miller, and Robbie Miller, and the adoring grandmother of Daphne and Cecilia. She was the dear sister of Gino (Lisa) Biondi, Steve (Marissa) Biondi, and Julie (Chris) Griffin."
Cindy was passionate about the Detroit Lions. She attended each and every home game, sitting in the fifth row right behind the Lions bench.
"Some of her best memories were attending the two home playoff games with her daughters in 2024. Her family knows that she will be there in spirit when the Lions win it all."
A memorial gathering for Cindy will be held on Friday, October 16, from 3 p.m. until 6 p.m. at the L.J. Griffin Funeral Home, Northrop-Sassaman Chapel, on 19091 Northville Road (at 7 Mile Road). A funeral service celebrating Cindy's life will follow at 6 p.m.
Dan Miller has become one of the staples of broadcasting in the region, as he is one of the most popular play-by-play voices covering the National Football League.
He shared in a Social House News feature the passion his wife Cynthia and his children had for the Lions.
"My wife loves football (Cindy attends all Lions games), my kids love football," Dan expressed. "When I'd have a Saturday off in the fall, my daughters would come downstairs and ask, 'What college football games are on today? We'd sit around the TV, they'd have their computers on their lap and we'd watch games. When the noon games were about to end, they'd ask, 'What games are on at 3:30?' It was heaven for me."
Cynthia Miller battled Leptomeningeal disease.
The entire staff of Detroit Sports Podcast and Lions On SI sends its deepest condolences to the Miller family during this time of grief and sorrow.

title: Detroit Lions Week 5 Updated Depth Chart Against Cardinals
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are set to battle the Arizona Cardinals with a chance to get back over .500 ahead of their bye week.
Detroit is coming off a tough loss to the Carolina Panthers and has started the season 0-2 on the road. Against the 1-3 Cardinals, Dan Campbell's team has a chance to get some mojo with a road win. However, it won't be easy as the Cardinals have weapons that could be difficult for Detroit's defense to contain.
Here's an updated look at the Lions' depth chart for their matchup against the Cardinals.
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Joshua Dobbs.
Goff has been effective throughout the season and remains without a turnover. He ranks third in passing yards, behind Dak Prescott who played on Thursday and Bryce Young. He's also one of only three starters who have played in all four games to have not thrown an interception.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Sione Vaki. Reserve: Jacob Saylors. Inactive: Isiah Pacheco (Injured reserve).
Gibbs continues to be the dominant force in the backfield, with Vaki taking a majority of the reps when he's out of the game. Vaki has shown some improvements in pass-protection since the start of the year, and as a result has been continuing to earn more trust and opportunities.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: Tom Kennedy, Tay Martin. Inactive: Kendrick Law (Injured reserve).
Williams and TeSlaa are both coming up big for Detroit's passing game after slow starts, with TeSlaa coming off a career-best performance last week. The team continues to heavily lean on St. Brown, who ranks fourth in the league in receptions through four weeks.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserve: Jackson Meeks, Tyler Conklin
Even with the questions surrounding his future, LaPorta is off to a solid start early in the year. The Iowa product had a touchdown grab against the Panthers, and is up to 22 catches through four games. Wright is coming off a rough showing in which he received a fine and was penalized twice.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backup: Larry Borom Inactive: Gio Manu (Non-football injury)
The Lions have been able to maintain some stability up front with Sewell and Miller staying healthy to play their third consecutive game together. Miller continues to improve in his rookie season, while Sewell has maintained his reputation as one of the best tackles in the league.
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backup: Miles Frazier. Inactive: Ben Bartch (Out, Foot).
Bartch is sidelined for the third straight game with a foot injury, meaning Mahogany stays unchallenged at the left guard position as the competition simply hasn't materialized the way Campbell hoped it would. Ratledge has been solid up to this point on the right side.
Starter: Juice Scruggs. Backup: Seth McLaughlin. Reserve: Tate Ratledge. Inactive: Cade Mays (Out, Wrist).
A big development occurred earlier in the week with Cade Mays returning to practice. He won't play this week, but could return after the bye which would make things interesting for Scruggs. The veteran has been reliable at center, and could slide into a starting role at left guard or at the least provide valuable depth.
Starters: Tyleik Williams (Questionable, Foot), Alim McNeill. Backups: Skyler Gill-Howard, Levi Onwuzurike. Reserve: Mekhi Wingo.
Williams is listed as questionable but told reporters that he plans to play against the Cardinals. McNeill is coming off another big game in which he logged his third sack of the season, putting him well ahead of a career-high pace.
Starters: Aidan Hutchinson, D.J. Wonnum. Backups: Tyler Lacy, Derrick Moore. Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Ahmed Hassanein. Inactive: Payton Turner (Injured reserve).
Starters: Jack Campbell, Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez. Backups: Trevor Nowaske, Jimmy Rolder, Amen Ogbongbemiga Reserve: Devin White. Inactive: Damone Clark (Injured reserve).
The Lions have gone away from White after he played a starter role the first two weeks of the season, which also correlates with Rolder's increased role. Ultimately, the Lions appear to be comfortable utilizing the young option along with the athletic Nowaske in certain situations.
Starters: D.J. Reed, Roger McCreary. Backups: Ennis Rakestraw Jr., Keith Abney. Reserves: Khalil Dorsey. Inactive: Rock Ya-Sin (Out, Hamstring).
Ya-Sin has been ruled out, which seems to solidify either McCreary or Rakestraw getting another start. Of the two, Rakestraw has seemingly been better by a small margin and has positive moments including a pass breakup last week. Abney could see an increased role as well, be it at cornerback or safety.
The Lions won't have to worry about Marvin Harrison Jr ., who will be inactive with the anticipation of being traded early next week.
Starters: Chuck Clark, Christian Izien. Backups: Jalen Mills (Practice squad elevation), Bishop Fitzgerald. Inactive: Brian Branch (Out, Achilles), Kerby Joseph (PUP), Avonte Maddox (Injured reserve), Thomas Harper (Injured reserve).
Clark and Izien are both veteran presences who have had good moments, with Izien looking like one of Detroit's best offseason additions. Mills was called up from the practice squad for the third and final time, which means the team will have to decide whether or not to add him to the active roster moving forward.
Branch returned to practice and could be in line to return after the bye, which could make Mills and even potentially Fitzgerald expendable. Fitzgerald has yet to be active in a game since being poached off of the Steelers' practice squad.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten. Kick returners: Tom Kennedy, Jacob Saylors. Punt returner: Tom Kennedy.
The Lions have yet to make any changes to their special teams units through four weeks. Bates remains perfect on field goal and extra point attempts.
