title: Will the Chiefs' Offensive Line Stabilize After the Bye Week?
full_text:
In some instances, an early Week 5 bye could be an unwelcome arrival for an NFL team, particularly for an undefeated squad with the type of momentum that only comes with four consecutive wins. For the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs, however, it might be exactly the right time for the sake of their uncertain offensive line.
While we use this bye week to evaluate a few key position groups for the current No. 1 seed in the AFC, you may not expect too much concern for the only unbeaten team in the conference.
Still, offensive line uncertainty has been one of the defining storylines of the Chiefs' strong start. How will the group come together after the bye week? That's the team's biggest issue to solve before they host the Los Angeles Chargers on October 18.
Starting left tackle Josh Simmons has missed the first four games of the season with a bulging disc, an injury the team only publicly defined on September 30 . Starting left guard Kingsley Suamataia was benched for the Chiefs' Week 4 showdown against the Las Vegas Raiders, reportedly due to a " coaching decision ."
Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has held up at left tackle in Simmons' absence, while veteran backup Mike Caliendo got the left guard reps in Las Vegas. Right tackle Jaylon Moore has had his ups and downs, leaving an interesting question for the Chiefs to answer— Benson or Moore at right tackle? —when Simmons returns.
Even All-Pro center Creed Humphrey has had some issues to begin the year, tossing some bad snaps and starting the year on pace to have career-low grades from Pro Football Focus .
To be fair, across an array of offensive line metrics , evaluation of the Chiefs' performance varies —a frequent phenomenon due to the variety of often-subjective ways O-lines are evaluated . Still, with such uncertainty at left tackle, it's seemed apparent that the unit has not yet fully gelled to be as solid as the sum of its parts.
Pass block grade of offensive linemen in true pass sets only Mahomes/Trevor good What happened to the Broncos' OL?? pic.twitter.com/DQCqy3lTpE
The Chiefs bolstered their depth on the O-line just before roster cutdowns, trading for veteran lineman Joshua Ezeudu from the New York Giants and undrafted rookie tackle Diego Pounds from the Baltimore Ravens.
Ezeudu has taken five offensive snaps for the Chiefs, while Pounds has been inactive through the Chiefs' first four games. Pounds remains an intriguing developmental tackle prospect, but his future on the field appears to be some time away. Ezeudu is on a one-year deal and provides short-term versatility at guard or tackle, though either Benson or Moore would clearly be the team's backup swing tackle when Simmons returns.

title: Chiefs Rookie and Sophomore Power Rankings: Assessing the Landscape at Bye Week
full_text:
Somehow, we're simultaneously about a month through the 2026 NFL season already but still have several months to go before we truly find out who some teams are. Don't get it twisted — multiple pretenders have already managed to stand out, but the cream of the crop won't be made obvious for quite some time.
Sitting at 4-0 on the year, the Kansas City Chiefs' hope is for them to be categorized as the latter once the postseason rolls around. That'll take continued impact from general manager Brett Veach's rookie and sophomore classes, which have presented both positive and negative value to this point.
At the bye week, let's break down the Chiefs' rookies and sophomores by ranking each 53-man roster member in tiers. Be sure to return to this series each week to see who's moving and shaking.
Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott isn't included due to him currently being on the physically unable to perform list .
There's no derailing the Nohl Williams hype train, even after an afternoon and evening in which the second-year cornerback got flagged for a pair of costly penalties . He remains a promising young building block in the secondary, forming a two-man show with rookie Mansoor Delane that could terrorize opposing offenses for years to come.
Second-round pick R Mason Thomas has bounced back from some rough moments in the last couple of weeks, flashing rare bend and quickness as a pass rusher on the outside. According to Pro Football Focus , he set a new career high with five Week 4 pressures. Late first-rounder Peter Woods may have just turned in his worst performance to date, although the interior lineman was also reportedly banged up at some point in the contest.
The real X-factor here might be Day 3 running back Emmett Johnson. While he earned a respectable 16 offensive snaps on Sunday, he only got one touch. Perhaps if Kenneth Walker III's workload dwindles a bit coming out of the bye, the Nebraska product will get his time to shine .
With left tackle Josh Simmons still working his way through a back injury , the Kahlil Benson roller coaster keeps on running in Kansas City. His level of play has undoubtedly slipped, but he was surprisingly fine in Week 4 considering he had a fill-in next to him at left guard and, per TruMedia , the Chiefs trailed only the Houston Texans in throws relative to the sticks on average.
An ankle dislocation for wideout Tyquan Thornton might just earn sophomore Jalen Royals some more snaps, but only if an external acquisition isn't made and the coaching staff deems the former Utah State standout worthy of the reps. Another member of the 2025 NFL Draft class, defensive end Ashton Gillotte has received more than a 40% workload share in three consecutive weeks and had a season-high three quarterback hurries in his last performance.
Bryson Eason , as promised, finds himself getting bumped up after being activated for the second week in a row. He could just as easily come back down given the restrictions capping him at three practice squad elevations per season. For now, he's worth keeping an eye on.
The only people who truly know when Simmons is coming back seem to be Simmons himself and those within the building at 1 Arrowhead Drive. Heck, there may not even be a solidified plan. Kansas City certainly hasn't done itself many favors with how it's handled the injury situation to one of its more polarizing youngsters, but all it'd take is a post-bye return for just about everyone to probably sweep that under the rug.
Late-round draft selection Cyrus Allen was the flavor of the summer in Chiefs circles; the Thornton injury will bring that buzz back around for the fall. Elsewhere on offense, tight end Jake Briningstool is still an occasional sighting on the field. Running back Brashard Smith is a special-teamer through and through . Barring injury, cornerback Jadon Canady is stuck in the same boat.
This is where things get a little interesting. Linebacker Jeffrey Bassa isn't in the huddle much on defense, but could forcing a fumble on special teams be the launching pad he needs for an increased overall role? Undrafted free agent Xavier Nwankpa helped seal the deal against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 4 by picking off a pass on his only defensive snap. It doesn't get much more efficient than that.
Nothing much to see here, truthfully. Both tackle Diego Pounds and defensive end Jack Pyburn have made routine appearances on the game-day inactives list in recent weeks. Seventh-round quarterback Garrett Nussmeier always carries an outside shot to get on the field, although it'd take a catastrophic stretch of injuries to both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields for that to happen as the emergency third signal-caller.

title: Kenneth Walker Has Been Incredible, But Emmett Johnson's Time May Be Coming Soon
full_text:
Through the first four games of the 2026 NFL season, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker has been one of the best players in all of football and is firmly on track to be in the Offensive Player of the Year conversation in his first campaign with the Chiefs.
The only downside of Walker's 2026 so far? He's taken a whopping 99 touches through four games, putting him on pace for 420 touches this season. During his four years with the Seattle Seahawks, Walker recorded 255, 248, 199 and 252 regular season touches, respectively. It's still a compliment to note that Walker has been too dominant to take off the field, but with a long-term view of the Chiefs' season, another back will need to spell Walker at some point.
During the Chiefs' bye week, we'll be taking a closer look at a few key position groups to see how they've stacked up to preseason expectations and where they could improve after the bye. However, for the Chiefs' running backs, "improvement" seems almost impossible.
Walker has been darn near perfect through four games, and his impact on the Chiefs' offense has been remarkably evident. From his ability to be the "easy button" for Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes to his home run-hitting ability out of the backfield , Walker has exceeded even the most optimistic offseason expectations. Now, can the Chiefs keep Walker fresh enough to stay that consistent late into the year?
Outside of Kansas City, rookie fifth-round pick Emmett Johnson may be flying under the radar. He has 16 carries for 56 yards and five catches for 74—not quite enough to be added in most fantasy football leagues. However, Johnson's highlights have been about as impressive as anyone's.
Emmett Johnson has some MOVES 😮‍💨 (via @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/yEWu90SL7G
Even while currently standing in Walker's shadow, I'm confident that Johnson would have been the best running back in KC's 2025 backfield, and probably by a large margin.
Emmett Johnson is 1 of 5 RBs with 10+ missed tackles forced (MTFs) The 4 other RBs have 40+ touches each. Emmett Johnson has 10 MTFs on just 14 touches. Absurd.
Through four games, Walker has taken 75% of the Chiefs' offensive snaps (196) while Johnson has taken 26% (69). That's the 13th-most offensive snaps on the team for Johnson, and his role should only grow from there.
As long as Johnson is trusted by the coaching staff—and if he wasn't, I don't think the team would have parted ways with Emari Demercado during roster cuts—his workload should increase during the Chiefs' midseason grind as the team tries to spare Walker from a few hits while trying to keep him in top form for a postseason run similar to what he did for the Seahawks en route to his Super Bowl MVP award in February.
Even without significant statistical output so far, Johnson is dynamic enough that Walker can leave the field without allowing opposing defenses to let their guard down on the running game.
The only potential "negative" for the Chiefs' running back room so far would come in the evaluation of second-year seventh-round pick Brashard Smith. (Even then, "negative" is probably too strong.) Smith has taken only six offensive snaps this season, catching one pass but taking zero carries.
The optimistic case for Smith is that he's firmly behind one superstar back and one extremely promising rookie. On the other hand, Smith saw the field sparingly last season, recording just 44 carries (with 26 coming in the team's two games against the Las Vegas Raiders) in 2025. Smith's speed is still a unique enough trait that he should be worth keeping an eye on as the season unfolds, but he's more of a special teamer and injury insurance until further notice.

title: Chargers Trade Deadline Big Board:  Realistic Targets and Trade Assets
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers season has been an absolute disappointment given the expectations heading into the season. The Chargers have shot themselves in the foot nearly every week with questionable in-game decisions, poor preparation and injuries have mounted.
Los Angeles dropped their fifth straight game to hand the 2026 Chargers the worst start for the franchise since the 2000 season. They took on the Denver Broncos in week five with a severely depleted roster and ended up starting four rookie offensive linemen.
The Chargers roster had several questionable holes and depth entering the season and most of those questions have become problems to one degree or another. Looking forward to the trade deadline, is it realistic that a team staring down the barrel of potentially the worst season in franchise history would be buyers? No, they definitely wont be looking for mega deals or franchise-altering additions. However, simple trades for players on expiring contracts that could be potential free agent targets in the offseason may be worth lat-round considerations.
The Chargers are poised to be sellers at the trade deadline. Despite mounting injuries, the Chargers do have several strong position groups and may be able to get draft compensation for certain players. Most NFL trade deadlines come and go quietly, the Chargers likely wont conduct a fire sale but a handful of players could finish their 2026 seasons elsewhere.
The Chargers are likely to deal Khalil Mack to his destination of choice. Los Angeles will still have Tuli Tuipulotu and rookie Akheem Mesidor but behind them is veteran Bud Dupree and practice squad edge rushers. For the rest of this season and for the future, edge depth will be needed.
Former UDFA from the Kansas City Chiefs Malik Herring started the season with the Titans and made his way to the Dolphins where he has been playing significant rotational snaps. More importantly, Herring's pass rush productivity rate is higher than Bud Dupree and has graded out significantly higher as a run defender.
The Chargers could use him if Khalil Mack is gone and potentially get an early look at a potential long-term depth piece. Herring likely would not cost more than a late-round pick swap.
The Chargers already have one weapons grade ginger in Scott Matlock, why not add another? Ko Kieft is listed as a tight end but operates much more as a fullback. He can be trusted to handle defensive ends and edge rushers one-on-one and will clear holes for running backs.
Kieft missed most of 2025 with a broken leg and returned to Tampa Bay this past offseason but has not been getting snaps when healthy. Kieft is a savage blocker and could immediately help in many formations and uses.
TE Ko Kieft (41) is here to kick ass and chew bubble bum...and he's all out of gum. https://t.co/Okw3he3x3N pic.twitter.com/YEf7z6CF8b
Kieft may be redundant with Matlock and  Alec Ingold on the roster but Matlock is on an expiring contract and Ingold has not been playing particularly well and the Chargers have been cycling through tight ends so far this year. If the Chargers plan to deploy a fullback in 2027, it would be great to get a look at another option before free agency. Kieft would likely not cost more than a late Day 3 pick.
It is no secret at this point that there are trade rumors around Khalil Mack. He deserves to go wherever he wants to go to compete for a contender. He can still provide leadership and be a productive edge for a team in need. The Chargers will likely net an early to mid day three pick for Mack.
It would be hard to see homegrown local linebacker Daiyan Henley leave the franchise but he is on an expiring deal and the Chargers have young linebackers ready for playing time alongside several veterans. Henley still boasts speed and coverage skills who could help a team in need. He would also likely net a mid day three pick.

title: Jim Harbaugh’s Damning Quote After Chargers Fall to 0-5 Signals Total Crisis in LA
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have now fallen to 0-5 to begin the 2026 NFL season, a season where they were supposed to be one of the Super Bowl frontrunners. A season where the exciting hiring of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was supposed to finally give Justin Herbert an environment conducive to success. A season where new hire Chris O'Leary was supposed to continue the elite defensive ecosystem left by now-Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter.
The fact of the matter is that this team is in complete shambles and their leader, Jim Harbaugh, is now running out of answers to be able to help this team fight for competency in the National Football League.
Harbaugh, known for quirky catchphrases and toughness that is infectious through football locker rooms, is seemingly out of, to quote one of those aforementioned catchphrases, "an enthusiasm unknown to mankind."
In the most recent post-game press conference after the Denver Broncos took a 23-17 victory over the Bolts in Week 5, Harbaugh was asked about the message for the team after now being 0-5. He responded with: "Yeah, I don't know what that message is."
Chargers HC Jim Harbaugh on message to the team at 0-5: "Yeah, I don't know what that message is.
An obviously damning statement from the "CEO" head coach who is supposed to be known for his leadership and mentality. He does follow up that statement with a generic motivational comment: " It's just in the players to just fight their hearts out, to play, give it everything they have. That's the only way. That's the best way."
The entire press conference exchange is another shake to what is the Chargers' crumbling foundation. While it was shut down, there have already been talks of Mike McDaniel being fired , with that hot seat seemingly spreading to Jim Harbaugh. Simply put, the team is desperate for answers, and their leader has none.
Even with the hot seat beginning to heat up, it should be noted that Harbaugh's ability to motivate is highly respected throughout league circles, with former Chargers general manager Tom Telesco recently commenting on Daniel Jeremiah's podcast, Move the Sticks , "If you didn't have a head coach right now and you're like, 'We need someone to help us get out of this [the 0-4 start],' it'd probably be Jim Harbaugh." This belief is likely shared within the Chargers front office, making the Harbaugh exit as the Bolts' head coach a much longer wait than if he were someone else.

title: Chargers Stock Report: Three Players Rising and Two Falling After Week 5
full_text:
While the entire Los Angeles Chargers team is lacking any sort of excitement or hope for the team's chances of doing damage later in the season, it is still reasonable to look at some guys on the roster who may be impactful in the future or guys who will not stick around as they are not performing up to expectations.
Kimani Vidal was arguably the lone bright spot of the Chargers offense in Week 5. The team was down their top five wide receivers and was down to nearly an entire backup offensive line. Vidal, as the team's third RB, had an electric run that gave the Chargers one of their only highlights of the entire season.
Vidal had eight carries for 57 yards and a touchdown, coupled with a few nice blocks on Herbert scrambles, continuing to grow his trust in this offense.
Oronde Gadsden II is a talented tight end who has shown plenty of promise in his rookie season, but in Year 2, he has looked like a completely different player. He is not featured in the offense and is not someone who is seemingly making the same plays as before.
He is falling on this team, as he had one target for this entire game, even with the Chargers missing the majority of their receiver room.
Charlie Kolar returned in Week 5 after missing a few games with a forearm injury, making his impact known early. He made an impressive catch-and-run...that ended in a fumble. Which is obviously not a great look, but outside of this error, he helped the Chargers' running attack, making key blocks on the first and second levels of the defense. Kolar was the team's leading receiver with three catches for 37 yards.
Keaton Mitchell is still featured heavily in this Bolts' offense, garnering six carries for 11 yards and three receptions for 18 yards. While Mitchell has shown promise as a receiver, he has yet to have an elite chunk-run play, showing why the Chargers went out specifically to add him to their roster. His 1.8 yards per carry is simply not enough.
The final name on this list is Akheem Mesidor , the Chargers first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Mesidor has played well in his role as the team's EDGE3. He has shown immense effort and skill, collecting another sack and forced fumble in Week 5. He also led the team in tackles with eight. Look for Mesidor to continue rising, giving the team at least one player to build around for the 2027 NFL season.

title: Predicting Chargers' Starters vs Broncos for NFL Week 5: Is There Anyone Left Alive?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-4, banged up and are already plugging roster holes with practice squad elevations and free agents off the street... it is only Week 5. They welcome in their division rivals the Denver Broncos to SoFi Stadium in week five with the hopes to snag their first win of the season.
The Chargers' 2026 season is barely breathing. The anemic offense showed signs of life in the second half against the Seahawks in week four. There is a path forward for them to save their season but any hope has to start with getting a win over the Broncos. It will be a tall task with their injuries.
Quarterback: Justin Herbert Running back: Omarion Hampton Fullback: Alec Ingold Tight end: Oronde Gadsden II Wide receiver: Tre' Harris Wide receiver: Marquez Valdez-Scantling Left tackle: Branson Taylor Left guard: Logan Taylor (R) Center: Jake Slaughter (R) Right guard: Cole Strange Right tackle: Travis Burke (R)
The Chargers will be sending out a makeshift offensive unit of backups and new roster additions to face off against the Denver Broncos. Los Angeles lost four of their starters on offense against the Seattle Seahawks including left tackle Rashawn Slater who just underwent tight-rope surgery to help a high ankle sprain heal.
Right tackle Joe Alt is also out of this game as is wide receiver Quentin Johnston who suffered a chest injury, likely on a 44 yard reception where he leaped into the air and took a free fall and landed flat on his back. Left guard Trevor Penning, who already was the Chargers' fifth option at left guard since training camp, was placed on injured reserve as well.
Second-year offensive lineman Branson Taylor will make his 2026 debut against Denver after being sidelined for the first four weeks after suffering an injury in the preseason and was placed on IR to start the season. In addition to the return of Taylor, veteran Daniel Brunskill was signed to the practice squad earlier this week and he was elevated for the game despite being with the team only a few days. He has experience at all five positions but has the majority of his career snaps at right guard and center.

title: Jerry Jeudy Trade Rumors Heating Up: Chargers Should Target Browns Receiver
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers should be looking at every possible way to improve their offense, and Jerry Jeudy is a name worth considering. The Cleveland Browns receiver has become a subject of trade speculation, creating a potential opportunity to add another weapon for Justin Herbert.
NFL insider Adam Shefter revealed that Juedy could possibly be up for grabs at the trade deadline.
Sometimes, finding a player who needs a fresh start can be just as valuable as bringing in an established star. Jeudy has already shown that he can be productive in the NFL. The question is whether he can return to that level of play and become a more consistent part of an offense.
For a Chargers team looking for ways to get more out of its passing game, that is something worth investigating.
One of the biggest advantages of having a quarterback like Herbert is the ability to attack defenses in different ways. He can make difficult throws, push the ball downfield and give his receivers opportunities to make plays. But even a talented quarterback can benefit from having more options available when a defense takes away his first read.
That is where Jeudy could become an interesting addition.
The receiver recorded 1,229 receiving yards during the 2024 season with Cleveland, proving that he is capable of producing big numbers. His production fell to 602 yards in 2025, and he has gotten off to a quiet start this season. The coaching staff would have to determine how Jeudy fits into the existing offense. Also, how many opportunities he could realistically receive and whether he would improve the team’s current group of receivers.
That is why the asking price should be a major factor. If Cleveland demands a significant draft pick, Los Angeles should carefully consider whether the potential reward justifies the investment. If the Browns are willing to negotiate a more affordable deal, the conversation becomes much more interesting. We all should have some what of an idea what he is worth, which in my opinion it’s totally worth it.
His recent production shows that there are legitimate concerns, and the Chargers would need to be comfortable accepting that risk. Still, the potential upside deserves attention. Jeudy is not an unproven prospect who has never demonstrated what he can do at the professional level.
Ladd McConkey seems to be the only bright spot to this core, based on the last four games. Bringing in another playmaker could elevate the others purley based on competition. The bottom line is simply that the Chargers need help, and this could potentially be a perfect fit.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: Does the Losing Cycle Finally End Against the Broncos?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers need a win that gives analysts and fans a reason to believe again.
Obviously potential has never been the only question surrounding this team. The bigger concern is whether the Bolts can put everything together when it matters most. Sunday’s divisional matchup against the Denver Broncos gives them another opportunity to prove they can compete.
Of course no divisional matchup is ever taken lightly, so there is always pressure when two AFC West rivals meet. Especially when a team is trying to change the direction of its season.
Denver will not make things easy. They have their own reasons to take advantage of this matchup. These type of games often come down to execution, discipline, and which team makes the fewest mistakes when the pressure starts building.
The image of Justin Herbert trying to escape Denver’s pass rush tells an important part of the story. The Chargers have a quarterback capable of making difficult throws and extending plays, but there is only so much one player can do when the opposition consistently disrupts the offense.
Herbert’s ability is not the issue. The challenge is giving him enough time and support to operate effectively. When defenders get into the backfield before routes develop, even a quarterback with his arm talent can find himself fighting an uphill battle.
The Bolts need to establish better offensive rhythm and avoid putting their quarterback in situations where every possession requires something extraordinary.
At the same time, Herbert has to remain patient. Not every play needs to become a highlight, and forcing a difficult throw can turn a promising drive into a wasted opportunity. The best version of this offense is one where he can make an impact without feeling like the entire game rests on his shoulders. That responsibility also falls on the coaching staff and the rest of the roster. They need their running game, protection, and playmakers to contribute. If the offense becomes too predictable, that elite defense will have more opportunities to dictate the pace.
Defensively, they must find a way to make life uncomfortable for Bo Nix without giving away easy opportunities. Winning third downs, limiting explosive plays, and creating pressure at the right moments could make a significant difference. The team cannot afford to spend the entire afternoon trying to recover from mistakes.
According to NFL senior insider Adam Schefter, Sean Payton will see an increase in play-calling moving forward. Which makes things for the defense way more complicated.
My biggest concern heading into this matchup is consistency. The Bolts need to demonstrate that they can respond when things do not go according to plan. Every team looks capable when the offense is moving and the defense is making stops. The real question is what happens after a turnover, a stalled drive, or an opponent’s scoring run.
That is when a team shows its character.
The Broncos are a serious divisional test, and the Bolts need to treat them accordingly. If they can put together a complete performance, it has a chance to change the conversation. Until then, questions about consistency will continue to follow this team.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Paint a Khalil Mack Bears Trade at Good Price for Chargers
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers sit 0-4 with an injury disaster on their hands ahead of what could be an 0-6 mark by the bye week.
Understandably, it’s time to talk about doing right by Khalil Mack and trading him .
Not a fun topic for Chargers fans. But given the state of things and the fact Mack might be on his final season in the NFL, most probably accept it by now.
Naturally, of the likely Mack trade landing spots , the Chicago Bears are by far the most sensible.
And if a rumor that suggests the asking price on a Mack trade is true, the Chargers might as well go ahead and do it.
The Chargers don’t have much leverage in a Mack trade. They’re bad and he’s older, so even desperate teams won’t cough up too much.
That tracks with new buzz from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones , who spoke with a general manager and one assistant general manager in the NFL who pinned Mack’s trade value at about roughly a fifth-round pick.
Jones added this: “But Khalil Mack to Chicago is something multiple league sources told me makes the most sense if both teams continue on their respective trajectories.”
For the Chargers…might as well. They’re asking a team to take on about $5 million in remaining contract with Mack if he gets moved this week or next, too.
The Chargers probably aren’t going to find a sell-high moment better than this with Mack. He’s playing really good ball right now amid the chaos. And to their credit, the Chargers front office is pretty good at finding hits in the fifth round like Oronde Gadsden, Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart in recent years.
If the Chargers keep losing, the focus needs to shift to the future, anyway. Tuli Tuipulotu is the new heart of the pass-rush for the long-term and needs a new contract, while Akheem Mesidor is a first-round rookie who could use all the developmental snaps.
Again, not a super-fun topic for Chargers fans. But gently blowing up the roster (before potentially the coaching staff too) means selling off what they can and investing heavily in things beyond this season.
That includes Mack, who deserves a chance to go compete for a Super Bowl somewhere.

title: Sunday Morning Rams Notebook: Sean McVay Linked to Amazon, Myles Garrett Update, and More
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 5 looking to build some momentum after their comeback victory over the Philadelphia Eagles. At 2-2, the Rams have an opportunity to get above .500 for the first time this season when they host the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football.
Several stories have emerged this week that are worth exploring further, including Myles Garrett’s return timeline and whether the Rams will be a team to watch ahead of the trade deadline. Let’s get into this week’s Sunday Morning Rams Notebook
It seems as if almost every year there is some speculation around Sean McVay leaving coaching and going into broadcasting. The door opened once again recently when details emerged from the new contract that Kirk Herbstreit signed with Amazon Prime.
According to Andrew Marchand from The Athletic , there is a clause in Herbstreit’s contract that would allow the network to move on from him if Sean McVay were to become available.
“The terms give Amazon flexibility to move on if one of its top targets, like Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay, becomes available, according to sources briefed on the decision who were not authorized to speak publicly,” wrote Marchand.
There is some history with McVay and Amazon Prime. Back in 2022, Prime tried to recruit McVay after the Rams went 5-12 and had a disastrous season. According to Marchand, Al Michaels preferred McVay over Herbstreit. However, McVay signed a new contract with the Rams and has remained with the team for the last four seasons.
With that said, McVay was close to leaving coaching for media after the 2022 season.McVay said this himself last year when he went on “Bussin’ With the Boys .”
"I almost quit coaching," McVay said. "And you can use the narrative that I was gonna go to media or whatever. But the truth would have been, I was quitting. I couldn't handle the losing. It was almost like a scarlet letter. I mean, there was moments…I was like counting down the days for that season to be over. Like, what a fraud."
There is some speculation that McVay won’t coach forever. He’s only 40 years old and has been coaching for 10 years. McVay has two kids with his wife Veronika Khomyn, and it’s possible that he leaves coaching at some point to get a better work-life balance.
Still, that doesn’t seem imminent, and the clause in Herbstreit’s contract appears to be more about the network protecting itself and maintaining flexibility. It’s possible that McVay leaves at some point. He could potentially tie himself to Matthew Stafford and leave once the Rams’ quarterback retires.
Mike Sando from The Athletic noted that some who know McVay suspect from afar that something has been bothering him this season. At the same time, with McVay’s input, the Rams just drafted a rookie quarterback in April to take over for Stafford. All of the McVay in the media rumors remain speculation at this point.
McVay was supposed to have an update for the media on Myles Garrett on Thursday, but didn’t. The result was some panic that the Rams were hiding more information than they were letting on when it came to Garrett. It was an understandable conclusion given how the Rams have handled the injury since July.
This trade has been a disaster for the Rams. https://t.co/VdXC1OzpJQ
However, McVay’s tone on Thursday when it was brought up was that he genuinely forgot. There were three days between McVay’s first media availability this week on Monday and when he spoke again on Thursday. The Rams’ head coach came ready with an update during Saturday’s media availability .
“He’s making good progress, but what I will say is he's not ready to say whether we'll open that window or not,” said McVay. “It's week to week in terms of how he feels, but I would say it's more likely that we do not start his clock next week.”
McVay stressed the importance of not just putting Garrett in a position to play, but in a position to return to performance. In Week 1, Garrett was in a position to play, but after the game he told the media that he didn’t feel like himself. The Rams will continue playing it safe with Garrett, which is how they’ve generally handled the situation since July.
While Garrett is eligible to return to practice next week ahead of the Rams’ game against the Arizona Cardinals, it doesn’t appear that he will. If you’ve followed our coverage here on Rams On SI, that shouldn’t come as a surprise.
A few weeks ago, it was reported by NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport that Garrett was given a six-week timeline following his arthroscopic knee surgery. However, last week, Jonathan Jones of The Athletic r eported that Garrett could return for Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders.
Since the beginning, Garrett has been determined to beat the timeline, but that doesn’t mean the Rams aren’t going to continue erring on the side of caution. Four weeks always seemed optimistic, with five weeks being more realistic, and six weeks being a worst-case scenario.
We’ll have to wait and see what happens with Garrett, but waiting another week to open his practice window provides the Rams with more flexibility. It wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams open his practice window ahead of the game against the Raiders, see how his knee responds, and then decide whether to activate him to the roster. Much like with Aaron Donald on the Commissioner’s Exempt List to begin the season, the Rams have some flexibility.
The NFL trade deadline is about a month away, but don’t expect the Rams to make any big splashes. Unless the situation drastically changes, it would be a surprise if they made a significant move. There are two main reasons for this, along with how the Rams’ front office and coaching staff may view their situation.
After signing Eric Kendricks to the practice squad this week, the Rams only have around $981k. That’s almost half as much as the next closest team. That little cap space makes it very difficult for the Rams to do anything via trade. It might not even be possible for the Rams to make it through the rest of the season on that number. At some point, they may have to rework a contract to open up some cap space, but their current financial situation makes a trade unlikely.
Additionally, the Rams don’t have the draft capital available to make a big trade. While the Rams have a second-round pick in 2027, if they were to move that, they wouldn’t pick until the fourth round. It’s possible they could look to move picks in 2028 like the Baltimore Ravens did when they acquired Cam Jurgens from the Philadelphia Eagles last week. However, the Rams don’t have a second-round pick, and moving their first would put them in a difficult spot.
It’s possible the Rams don’t see their roster in a spot where they need to make a trade to get over the top. The front office and coaching staff will likely see Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson returning from injured reserve as in-season additions.
An argument can be made that the Rams need a third wide receiver, but they will see Ferguson as a player to fill that role in the offense. This isn’t to say that a trade won’t happen or that the Rams won’t explore anything. However, it does remain unlikely.
Earlier this week, Mike Ditka passed away at the age of 86. While I never got the pleasure of meeting Ditka, he was a big part of my NFL Sundays growing up. I remember watching Mike Ditka on ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown, which was a must-watch for me on Sunday mornings. I’ll always remember Ditka as a no-nonsense personality who wasn’t afraid to speak what was on his mind.

title: Rams Week 5 Injury Report: Aaron Donald Among Three Starters Set to Return vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to get multiple starters back as they head into Week 5 to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football. After missing last week, tight end Colby Parkinson, cornerback Jaylen Watson, and defensive lineman Aaron Donald all look to be ready to go for Monday’s game. The only player with a game designation on Saturday’s injury report was safety Quentin Lake, who is listed as questionable.
Lake didn’t practice on Thursday or Friday with a hip injury, but was upgraded to limited on Saturday. There wasn’t too much concern with Lake this week with the Rams just being smart with him given his workload this season.
“He got it when he fell backwards on something so it's a weird deal, but he's doing good,” said McVay this week. “We're just being smart with him. He's played so many snaps. We just wanted to be smart.”
Edge rusher Josaiah Stewart also didn’t practice earlier in the week, but was limited on Saturday. Stewart wasn’t given a game designation and presumably will be good to play. The same can be said about linebacker Nate Landman, who has been banged up over the last couple of weeks. Landman was a full participant on Saturday.
While Donald didn’t practice on Saturday, that has been his routine this season. All indications are that Donald will play. Speaking to the media this week, Donald said, “I'm planning to play this week.”
The Rams missed Colby Parkinson last week, as they were unable to utilize their usual 13 personnel packages with three tight ends. Without Parkinson, the Rams utilized 11 personnel at an 88 percent rate , which was their highest since Week 5 of last season. Cornerback Jaylen Watson is also set to make his return. Josh Wallace played well in his absence, but getting Watson back will provide a big boost to the Rams’ secondary.
“They're good to go," McVay said.
On the Bills’ side, defensive lineman Ed Oliver and wide receiver Joshua Palmer have already been ruled out. The Rams will certainly be watching the status of wide receiver DJ Moore before Monday’s game. Moore is officially listed as questionable along with defensive lineman Landman Jackson and cornerback Dee Alford.
The Rams have struggled to find consistency through the first four weeks of the season, but getting healthier should help as they look to build on last week's win over the Eagles. With Donald, Parkinson, and Watson expected to return, the Rams will have several key pieces back in place for one of their toughest matchups of the season.

title: Rams Coaches Detail Biggest Challenges of Facing Josh Allen and Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams a re set to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Heading into the season, both teams were seen as Super Bowl contenders. It wouldn’t be surprising if this ended up being the Super Bowl matchup when all is said and done.
However, heading into Week 5, both teams are still trying to find their rhythm. The Bills are 3-1, but haven’t played well the last two weeks. They turned the ball over five times and somehow still managed to beat the Los Angeles Chargers. Meanwhile, the Rams have been up and down and have yet to get above .500. A win on Monday night could propel either team into a winning streak.
Throughout the week, the Rams’ coaching staff and players have spoken about some of the challenges that the Bills will present.
When the Rams and Bills played in 2024, Josh Allen threw for 342 yards and three touchdowns as he went on to win MVP. Allen not only has one of the best arms in the NFL, but he’s also a great athlete with the ability to make plays with his legs.
Allen has 1,039 yards passing this season to go with six touchdowns and three interceptions. His 0.18 EPA per play ranks fifth in the NFL. While the Rams have the No. 2 overall pass defense, Allen will provide a good test. Over the last three weeks, the Rams have faced Jameis Winston, Bo Nix, and Jalen Hurts. Allen will give the Rams their biggest test since playing Brock Purdy in Week 1.
“You can see he's obviously one of the ultimate competitors in this league,” said defensive coordinator Chris Shula. “He's a great quarterback standing there playing in the pocket. Then, you can see all the off-schedule plays that he makes. He's one of the best players, if not the best player, in the NFL right now.”
The Rams are set to get Aaron Donald back against the Bills as well, which should help against Allen.. Donald missed last week with a sore back, but is set to return for Monday night’s game against the Bills.
Donald has played against the Bills three times, but only twice has he faced Josh Allen. In 2022, the Rams lost to the Bills 31-10 in the season opener. Donald had one sack in that game. In 2020, Donald had a vintage performance, recording two sacks with a forced fumble and fumble recovery.
“He's a playmaker,” said Donald. “He's a different type of player. I call him a futuristic ‘Big Ben’, more athletic, harder to tackle, a lot faster, able to move a lot differently. He can hurt you in a lot of different ways. He's not easy to take down. He's a playmaker. That's all you can say. You have to find ways to keep him in the box, make sure when you get your hands on him, make sure you get him down to the ground. Don’t let him stiff arm you and be able to look downfield and throw a touchdown. He’s a guy that you have to worry about and have to try to find a way to affect [him].”
Back in 2020, the Rams previously had interest in Jim Leonhard, but ended up hiring Brandon Staley instead. Leonhard spent the last two years on the Denver Broncos’ coaching staff before he was brought in as the defensive coordinator for the Bills this offseason under Joe Brady.
The Bills currently rank 29th in defensive EPA and have especially struggled against the pass. They’ve allowed 0.11 EPA per pass, which ranks 26th in the NFL. Over the first four weeks of the season, the Rams have struggled to find some consistency in the passing game . Playing the Bills could provide them with an opportunity to get things back on track.
“I have a lot of respect for him, his career, his background, type of mentality that he has in general,” said Rams offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. “You can see that all over their defense with their ability to challenge you with different looks, their ability to move guys into different spots and honestly have an attacking style. They do a great job up front. Their front makes their squad go. If you don't take care of those guys both in the run game and in the pass game, you can end up in some tough spots. As much as you can, you want to stay on track and not let those guys be able to set a rush and be able to pin their ears back.”
If the Rams are going to win this game, they’ll need their top two wide receivers in Davante Adams and Puka Nacua to step up and play well. With Nacua out of the lineup in Weeks 2 and 3, Adams played like he was in his prime, recording back-to-back 100 yard games. The Rams have yet to get both players going in the same game this season.
Last week, Romeo Doubs had success with the New England Patriots when facing off against Maxwell Hairston.Doubs scored two touchdowns on Hairston, and the Rams may try to get a similar matchup with Adams. However, this will be Adams’ first time facing a defense coordinated by Leonhard, and he spoke about that challenge on Friday.
“Watching as much tape as possible, whether that's stuff that they've done against us, this season, or things that they've done in the past,” said Adams. “Also, not getting too wrapped up in that because come gametime, you have to react to the coverages or whatever they decide to throw at you. You can get immersed in everything and think you have it figured out, but you still have to react once the call is made and once the play starts. I like to have a decent idea of what they like to do. Then go and roll with the punches from there during the game.”

title: Rams Midweek Report: Searching for Consistency, Myles Garrett Update, Trade Deadline Outlook
full_text:
A big theme this week for the Los Angeles Rams has been whether they can find some consistency . The Rams have the No. 2 offense and No. 2 defense, but the 32nd-ranked special teams unit. They have a top-five offense but are just 19th in points per game. They have a top-5 offense, but are just 19th in points per game.
If the Rams are going to become the team that many expected coming into the season, they need to find consistency. This is a team that’s been penalized 21 times over the last two weeks, the most in a two-game stretch under head coach Sean McVay. They have a -5 turnover differential through four games, which is tied for 28th in the NFL. Untimely turnovers, penalties, and special teams gaffes have been a recurring problem for this team.
“I'm interested to see how we can play cleaner football,” said McVay on Monday. “We have to play better. We have to consistently do it in all three phases and we have to earn the right to play better quality football. We have to all coach better too.”
The Rams are doing things that we aren’t accustomed to seeing from a McVay-coached team. That’s what makes the penalties and untimely mistakes so baffling at times . McVay can become pass-happy at times, but over 100 pass attempts in a two-game stretch is unheard of even for him. Sunday marked the first time since 2012 that Stafford had 50 or more attempts in back-to-back games.
Through four weeks, Matthew Stafford has an EPA per pass of -0.01. At this time last year, it was 0.15. Stafford starting the season slowly is nothing unusual, but his mistakes have cost the Rams in big moments or put them in difficult positions.
“Definitely room for improvement. There have been some really bright moments and some stuff I'm really proud of and stuff that I definitely wish I could take back to help us be in a better position to win games,” said Stafford. “I want to do everything I can to put our team in the best position to succeed. I've done that sometimes this year and other times I have not. I want to make sure that I do that at a more consistent clip moving forward.”
Given that teams no longer play their starters in the preseason, there is some belief that it can take those first three or four weeks for starters to get up to speed. The Rams have now played four games. There are no more excuses.
Coming into the season, this was a team with high expectations, and they have yet to really play up to that level. A lot of that is because of the lack of consistency. After coming back from 10 points in the fourth quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles, the Rams seemed to find something. They’ll have a chance on Monday night to show whether they can carry that over or if it was just another flash in the pan.
"It's that time of the year where you're establishing your identity both schematically and the mentality that you play with," said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase. "There are things that we can do to take care of stuff that we can control so that's been an area of emphasis for us, especially this week."
Prior to the season, the Rams placed a pair of offensive linemen in Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich on injured reserve. Trost injured his hamstring in the first preseason game and Dedich managed a hand injury all summer. With the Rams having played four games, both players are eligible to come off of injured reserve . However, it doesn’t appear as if the Rams are in any rush to do so.
“Those guys, they could,” said McVay. “We could open that up, but that's not a conversation that we've had at this point.”
It makes sense for the Rams to hold off for now, as both players are depth pieces and not immediate starters. The Rams only have eight injured reserve return designations to use and they are already set to use two on Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson. There’s a chance one or both are activated at some point, but given the current health of the offensive line, the Rams are waiting.
McVay was asked on Thursday whether Garrett will return to practice after his four-week injured reserve window. Monday night will mark Garrett’s fourth game that he’s missed and he’ll be eligible to return.
“I'm not sure yet,” said McVay. “I know that the rehab is progressing well. He's looked good in the meetings.”
The Rams’ head coach had previously mentioned that he would have more of an update, but that was not the case on Thursday. With that said, based on reports that exist , the Rams remain hopeful that Garrett will return next week, but Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders is more realistic. Garrett had a six-week timeline, which would have put him on track to return in Week 8 against the Los Angeles Chargers, but that was more of a worst-case scenario. Garrett has been progressing ahead of that.
Prior to Sunday’s game against the Eagles, the Rams placed Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve . Just when Ferguson was starting to have a positive impact on the offense and become a featured piece, a medial ankle sprain has forced him to miss time.
Ferguson will have to miss four games, which would put his return in Week 8 against the Chargers. Based on what McVay said on the Coach McVay Show this week with JB Long, it doesn’t seem like Ferguson will miss any more time beyond that.
“He’ll be back. He’ll be ready to go after those four weeks,” McVay said.
I wouldn’t expect the Rams to be active at the trade deadline. That doesn’t mean they won’t make a move, but it would be very difficult for them to do anything significant. It’s possible the Rams will see Myles Garrett’s return and getting Terrance Ferguson back as in-season additions.
There are a few things to note here. The Rams currently only have around $981,000 in cap space. That’s by far the lowest in the NFL. It would be nearly impossible for them to take on another contract at that number. TThe Rams also don’t have a lot of draft capital to send away. They don’t have a first- or third-round pick next year. If they moved that second-round pick, they wouldn’t select until the fourth round. Additionally, they don’t have a second-round pick in 2028. While the Rams could use a third wide receiver, it just isn’t something that will be in the cards.
It’s certainly possible that the Rams will beat the Bills on Monday night . The Bills are dealing with injuries in the secondary, which will provide the Rams an opportunity to get something going in the passing game. However, the Bills are coming off of a loss last week and will be ready to play a clean game.
A loss to the Bills isn’t the worst thing. That would put the Rams at 2-3 with two of their three losses against AFC opponents. The Rams can ‘get right’ against the Cardinals in Week 6 and then the schedule lightens up. It’s possible the Rams could rattle off six straight wins before playing the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 13. A Week 14 matchup against the 49ers will then provide an opportunity to avenge their loss in Week 1.
The Rams signed Eric Kendricks this week, which came as a bit of a surprise. While some have speculated that Kendricks is a special teams addition, it may have been more than that. Some of Kendricks’ early role may come on special teams. The Rams have already used two of Eli Neal’s three roster elevations. Grant Stuard is also dealing with an injury this week.
However, at 34, Kendricks likely wouldn’t have signed on simply to play special teams. He’s beyond that point of his career. His addition will give the Rams some flexibility to manage Nate Landman’s injury if needed, while also allowing Kendricks to rotate in alongside Omar Speights. He may have a bigger role once he settles in.
Eric Kendricks is joining the Los Angeles Rams! 🔥🍿 pic.twitter.com/CKNjIj1sO0
On Friday, several players had their designations upgraded. Defensive lineman Aaron Donald was limited on Thursday, but was a full participant on Friday. The same can be said about tight end Colby Parkinson. The Rams will be glad to have both players back against the Bills.

title: 5 Keys to Victory for the Rams Against the Bills in Week 5
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to host the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on Monday Night Football in Week 5. With a win, the Rams could get above .500 for the first time this season . Over the first month, the Rams have been scrapping to get by, and Monday night will provide a good test against a team many consider to be a Super Bowl contender. Here are five keys to victory for the Rams to beat the Bills.
Under Joe Brady, the Buffalo Bills have had their most successful run game under Josh Allen. James Cook has a 52.9 percent rushing success rate. Cook’s 11.4 percent explosive run rate is also the highest in the NFL.
For the Rams defense to operate the way it wants to, stopping the run is key. It’s something that they didn’t do in Week 1. However, over the last three weeks, they’ve been much better. Their -0.2 EPA per rush allowed in that span ranks sixth in the NFL. The Rams need to be able to contain James Cook and limit the explosive runs. That will also limit what the Bills can do in the passing game with their tight ends in heavy personnel.
Last week, Kyren Williams became the first Rams running back since Todd Gurley to have at least 10 carries and 10 receptions in a game. The Rams have struggled to find a third wide receiver in the offense with Terrance Ferguson on injured reserve. It’s possible that Williams can be that third option in the passing game.
The Bills could provide another opportunity to get Williams involved. Defensively, the Bills have allowed the third-most targets to running backs with 21 receptions. Their 162 receiving yards allowed to running backs are the seventh-most and they’ve allowed three receiving touchdowns. This is an area where Williams showed last week that he can be a threat in this area, and the Rams may need him to contribute again.
For as solid as the Bills have been at tackle in the past, that hasn’t been the case this year. Dion Dawkins allowed a seven percent pressure rate last year and that’s up to 12 percent in 2026. For the most part, Dawkins has struggled this season.
#Patriots rookie Gabe Jacas's bull-rush puts five-time Pro Bowl LT Dion Dawkins on the ground. pic.twitter.com/8Wu10Z0Tle
This is a matchup that the Rams will have to win if they’re going to have a chance in this game. Byron Young has one of the highest pressure rates at 18.8 percent among edge rushers. That ranks 10th in the NFL. He also ranks eighth with 18 pressures. Without Myles Garrett, the Rams need Young to continue taking over games as he did last week.
The Bills have struggled at cornerback this season as they’ve dealt with some injuries. However, it’s also just not a position group that’s played well. The Rams should have the advantage here throughout the game. Puka Nacua returned from injury last week, but the Rams will also need Davante Adams to play like he did in Weeks 2 and 3.
If the Rams can get Adams isolated against Maxwell Hairston a few times, that’s a matchup they can take advantage of and find success with. Romeo Doubs scored two touchdowns against Hairston last week. The Rams haven’t gotten the connection between Stafford and Adams going in the red zone yet this season. Monday night could provide an opportunity.
When in doubt, attack Maxwell Hairston. He’s been horrible Bench him. Put in Kani Walker pic.twitter.com/MW1ELJHLKq
For as much as fans will want the Rams to play man coverage, that’s simply not something they can do against Josh Allen. Allen has the ability to scramble for large gains, which are effective against man. Against man coverage, Allen has a 0.36 EPA per play, which is the sixth-best in the NFL. Against zone coverage, that drops by more than half to 0.17.
This isn’t to say that the Rams should stay away from man coverage altogether. However, Chris Shula will need to mix up his coverages and do so selectively. He’ll need to pick his spots and do the same when he opts to blitz. This will be a good test for Shula and the defense, who haven’t faced a true challenge since playing the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1.

title: Matchups the Rams Must Win to Beat the Bills on Monday Night Football
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams play the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in what should be one of the best games of the week. When these two teams have gotten together in the past, it usually comes down to a dramatic finish. Two of the last three games have been decided by three points or less. Here are three matchups that could decide the game between the Rams and Bills.
This season, the Rams have averaged 1.5 yards before contact in the run game, which is the sixth-most in the NFL. However, when Deone Walker is on the field for the Bills, teams have averaged 0.1 yards before contact compared to 1.8 when he’s not on the field. Walker has been a key piece on the Bills’ defense, and they are much better when he’s on the field. On all plays, the Bills average 5.2 yards per play compared to 6.2 when he’s off it.
Deone Walker lol I'm not fully convinced he knows what he's doing on a down-to-down basis... but this dude is massive and athletic lol some straight freakazoid reps pic.twitter.com/WM4b45MrHY
If the Rams are going to get the most out of Matthew Stafford on Monday, they need to be able to remain balanced in the run game. They also need to protect the pocket. That starts with Coleman Shelton, Steve Avila, and Kevin Dotson against Walker. Walker’s 20 impact plays rank third in the NFL among interior defensive linemen.
It’s no secret that the weakness of the Rams’ defense is at linebacker. The Bills utilize heavy tight end sets more than any other team in the NFL. This season, the Bills have utilized 12 personnel on 20 percent of their offensive snaps and 13 personnel on 26 percent of their offensive snaps. Out of 12 personnel, the Bills rank third with 0.31 offensive EPA per play.
While Dalton Kincaid may not be a featured piece of the Bills’ offense, when he gets involved, he can be successful in the pass game. The Bills could have a huge matchup advantage here with Kincaid against Omar Speights, who can struggle in coverage. Speights has allowed 1.51 yards per coverage snap this season, which ranks as the eighth-most in the NFL. Both of the Rams’ linebackers are better in the run game.
The Rams will need to be ready on the offensive line as the Bills have the personnel up front to take over a game. Despite having to throw more than 100 times over the last two weeks, the Rams have done well from a protection standpoint. The Rams held one of the better pass rushes in the NFL in check two weeks ago against the Denver Broncos. The Bills will provide another challenge.
NFL sack leaders through Week 4 Greg Rousseau        6.0 Dallas Turner            5.5 T.J. Watt                      4.5 Will Anderson Jr.     4.5 Mason Graham       4.0 pic.twitter.com/IcCI3R05IF
This season, the Bills have a 45.8 percent pressure rate, which is the fourth-highest in the NFL. It’s a group led by Greg Rousseau. His 24 pressures rank fourth in the NFL, despite him facing the sixth-most double teams. He also leads the NFL with six sacks. Warren McClendon has been good, but he certainly has his deficiencies.

full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Coming into this game, the Rams are 2-2 after beating the Philadelphia Eagles last week, 24-20, and coming back from 10 points down in the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, the Bills lost their first game of the season, falling to the New England Patriots, 29-26.
Through the first four games of the season, the Rams have yet to truly find their identity. Matthew Stafford has been inconsistent and special teams remain an issue.Already two games behind in the NFC West, the Rams can’t afford to fall much further behind.
For as inconsistent as the Rams have been, the Bills have had their moments as well. They turned the ball over five times against the Los Angeles Chargers and somehow managed to win. The Bills’ defense has struggled early on, and Drake Maye had his first strong game of the season after not playing well in the first three games.
If there was ever a chance for the Rams to get it right on offense, it’s this game against the Bills. The Bills rank 26th in pass defense EPA per play. Additionally, their 48.2 percent pass defense success rate ranks 30th. This is a team that has struggled to stop opposing passing attacks. While the Rams will be without Terrance Ferguson, this could be a game for Stafford, Davante Adams, and Puka Nacua to take over.
Hairston has allowed just eight receptions on 19 targets this season, which is an improvement over his rookie season. However, last week, he struggled against Romeo Doubs on the outside. Doubs had six receptions for 58 yards and two touchdowns. Both of Doubs’ touchdowns came against Hairston.
Maxwell Hairston is having TROUBLE today against Romeo Doubs. Hairston’s holding penalty on 3rd gives NE a fresh set of downs inside the five. Then gets beat by Doubs again for another TD… NE retakes the lead 21-17 #BillsMafia pic.twitter.com/HsmMHCS8zI

There’s an opportunity for the offense to get going against the Bills’ secondary, but can Stafford and Co. be trusted not to make a costly mistake? With the Bills coming off of a loss, the Rams get a more focused Buffalo team and come up just short. Bills 30, Rams 27

title: Rams Injury Report: Aaron Donald Among Three Key Starters Who Could Return vs. Bills
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams will hope to get multiple starters back in Week 5 as they get set to take on the Buffalo Bills. After missing Aaron Donald, Colby Parkinson, and Jaylen Watson against the Philadelphia Eagles last week, the Rams are hopeful that all three will be back for Monday night’s game.
"The expectation is that as long as they progress accordingly then they'll be ready to go," said head coach Sean McVay. "I want to see how Jaylen feels. We'll get a little shoulder harness out there, [see] how he's going to be able to block destruct. Colby is really progressing in a very positive direction. We'll be smart with the kind of reps that he takes. Then like I mentioned to you guys with Aaron, [we'll] see how his back responds. Everything is trended in the right direction.”
On the initial injury report, Donald, Parkinson, and Watson were all listed as limited participants on Monday. Donald was a surprise addition to the injury report last week after head coach Sean McVay said that he had a sore back after the game. The Rams erred on the side of caution by resting Donald last week, and the team was able to get a win without him. All indications are that Donald could play on Monday night .
Additionally, the Rams will hope to get Parkinson back after he was inactive last week with an AC sprain in his shoulder. The Rams will certainly welcome Parkinson back as they look to get back to 13 personnel this week. Without Parkinson, the Rams utilized 11 personnel at their highest rate since Week 5 of last season.
Jaylen Watson also missed last week after dislocating his shoulder in the loss to the Broncos. Getting Watson back before facing a good Bills offense would be a huge boost for the defense. The Rams will look to ramp up Donald, Parkinson, and Watson as the week progresses.
Also on the injury report were linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), edge rusher Josaiah Stewart (groin), safety Quentin Lake (hip), linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder), and wide receiver Davante Adams (rest). None of them participated in practice on Thursday.
According to The Athletic’s Nate Atkins, Lake’s injury is minor, and he was heavily iced after Sunday’s game. Landman has been on the injury report the last three weeks and has played. Stewart showed up on the injury report toward the end of last week and managed to play on Sunday. Still, he’ll be one to monitor.
"He's so tough. He pushed through it," said McVay. "He got it when he fell backwards on something so it's a weird deal, but he's doing good. We're just being smart with him."
Not practicing today will be DB Quentin Lake (hip), LB Grant Stuard (hamstring), OLB Josaiah Stewart (groin), ILB Nate Landman (shoulder) and WR Davante Adams (veteran rest day). Lake's injury is minor, Sean McVay said. Lake had it pretty iced up after the game on Sunday.
McVay mentioned that wide receiver Konata Mumpfield had a rotator cuff contusion during his Monday press conference. Mumpfield was a full participant on Thursday.
On the Bills’ side, the Rams will be monitoring the availability of wide receiver DJ Moore, defensive lineman Ed Oliver, and cornerback Dee Alford. All three did not practice on Thursday. Additionally, defensive lineman Landon Jackson and cornerback Christian Benford were limited.
The Rams will certainly hope to be as close to full strength as possible heading into Monday night’s matchup against the Bills. While they managed to overcome several key absences against the Eagles, doing so against the Bills will present a more difficult challenge. With Donald, Parkinson, and Watson trending in the right direction, the Rams could be getting some much-needed reinforcements at an important point in their season.

title: How to Watch Rams vs. Bills in Week 5 (Start Time, TV Channel, What to Watch For)
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are set to take on the Buffalo Bills in Week 5 on Monday Night Football at SoFi Stadium. After beating the Philadelphia Eagles last week, the Rams are 2-2 and back at .500. Meanwhile, the Bills lost their first game in their new stadium, falling 29-26 to the New England Patriots.
Prior to losing to the Patriots , the Bills looked like an unstoppable force. They beat the Los Angeles Chargers the week before despite turning the ball over five times. Heading into Week 5, the Bills rank fourth overall in total DVOA.
The Rams were staring a 1-3 record in the face before overcoming a 10-point deficit in the fourth quarter. If they’re going to win at home against the Bills in primetime, they’ll need to find a way to be much more consistent.
For the second time this season, the Rams will play at home on Monday Night Football. They played the New York Giants in Week 2, snapping a five-game losing streak on Monday Night Football. The Rams last played the Bills in primetime to open the 2022 season and lost, 31-10.
Fans should expect plenty of penalties in this game. Scott Novak's crew is now responsible for the two games with the highest combined penalty totals this season. Last week, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Chargers combined for 30 penalties for 280 yards. In Week 2, the Green Bay Packers and New York Jets combined for 27 penalties for 280 yards.
Bills-Rams MNF uniform matchup is set. Appreciate Buffalo going white pants against the royal-heavy Rams.  Best possible primary outcome for this one. pic.twitter.com/ZYOisQaFw5
The Rams and Bills have played some dramatic games in the past. When these two teams met in 2024, the Rams won 44-42 after the Bills nearly erased a 38-21 fourth-quarter deficit. The Rams almost came back from a 28-3 deficit in 2020, but lost 35-32. Back in 2012, Sam Bradford found Brandon Gibson with under a minute left to win 15-12. In the all-time series, the Bills lead 9-6 and have won three of the last four.
Over the past few seasons, Matthew Stafford and Josh Allen have been two of the most prolific quarterbacks in the NFL. They’ve met three times in the regular season, with Allen leading the head-to-head, 2-1. On Monday night, each player has an opportunity to reach a different milestone.
With a win on Monday Night Football, Josh Allen can become the fourth quarterback all-time with at least 100 wins, including the postseason, in his first nine seasons. He can also tie for the third-most regular season wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine seasons. Only Russell Wilson and Patrick Mahomes have more. Additionally, if Matthew Stafford throws a touchdown pass, he can surpass Ben Roethlisberger for the sixth-most touchdown passes, including the postseason, all-time. With three touchdown passes, he can become the first player in NFL history with at least 150 touchdown passes with two franchises.
This season, the Rams and Bills have used three-tight-end sets at the highest rates in the NFL. The Rams lead the NFL in 13 personnel usage at 31 percent. Meanwhile, the Bills are right behind them at 20 percent. Additionally, The Bills also frequently utilize 12 personnel, featuring two tight ends. Tight ends play a huge role in both offenses, making their usage something to watch on Monday night.

title: Rams' Penalty Problems Are Real, but the Numbers Tell a Bigger Story
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Denver Broncos in Week 3, they were penalized 13 times for 91 yards. It was the most accepted penalties against the Rams in a game since Week 4 of 2020. Last week against the Eagles, the Rams were penalized eight times for 100 yards. The 21 accepted penalties for 191 yards against the Rams are their most over a two-game stretch during Sean McVay's tenure as head coach.
The recent uptick in penalties by the Rams is simply uncharacteristic of a Sean McVay-led team. Throughout the McVay era, the Rams have struggled to score in the red zone at times due to questionable play-calling. This season, the Rams have had to settle for field goals because of penalties.
“The things that really chapped me that I think are a reflection of an undisciplined team are the pre-snap, the procedural things,” said McVay this week. “Those are the things that we can control with focus and concentration. They'll happen from time to time, but we have to minimize those situationally whether that's jumping offsides offensively, things like that, even making decisions where there's no discrepancy on.”
The past 2 weeks, 21 accepted penalties against the Rams measured 191 yards. Both figures are the most in consecutive games in 10 season under Sean McVay, a span of time in which discipline has been a hallmark. I just looked through them all, a few things to note: *Penalties…
In Week 3 against the Broncos, the Rams had to settle for field goals after an offensive pass interference penalty on Davante Adams and a hold on Steve Avila.
Last week, the Rams settled for field goals after a holding penalty on Davis Allen. According to Warren Sharp of Sharp Football Analytics , red-zone holding is up 38 percent, second only to 2019. After taking over at the Eagles’ 38-yard line, a seven-yard run from Williams was called back because of a questionable illegal blindside block.
BLINDSIDE BLOCK…on Puka Nacua?! What happened to the beautiful game of football… pic.twitter.com/RjcsS1MepO
However, this isn’t only happening to the Rams. This season, there have been the most red zone penalties per game by offenses in NFL history according to Sharp. More than 56.55 percent of red zone flags are on offense, which is up from 48 percent. There have also been the most penalties on third and fourth downs in the second half of games in NFL history.
For as frustrating as some of the penalties have been at times, context is important. This season, the relationship between the NFL players, league, and its officials has hit a breaking point. This week, the NFL suspended two officials for their on-field behavior . The 2026 season has seen the most flags in over a decade.
Penalties are certainly up for the Rams, but that’s also the case around the league. Despite the Rams being penalized more, they are still only tied for the 10th-most penalties per game with five other teams, and there are eight teams between 7.5 and 8.0 penalties per game. They have lost 0.15 EPA per play due to penalties, which is the 11th-worst in the NFL. With that said, the Rams still have a net penalty count of -11, which is the fourth-worst.
Penalty Impact so far this year (Somehow another Vikings defense stat) pic.twitter.com/0DByDipxfG
This is a case where multiple things can be true at the same time. Penalties are up around the NFL as a whole. Comparatively speaking, the Rams are also committing more penalties and ranking higher than they have in the past. The Rams have also been on the wrong side of some of the 50-50 calls, most notably the defensive pass interference penalty on Josh Wallace at the end of the game against the Broncos.
Throughout McVay’s tenure, the Rams have generally been one of the more disciplined teams in the NFL. It’s part of what makes the more recent uptick so jarring. Some of the increase can be attributed to the league-wide trend, but the Rams are also to blame. McVay has made it clear that those are mistakes that they need to clean up.
The league-wide trend of more penalties being called certainly adds some context, but it doesn't completely excuse the Rams' lack of discipline over the last two weeks. There are still things that they can control. If the Rams are going to reach their ceiling as a Super Bowl contender, they can't continue allowing self-inflicted mistakes to take points off the board.

title: Raiders Stock Report: 3 Players Rising, Falling After Week 5
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders had a rough day on the road against the New England Patriots. Few things went Las Vegas' way. Las Vegas has followed up its 3-0 start with two consecutive losses to two of the league's best teams.
This was always going to be Las Vegas' toughest stretch of games, facing the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots, Buffalo Bills, and Los Angeles Rams back-to-back. While the season's first three games showed growth, the last two showed where it still needs to improve.
The Raiders suffered an ugly loss on Sunday. It would be easy to say there were no positives from the performance, but that would be inaccurate. Just as there are negatives during wins, there are positives during losses, especially for a team in the early stages of a rebuild.
Las Vegas' loss to New England was their worst game of the season. The Patriots' offense posted one of the best offensive outputs in franchise history, yardage-wise. Las Vegas now has a clear idea of where they stand and how far they are from the league's best.
Below are a few players on the rise and some whose stocks are falling following the Raiders' Week 5 road loss to the Patriots.
Bowers continues to look like the league's best tight end after another impressive performance. Every team in the league knows the Raiders want to get the ball to Bowers, yet he still dominates when they need him. Bowers was again the team's leading receiver.
Bowers registered 110 yards on eight catches and gave the Raiders a puncher's chance on a day when they were clearly outmatched, outcoached, and outplayed. Bowers was one of the few bright spots from an all-around bad outing for the Raiders.
Tucker did not fill the stat sheet like he did in Week 2. However, his chances of doing so on an offense with Cody White as its next-best wide receiver are slim. Tucker caught two passes for 21 yards in the first half, both of which were significant for the struggling unit.
Porter had several big plays, including a fumble recovery. He also played solid coverage on several plays, showing the speed that helped him rise up the depth chart. It was a rough day for the Raiders as a whole, but it was encouraging to see Porter have some success.
The Raiders' defensive line is the deepest position group on the roster. Las Vegas needed that depth, losing multiple interior defensive linemen throughout the game. During that time, Butler, one of the Raiders' most experienced defensive linemen, quietly gave the unit solid play.
Shortly before halftime, Butler forced a fumble that was recovered by Porter. It did not result in points for the Raiders' offense, but it helped keep points off the board for the Patriots.
Las Vegas' questionable defensive backfield needed protection from the Raiders' defensive line. Last Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs and today against the Patriots showed what will likely happen throughout the season if the unit cannot generate a consistent pass rush.
The Raiders' defense has been aggressive all season. On Sunday, the unit seemed unable to generate a pass rush or stop quarterback Drake Maye, who was playing with several of his backup wide receivers.
Many of the struggles Cousins and the Raiders' offense are having are innate. Looking at the depth chart and the team's training camp and preseason, it was evident that the roster still had things to fix, especially on offense. Some of those things can't be fixed until next offseason.
It was well known that Cousins' health and age could affect things. The Raiders would not be 3-2 without Cousins' experience. However, the deficiencies Las Vegas' offense has do not match well with the deficiencies in Cousins' game at this point in his career. Defenses have figured that out.
The Patriots had backup wide receivers wide open downfield multiple times. It was not a talent issue; it was a schematic and roster issue. Las Vegas' defensive backfield and wide receivers are their Achilles' heel.

title: NFL World Goes Nuts As Raiders’ Fernando Mendoza Takes Field
