title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Jets’ Week 5 Game Against Browns (All Eyes on Thomas-Stephens Tandem)
full_text:
The Jets hope to get back on track in Week 5 after dropping their last three games. However, it will be no easy task for Gang Green, as the Browns come into town riding a three-game winning streak. Both teams are dealing with their share of injuries , but that’s part of the challenge every team faces over a season.
For the Jets, Sunday’s game could be a turning point in the season.
A loss would drop the Jets to 1-4 and put even more pressure on head coach Aaron Glenn’s future , especially with three of the team’s next five opponents having a winning record. That’s why coming away with a win is critical for New York.
With that said, here are the three matchups that will determine whether Gang Green gets back on track.
Several factors have contributed to the Browns’ hot start. Watson has played well, the defense has been great, and head coach Todd Monken has had a big impact.
One area that’s been almost been a non-factor, however, is Cleveland’s run game. Through four games, the Browns rank 23rd in rushing yards per game (93.8) and yards per carry (3.7). Star running back Quinshon Judkins just hasn’t been able to get things going, recording 177 rushing yards and averaging an abysmal three yards per carry.
The unit has been better, combining for 244 yards in the last two games, but it’ll need to step it up to keep the win streak going. Shutting down their run game should be among the Jets’ top priorities heading into this matchup.
New York emphasized improving its run defense by getting bigger up front in the offseason. The unit looked significantly better in the first two games, allowing just 131 rushing yards. However, they’ve regressed over the last two weeks.
In their losses to the Lions and the Bears, the Jets have been dominated at the line of scrimmage, giving up 363 rushing yards and eight rushes of 10 yards or more.
They’ll need to bounce back against the Browns.
Luckily for New York, Cleveland isn’t as explosive on the ground, with just nine runs of at least 10 yards through four weeks. Their offensive line hasn’t helped, as the unit ranks 24th with a 57.9 run-blocking grade , per Pro Football Focus .
To beat the Browns, the Jets’ defensive line must maintain outside leverage, clog the gaps, and prevent Judkins from reaching the second level. Forcing Cleveland into obvious passing situations would put the game in Watson’s hands and give New York’s defense more opportunities to generate pressure.
Watson has already had to bail them out of multiple games this season, with some victories coming down to the final whistle. If they can force Watson to do it all himself, they’ll have a chance to capitalize on his mistakes.
Although KC Concepcion Jr. and Harold Fanin Jr. lead the Browns’ pass catchers in targets with 17 apiece, it’s Denzel Boston who’s been Deshaun Watson’s go-to receiver .
That shouldn’t surprise anyone.
Standing at 6'4" and 215 lbs, Boston excelled at the University of Washington at moving the chains with his contested-catch ability and was an elite red zone threat, with 14 of his 20 touchdowns coming in the red zone. Those traits have quickly translated to the NFL, where he’s become Watson’s most trusted target.
Over four games, Boston leads the team in receiving yards with 284, while hauling in 13 catches for two touchdowns. Of his 22 targets, eight are on passes of at least 20 yards downfield , according to NFL Next Gen Stats.
Last week against the Steelers, Watson connected with Boston for a 60-yard completion, setting the Browns up for a touchdown three plays later. Boston has primarily run go routes, outs and comebacks, with some slants over the middle, giving him opportunities to use his size and playmaking ability at different levels of the field.
“(Boston is) only going to get better because he’s tough physically and mentally , he’s diligent, he’s got an excellent catch radius and plays strong to the ball,” head coach Todd Monken told reporters.
Limiting Boston from making explosive plays will be the top priority for the Jets. Outside corners Brandon Stephens and AZ Thomas will be tasked with neutralizing Boston’s big-play ability.
At 6-foot-1 and 6-foot-2, respectively, Stephens and Thomas have the size and the physical play style to match up with Boston. So far, the two have stood out in coverage.
Stephens has allowed just 11 receptions (18 targets) for 141 yards, while Thomas has given up 17 catches (21 targets) for 123 yards and two touchdowns. According to PFF, Stephens has posted a 74.4 coverage grade and Thomas a 70.2 , with both ranking among the top 20 cornerbacks in coverage among 103 qualifying players.
This matchup comes down to whether Stephens and Thomas can prevent Boston from creating explosive plays. They have the length and size to challenge him on any deep shot, but they’ll also have to limit his yards after the catch.
The Jets did a good job limiting downfield targets to Rome Odunze last week, but he was still making plays at the intermediate levels. They’ll need to avoid a similar outcome with Boston, who can hurt them with any room they give him.
Even after trading away superstar pass rusher Myles Garrett, the Browns’ pass rush has remained highly effective at generating pressure.
Cleveland has proven it can get after the quarterback with its front four, as the unit is tied for fifth in sacks (12) and sixth in quarterback pressure percentage (40.4%), despite blitzing at just a 27.3% rate.
This has allowed them to drop more defenders into coverage, where they’ve recorded four interceptions.
However, the Browns’ defensive line is banged up . Mason Graham, who leads the team in sacks with four, Kalia Davis, and Mike Hall Jr. all missed practice on Thursday, while Derek Barnett was limited. Their availability for Sunday is uncertain.
Even if some of those players miss Sunday’s game, Cleveland can still cause problems for New York, as they still have Isaiah McGuire, Maliek Collins and Jared Verse.
The Jets’ offensive line has been inconsistent through the first four weeks.
Starting left guard Dylan Parham has been the team’s best pass-blocker , per PFF , earning a 75.9 grade. However, he’s unlikely to play after missing the first two practices. Jordan Meredith has filled in over the past two weeks, but the five-year veteran has struggled, allowing two sacks and seven pressures across 40 pass-blocking snaps.
Left tackle Olu Fashanu hasn’t been any better, allowing five sacks and 11 pressures. If the Jets can’t improve their protection against Cleveland, then it could be another long day for quarterback Geno Smith.
To limit Cleveland’s pass rush, offensive coordinator Frank Reich must give Fashanu extra help on the left side, using a tight end, like Jelani Woods, or a running back to chip the edge rushers.
New York could also make life easier by establishing the run after struggling to do so over the last few weeks. This would keep the offense balanced, prevent predictable passing situations, and take the pressure off Smith.
Reich also needs to get the ball out of Smith’s hands faster. A mix of quick passes, screens, and play-actions would make life easier on the offensive line and create opportunities to attack downfield.

title: 3 Changes Frank Reich Must Make to Turn Jets' Offense Around Before It's Too Late
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. — Inconsistent. That's probably the best word to describe the Jets' offense through the first four games of the season. In some games, like Week 3 against the Lions, the offense looks solid. In other contests, like last week against the Bears, the offense failed to produce much of everything.
For offensive coordinator Frank Reich, the stats highlight a poor overall group.
New York ranks as the 25th-best offense in the league and the sixth-worst rushing attack in the game. The Jets' passing unit is ranked in the top 10, but failing to pick up a third-down conversion last week was another example of the recent frustration.
If the numbers show a struggling team, the tape only enhances those same issues.
For Reich and the offense, there are three things that the unit needs to fix going into Week 5's clash with the Browns. Otherwise, it will be another year in which the Jets fail to put up an offense inside the top 20.
After last week's abysmal performance , the Jets' offense dropped to fourth-worst in the NFL on third down. They saw many third-and-short opportunities against the Bears but even failed to pick those up.
For Reich, the reason for it is simple, he has to be better as a play-caller.
"I'm ultimately responsible for that," Reich said. "We had two short fields that yielded six points, and I think if that yields more than that, it allows us to apply a little bit more pressure than we did."
There are different reasons why a team fails to convert on third down. Some plays could start with a breakdown in blocks along the offensive line. A bad pass here, a missed read there and everyone always tends to have a hand in third-down struggles.
But when everyone is at fault, then it becomes a coaching issue. Reich needs to make sure his guys are more buttoned-up going forward.
The Jets have loved Braelon Allen for years now . His size as a 6'2", 250-pound running back makes him an intriguing weapon for any offense. The problem for him is that he hasn't been productive.
Sunday's loss in Chicago was his best game, rushing 14 times for 59 yards and a 4.2-yard-per-carry average. Meanwhile, Isaiah Davis didn't receive a touch on Sunday .
New York's fascination with Allen or Davis has never truly made sense, especially when production between the two couldn't be further apart. While Allen has recorded a career yard-per-carry average of 3.7, Davis has averaged over 5.6 per opportunity.
In short, Davis is more efficient and more productive, even if the Jets won't play him.
With Breece Hall still dealing with a quad injury, the Jets must give up this idea of Allen being the team's lead back. He isn't efficient enough to do it. Davis must receive touches going forward.
New York is without Hall, AD Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. Four of the team's top six targets have missed games over the last few weeks .
The easiest way to put up points is to get the ball to the other top targets: Garrett Wilson and Kenyon Sadiq. Getting the ball to your better players is an excellent way of keeping teams that may have more talent than you in bind.
Instead, Reich chose to focus his efforts last week on getting the ball to Allen, who, as we've mentioned, has never shown an ability to carry an offense on his own. Allen saw 16 touches in last week's game. Wilson and Sadiq combined for eight.
Inexcusable, yet Reich tried to do it.
Was that the problem? Just not converting on third down? Or was featuring a backup running back at all a bigger issue?
Good teams stay good because they get the ball to their best players and let them use their talent to succeed. Bad teams try to outsmart the good teams and, in turn, end up costing themselves.
The Jets are a bad team right now, and they will stay bad as long as Reich thinks he can outsmart other coaches.

title: Jets Friday Notebook Week 5: Key Injury Updates, Nahshon Wright's Outlook & More
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. — The Jets need a win, and fast.
At 1-3, the organization has little wiggle room to remain competitive this season. They also happen to be walking into a home contest this weekend against the 3-1 Browns in what is expected to be rainy weather. According to AccuWeather, there is a 94% chance that rain from Tropical Rainstorm Isaias will impact the East Rutherford weather on Sunday.
At practice on Friday, the Jets shifted their focus to the Browns with some key notes along the way.
So let's open up the notebook and see what fans should know heading into the weekend.
There's good news and bad news when it comes to the Jets' injury front.
The good news is that starting tight end Mason Taylor is expected to play on Sunday after missing the last two games with an injury. He will be a welcome addition to the offense heading into Week 5. Jarvis Brownlee and Kingsley Enagbare are also expected to practice today and could be in line to start on Sunday.
In the case of Adonai Mitchell, the team also believes he could eventually get back to practice next week with a finger injury that did not require surgery, according to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn.
But is the finger broken? A sprain? No one seems to know . All Glenn will say is that no procedure was done.
"(Adonai is) progressing faster than we thought that he would," Glenn said. "Once we got to the end of it of knowing exactly what the prognosis was when it comes to his finger."
That said, the likes of running back Breece Hall, Mitchel, and left guard Dylan Parham will all miss Sunday's action against the Browns due to their slate of injuries. Glenn did seem hopeful they could also return to the practice field next week, but they are not making any promises or clear expectations.
The Jets signed Nahshon Wright this past offseason to help fix a secondary that was one of the worst in the league last year. Wright was coming off a Pro Bowl season in Chicago, and his ball-hawking abilities were seen as a positive for a Jets team that failed to record an interception the previous year.
So far this season, though, Wright hasn't played . In fact, New York has made him a healthy scratch in the last two weeks, leaving some to wonder whether his time in Gotham is already nearing its end .
On Friday, Glenn broke down exactly why Wright has been on the outside looking in. While the Jets brought him in to help fix the defense, the cornerback room has played a lot better than anyone could have previously predicted.
Glenn is correct. Stephens and Thomas are both ranked as top-20 cornerbacks in the league in pass coverage. Stephens, specifically, is in the top 15. The development of their outside corners has been a small positive for the 1-3 Jets.
While Glenn did say Wright will eventually see the field, barring injury or poor play, it's hard to pinpoint exactly where at this time.
Every coach looks at the NFL season in quarters. The first four games of the year are the "first quarter" of a season, and so on. Glenn confirmed that's exactly how he looks at where the Jets are going forward.
Even if they were bad in the "first quarter" of the year.
"I think it helps to look at it in that aspect," Glenn said. "Knowing that we're 1-3 this quarter, we have another quarter to be able to see how we improve on that. I think sometimes it makes it easy to just condense the season into that, so guys can stay just pinpointed and focused on it. Also, I think it's important you just look at each game and just go from there."
As the Jets prepare for the second quarter of the season, they will have three games against teams that didn't make the playoffs last season. The Browns, Dolphins and Raiders are all teams that the Jets need to beat in order to keep their season alive.
And at the end of the day, if they can win the second and third quarter of the year, it may put them in better standing moving forward.
Part of that switch, though, is getting the team to start fast. New York has found themselves in offensive holes over the last few weeks, and it's something the team is working to correct.
"Just for the psyche of your team, just for the fans and all that, it's obviously pretty good to be able to do that," Glenn said.
While Gang Green's psyche is poor right now, it's even worse for the fans. If the Jets want to show they have grown as an organization, Sunday is as much of a must-win as ever .

title: Jets Share Another Cryptic Adonai Mitchell Injury Update: What Exactly Is Going On?
full_text:
The Jets are working hard as they prepare for a Week 5 clash with the Browns , hoping to end their losing streak at three games. Head coach Aaron Glenn will need all hands on deck to overcome a 3-1 Cleveland team that has exceeded expectations, which is why No. 2 wide receiver Adonai Mitchell's health has been a hot topic among New York fans in the lead-up to Sunday.
After all, Mitchell missed Weeks 3 and 4 with a mysterious hand injury the Jets have bizarrely been cryptic about—even after he was spotted in practice last month with a heavily taped hand (h/t Sleeper NFL). All Glenn told fans was that Mitchell's finger got caught in a teammate's jersey during practice and that it wasn't broken, opting not to detail an official diagnosis.
Fast-forward to Week 5, and the mystery continues: Mitchell will miss Sunday's contest against the Browns, according to ESPN 's Rich Cimini on Friday. The situation became even more frustrating when Glenn seemingly admitted to not knowing "if it’s a sprain or fracture," per Cimini, and that surgery wasn't required.
Aaron Glenn continues to be evasive with regard to AD Mitchell’s finger injury. Wouldn’t say if it’s a sprain or fracture, suggesting he doesn’t know. Says there was no surgical procedure. Adds, “He’s progressing faster than we thought.” This will be Mitchell’s third missed game.…
Even though Glenn added that Mitchell is "progressing faster than we thought," that kind of update doesn't exactly mean much when the Jets have been considerably mum on the situation.
Injuries happen, and some are harder to diagnose than others. That said, the Jets have had over two weeks to explain exactly what's going on with Mitchell, yet nothing concrete has come out. It especially isn't encouraging when Glenn sounds like not even he knows what's happening. You'd think that enough imaging would be done by now to determine what's going on.
Did Mitchell's injury look like it'd heal quickly only for him to suffer a setback? Are the Jets worried that the situation is worse than it is? Do they regret not putting him on injured reserve as soon as the issue popped up?
Those are all pressing (and valid) questions stewing in the minds of Jets fans, making it clear that Glenn & Co.'s cryptic ways aren't doing anyone any favors.
Earlier in the week, Cimini discussed Mitchell's injury on Monday's edition of the "Jets Collective" podcast, saying he "would not shock me if we find out that (Adonai) had surgery." Obviously, Glenn said that wasn't the case on Friday, but the fact that the ESPN insider hasn't even seen Mitchell around team facilities only adds to the fear about how severe his injury is.
Sports fans need transparency from the front office and coaching staff, no matter how unfortunate a player's injury situation is. The Jets' faithful especially deserve that, after all they've been through over the last decade and a half. If Glenn and general manager Darren Mougey want to be seen as the right people to turn Gang Green around, they can't let situations like Mitchell's injury snowball into an avoidable avalanche.
Regardless of the sparse details regarding Mitchell's injury, the fact is that—no matter why—the Jets will be without their No. 2 WR on Sunday afternoon.
Naturally, that means Garrett Wilson should see more volume than the four targets he saw last week, after commanding 13 in the previous game. Isaiah Williams also has some momentum after scoring his first touchdown on a 58-yard reception last week, and Tim Patrick could be coming off IR after his practice window opened on Wednesday .
The Jets are still waiting to see more production from former taxi squad wideouts Malik McClain and Jamaal Pritchett, who haven't been targeted yet. There's also a good chance that Sterling Shepard will be elevated from the practice squad for the third time, with Tyler Johnson as another option waiting in the wings. That's without even mentioning the expanded action the tight end room could see, especially with Mason Taylor potentially returning to reform New York's talented 1-2 punch at TE with Kenyon Sadiq.
The Browns are off to a strong start, but their defense hasn't been perfect, and a 55.7 grade on PFF (T-26th) drives that home. Despite being shorthanded, the Jets' offense must capitalize on every chance it gets to put up points, or else any hope of looking like a competitive team this year could slip through their grasp.
In the meantime, let's hope the next update on Adonai Mitchell's status isn't as cryptic and makes it clear what New York fans can expect next for the 24-year-old receiver.

title: 3 Most Likely Will McDonald IV Trade Destination as His Jets Outlook Remains Unclear
full_text:
Through the first four games of the 2026 NFL season, Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV has been a clear disappointment . He has tallied one sack but has been nonexistent for a majority of the year, both in run defense and in getting after the quarterback. He went from having five pressures and a sack in the season opener to four sackless pressures in the last three games.
Not good for a first-round pick in need of a new deal.
If the Jets continue to keep losing, they will seemingly need to give away some of their talent on expiring contracts in order to accumulate more draft capital. McDonald may have an additional year of team control, but it's clear he's not in New York's long-term plans , potentially putting him on the move before the 2026 NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
And that could make McDonald attractive to at least three times around the league.
The Panthers have been ravaged by injuries, but they remain the one team that seemingly is competent enough on offense to win the NFC South again. In order to do so, they'll need to address some key areas along the defensive line.
Currently, Carolina ranks third worst in the league in pressure rate. Their eight sacks are also among the lowest in the league as well. If the Panthers want not only to get to the playoffs but also to find a way to win, they'll need to provide some semblance of a pass rush.
The potential acquisition of McDonald may put the team closer to some of the other playoff contenders in the NFC than people realize. The Panthers are good this year. They need a pass rusher like McDonald to put them over the hump.
With the NFC East in a state of flux, the Cowboys seem like the one team that actually has the pieces to win the division by default now, even if they fell to the then-winless Buccaneers on Thursday Night Football. Dallas still needs help on defense, though, especially when it comes to getting after the passer, currently owning the eighth-worst pass-rush grade (61.5) on Pro Football Focus .
The Cowboys have some concerns about stopping the run, but since trading Micah Parsons , they have clearly taken a step back when it comes to getting after the quarterback. McDonald is no Parsons, but he could provide an immediate boost to the group going into the later parts of the season.
Don't let their 4-0 record fool you: the 49ers are banged up across the roster. Despite that, the team is undefeated and playing inspired football. They do need some extra edge-rusher help as they go for a run at the championship.
McDonald has struggled so far this season, but he should be someone who can get after the quarterback at a consistent level. Outside of Nick Bosa, the 49ers could use extra players to aid in their defense when going against the Cowboys or Rams.
This seems like a fair deal for both sides as New York would want fair compensation in the draft.

title: Eagles-Jaguars Stock Report: Nick Sirianni Takes Accountability for Late-Game Collapse
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles suffered a disappointing 19-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday in London, dropping their third straight game in a dramatic finish at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Philadelphia, missing Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith while dealing with a patchwork offensive line, built a 14-7 halftime lead on a Will Shipley two-yard touchdown run and a 62-yard catch-and-run score from Jalen Hurts to Darius Cooper.
The offense then stalled completely after the break, managing just three second-half points, while rushing for a dismal 2 yards on 18 carries and finishing with 232 total yards against Jacksonville’s 408-yard output.
Trevor Lawrence threw for 331 yards and two touchdowns (both to Parker Washington), including a 27-yard fourth-down score that put the Jaguars ahead 16-14 late in the game. Cam Little missed the ensuing extra point, thanks to a backup long snapper, allowing Jake Elliott’s 48-yard field goal with eight seconds remaining to give the Eagles a 17-16 lead.
However, Ameer Abdullah returned the kickoff 53 yards to the Philadelphia 38-yard line, setting up Little’s game-winning 57-yard field goal as time expired. Nick Sirianni took the accountability afterward, saying he “lost us that game."
The Game-Wrecker: Jalen Carter set the tone with a first half for the ages against a pedestrian Jacksonville interior offensive line. The gifted Eagles' defensive tackle has two sacks, two forced fumbles, three tackles for loss, five pressures, and three run stops.
That's an NFC Defensive Player of the Month performance in 30 minutes of football and a signal that the Jaguars were in for a fight despite the game being dubbed an early Super Bowl contender vs. an injury-depleted mess.
Third-down life: The Eagles entered the contest having failed on their last 17 third-down attempts, dating back to Week 3 vs. Chicago. On Sunday in London, they converted their first third-down when Jalen Hurts found Dallas Goedert for a 5-yard gain on a third-and-three play.
Goedert missed the past two games with an MCL injury, and his presence was comforting for Hurts, who trusts the veteran tight end. Overall, Philadelphia finished 6-for-15 on third down. They also started 4-for-6 before finishing 2-for-9, so it's not all peaches and cream, but an incremental improvement.
Young o-linemen: The thought of center Jake Majors and left guard Willie Lampkin making their first NFL starts, and right tackle Markel Bell making his second start, was projected as too much to overcome.
However, all three took their opportunities and battled. It wasn't always pretty, but the trio played well enough for the Eagles' offense to operate in a similar fashion to what it usually does. The play was good enough to win, as evidenced by holding the lead with eight seconds remaining.
Missed Opportunity: After playing well in Week 4 as a replacement for All-Pro Zack Baun, who could not get through the concussion protocol, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. was set to start again. With Baun back, Trotter was going to start for the struggling Jihaad Campbell, who missed some practice time with a knee issue.
However, Trotter was tossed from the game on the opening kickoff, as he and linebacker Bryan Thomas Jr. were ejected for scuffling. It was way too heavy-handed by the officials, but Trotter can't put himself in that position. Campbell ended up playing the whole game next to Baun, indicating that his potential benching wasn't fully injury-related.
.500: The Eagles fell to 2-3 with Sunday's loss, making it the first time since 2021 that the franchise has been underwater during the regular season. Philadelphia isn't used to being in this position, which will make Howie Roseman's approach at the trade deadline even more interesting.
More injuries: You can add to the Eagles' injury list with two more notable contributors: Will Shipley and edge defender Jalyx Hunt.
Shipley, who was starting because Barkley and Tank Bigsby were both out, left with a foot injury in the second quarter and didn't return.
Hunt went down on the last play of the first half with what was described as an ankle and knee issue. After the game, he was seen by reporters in a walking boot, and the early concern is a high ankle sprain and an MCL issue, according to an NFL source. If that's the case, Hunt will be out for multiple weeks.
Kickoff coverage/end of game management: The kickoff coverage looked leaky from the opening kick, which was taken to the house by the Jaguars and wiped out by multiple penalties.
With eight seconds remaining after Elliott kicked a 48-yard field goal to seemingly steal the game, Philly kicked it to Ameer Abdullah, instead of playing it safe with a touchback. He returned it 53 yards and gave Little an opportunity from 57. Even with a backup long snapper who was wild high all day, the strong-legged Little was true.
It's also fair to highlight the two plays before Elliott's FG: an incompletion and a completion to Makai Lemon, where the rookie receiver went out of bounds. The Eagles' failure to force the Jags to use their final timeout there enabled them to use it to secure the eight seconds Abdullah and Little needed to play the heroes.
The travel narrative: The Eagles left South Philadelphia late Friday at 10:45 p.m. ET. The idea was to get to London, which is about a seven-hour flight and five hours ahead of the East Coast, in the middle of the day, power through Saturday, and keep the body clocks as normal as possible. The plan was developed with the understanding that the Eagles have to come back next week and host Carolina on Sunday, so it was essentially a two-week plan. None of it impacted the game, despite many trying to shoehorn it as a potential issue before kickoff.

title: Nick Sirianni Owns Up to Poor, Late-Game Decision Making in Loss to Jaguars
full_text:
Nick Sirianni blew it. He knew it, too, and admitted it.
“I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game,” said the Eagles coach after his team lost for a third straight time, this time to the Jacksonville Jaguars, 19-17, in Week 5. “...The guys fought so hard, and then I didn't make the decision that I should have made at the end of the game, and I cost us that game, and I put that fully on me.”
He could have owned up to a pair of mistakes in the game’s dying seconds.
First, his decision not to let Jake Elliott kick the ball into the end zone after Elliott’s 48-yard field goal gave the Eagles a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left in the game. With no timeouts, the Jags would have needed one play to get into field goal range.
Ameer Abdullah took the short kick gift and raced 52 yards, allowing for one more play: a 57-yard field goal attempt by Cam Little, which he made as time expired.
Second, for his decision not to drain more of the game clock after the Eagles’ offense somehow showed a spark of life and made a first down at the Jaguars’ 34 with 25 seconds left, trailing 16-14.
The Eagles were already in Elliott’s field-goal range at that point. He's been hot so far this season, making two 50-plus-yard kicks in two attempts. Instead of running the ball once or twice, two passes were dialed up. The first was incomplete, stopping the clock. The second went to Makai Lemon, who ran an out pattern and got out of bounds after picking up seven yards, again stopping the clock.
Finally, the Eagles ran the ball. The play lost three yards, and the Jaguars called their final timeout, something they might have done if the Eagles had run on first or second down. That would have meant the Eagles could have run their field goal unit out to attempt the kick as the clock wound down to under five seconds. By not doing that, there was still time on the clock to do what Jacksonville did.
“I'm prepared as a quarterback to not worry about those things,” quarterback Jalen Hurts told reporters when asked if he would have done anything differently in those final 25 seconds. “I'm honoring the play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game. When I'm up at night, yeah, I think about them. Should I have said something or should I have took a step back and said, ‘Wait?’ Ultimately, there's a commitment to that and going out there and executing. And this was one where it did not work in our favor.”
But the decision not to kick off into the end zone was coaching negligence. There’s a time and place to trust your tacklers on kickoff coverage, but this wasn’t the time or place.
The Jags opened the game with a kickoff return for a touchdown, but it was called back on a holding penalty. Additionally, t he Eagles were without more than half a dozen injured players , including one of their top special teams tacklers, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. , who was ejected on the opening kickoff.
The players charged with tackling Abdullah, Kelee Ringo, Jonathan Jones, and Arnold Ebiketie had no chance.
“It sucks,” Elliott told reporters after the heartbreaking loss. “I mean, you come all this way, you think you're in the driver's seat to win a big game and now we're feeling pretty down.”
So, Sirianni stood before the players in the postgame locker room and let them know this loss was on him.
“I think it's so important for every person to take accountability, because that's the only way you get better,” said the coach. “You build trust that way. … just sick the way that went, and my decision went there."
These two decisions could haunt the Eagles for the remainder of the season and could ultimately lead to Sirianni getting fired if the season doesn’t end with a playoff game.

title: 5 Winners, 5 Losers, & More From Eagles' Heartbreaking 19-17 Loss to the Jaguars
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles’ special teams won it. Then lost it.
Jake Elliott kicked a 48-yard field goal with eight seconds left, but a breakdown in the Eagles special teams’ kickoff coverage led to a 57-yard game-winner from Cam Little as time expired, giving the Jacksonville Jaguars a 19-17 Week 5 win in London .
Say what you want about all the injuries the Eagles have endured this season, but it's been their offense’s inability to do anything – nothing, really - in the second half that has led to this losing streak. The Eagles have scored just three second-half points in the last three games. The three they got from Elliott looked like they would win the game, but it wasn't to be.
The Eagles barely get first downs over the final two quarters. That ineptitude has left their defense hung out to dry and gassed when the fourth quarter arrives.
The loss dropped the Eagles to 2-3. It is the first time they are below .500 since 2021, which was Nick Sirianni’s first year as the head coach. It’s an amazing stat, as is the team’s second-half scoring drought.
The Eagles’ outing wasn’t without effort, especially in the first half as they forged a 14-7 lead, scoring two touchdowns, which were the first two first-half TDs the Jaguars allowed all season.
The Eagles, who didn't have superstars DeVonta Smith and Saquon Barkley, will host the Panthers next Sunday and entertain the Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Week 7.
Let’s get to some winners and losers:
Jalen Carter: The defensive tackle had an NFC East Defensive Player of the Week performance. He dominated in the first half, sacking Trevor Lawrence twice and forcing a fumble on both, though the Jaguars recovered both. He had four tackles, including three for loss.
Darius Cooper: Last year’s undrafted free agent ran a great route to get wide open, and Jalen Hurts hit him in stride for a 62-yard touchdown, giving the Eagles a 14-7 lead with 5:36 to play in the second quarter, which was the difference at halftime. He now has four touchdowns on the season .
DARIUS COOPER 62 YARDS!!! pic.twitter.com/TTJayV78mF
Willie Lampkin: The shortest player to start on the offensive line in an NFL game in a long, long time, the 5-foot-11 left guard paved the way on Will Shipley’s two-yard touchdown run to tie the score in the first quarter.
Quinyon Mitchell: The Eagles' defense made two defensive stands, and the cornerback was involved in both. The first was at the goal line, when he broke up a third-down throw in the end zone on a pass from the 1-yard line in the dying seconds of the first half.
Mitchell also recorded his first career regular-season pick later in the game. However, a failed fourth-down conversion by the Eagles' offense gave the Jags good field position late in the third quarter.
Eagles fans: Very few fan bases travel as well as Philly’s. They took over Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, booing the Jaguars, who aren’t used to that because they were the home team and play in London every year. It sounded and looked like a home game at Lincoln Financial Field.
Special teams: There's no way you can give up a 52-yard kickoff return to Ameer Abdullah with eight seconds left, putting the Jaguars in position to win, but Michael Clay’s kickoff return team did just that. Why not kick the ball into the end zone? With no timeouts and eight seconds left, the Jaguars would have had to do something heroic to get into field position.
Sean Mannion: He’s the offensive coordinator, so he has to bear the brunt of the miserable failures of the second half. With an offensive line in disarray and starting young players, why not use Carson Steele as a fullback, giving the offense an extra blocker in the run game? The Eagles ran for a minuscule 22 yards.
Jonathan Greenard: The outside linebacker missed five games last year with a shoulder injury that required surgery. He already had a pec strain and now has an ankle injury. After much pregame discussion, it was determined Greenard couldn’t play. His loss was particularly glaring when Jalyx Hunt needed help to get off the field with an injury on the last play of the first half.
Greenard has played 37 snaps so far this season. The Eagles made a big investment in him , signing him to a four-year extension for nearly $100 million, which hasn’t paid dividends -- yet.
Andrew Mukuba: Vic Fangio keeps saying he is happy with how the second-year safety has been playing, but sometimes his play speaks otherwise. For example, Mukuba was beaten badly on a short throw to Parker Washington, a sixth-round pick out of Penn State three years ago, which led to a 51-yard touchdown for Jacksonville.
Parker Washington just keeps making plays. @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/swaHaZV4sI
Jeremiah Trotter Jr.'s ejection: This goes to the official. Trotter appeared to be pancaking Bryan Thomas Jr. on the opening kickoff, then Thomas used both legs to kick Trotter as he rolled to the ground. Not sure how either player was ejected, but it was a big loss for the Eagles, who were set to start Trotter ahead of Jihaad Campbell.

title: Eagles' Dameon Pierce Has a Strong Benefactor in Nick Sirianni
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Dameon Pierce has arrived on the Eagles’ 53-man roster and could be a major contributor during Sunday’s game in London against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
The veteran running back has a strong benefactor in Philadelphia head coach Nick Sirianni.
The Eagles promoted the former Houston Texan off their practice squad this week. The move comes as injury thins the backfield—Saquon Barkley was ruled out Friday with a hamstring issue and backup Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve with a core muscle injury—leaving Pierce and Will Shipley as the healthy options behind an offense that needs production on the ground.
Asked what steered him back to Philadelphia after he was a victim on the initial cut to 53, Pierce did not hesitate. “ Nick Sirianni, ” he said, laughing, before explaining why.
“He’s a great guy. He’s vibrant. He loves the game of football. He loves what he does. And this locker room, to gel, we all gotta have good relationships,” Pierce said.
Sirianni returned the sentiment of Friday when asked about his relationship with Pierce by Eagles On SI.
The coach said the Eagles had tracked Pierce since he came out of Florida.
“There’re a lot of guys [in the draft] you end up loving that it’s like, ‘Oh man, he’s going to be good for them,’” Sirianni said. “I think it all started back then, and just like I said, it’s fun being around him. He brings constant energy to the football team. He’s obviously a very talented player and works extremely hard and runs extremely hard."
“I’m excited for his opportunity.”
That opportunity has been a long time coming. Pierce burst onto the scene as a rookie in 2022, rushing for 939 yards and four touchdowns on 220 carries for the Texans while adding 30 receptions for 165 yards. He was one of the league’s more productive first-year backs.
What followed was a steep drop: 416 yards in 2023, a reduced role and injuries (including ankle, hamstring and shoulder issues) in the years after, and only 26 yards on 10 carries in four games in 2025 before Houston waived him.
Pierce said the years of limited snaps were navigated with prayer and mental toughness.
“Being in this game, you gotta have a lot of mental strength, on the field and off the field,” he said. “Just finding that happy medium to where you can go and just control what you can control and be ready when the time is, for sure has helped.”
Pierce described the recent promotion as everything he has been working toward.
“Just having a lot of the mental toughness I had over the last few years, you know, probably not going the way I wanted it, but I’m all about timing,” Pierce said. “Just making sure I’m prepared on that field, making sure I’m ready to carry the torch for my guy.”
For Eagles fans who have not seen much of him, Pierce offered a short self-portrait: a down-to-earth player from South Georgia with humble roots, who tries to be detailed and explosive.
“I just try to bring the game to the defense, not try to let them dictate my game speed. If it’s there, take it. If not, wait on it,” he said.
Whether that translates into early-down work against one of the league’s better run defenses remains to be seen.
What is clear is that Pierce has been preparing for his second chance and Sirianni is excited to provide it for him.

title: Bringing in Andy Dalton Was a Mistake, One Howie Roseman Admitted When He Cut Him
full_text:
Andy Dalton was a mistake. Right from the very start, trading a seventh-round pick for the veteran quarterback just seven months ago made little sense then and even less now after general manager Howie Roseman admitted to the error by cutting Dalton before he was able to get on a plane to London for Week 5.
Why it took so long, only Roseman knows. Why he did it in the first place, only he knows.
The Eagles already had a capable backup in Tanner McKee and you knew they were going to take one in the draft after the QB they took in the 2025 draft, Kyle McCord, fled to Green Bay and then was traded to the Miami, where he serves as the backup to Malik Willis on the still-winless Dolphins.
And Roseman did, selecting Cole Payton in the fifth round. But it gets weirder.
The Eagles allowed Dalton and McKee to battle to be the backup. McKee, who is in the final year of his contract, was a good soldier about the battle, noting that every year you have to compete for your job.
The question of who Jalen Hurts’ top backup would be was a topic all summer. Head coach Nick Sirianni allowed it to remain an issue—and a distraction to a point—by not naming the backup even after the 53-man roster was set. It wasn't until the morning of the season opener that there was any clarity on who would be the No. 2.
Even the decision to keep four quarterbacks on the 53-man-roster was strange, especially because they had to part ways with Cam Latu, Cameron Williams, and others who had a better chance of helping this team than Dalton.
But they didn’t want to cut Payton and try to get him to the practice squad because they were apparently afraid another team would poach him.
Dalton’s resume was longer than McKee's. He had played in 179 games, with 169 starts, over 15 years. The Eagles were his sixth team. He threw one pass in his short stint in Philly. A Bears rookie safety intercepted it in the end zone.
The Eagles drafted McKee. They knew more about him from being up close with him than Dalton. McKee was a sixth-round pick in 2023. He made two starts, going 1-1. He played in six games and threw five touchdowns to just one interception.
It was a strange thing to watch him have to fight for his job. The Eagles could have saved a seventh-round pick next year and not traded for Dalton.
Granted, neither looked good this summer, and now Payton is an injury to Hurts and another one to McKee from being a starter. The way this season has gone, with one injury after another to key players, would it surprise anyone if that scenario eventually plays out?
Still, it was the wrong move, and a weird one to bring in Dalton. At least Roseman admitted it, even if it took four weeks of the regular season for him to do it.

title: 3 Eagles Lineup Decisions I'd Make If I Was Nick Sirianni in Week 5
full_text:
Nick Sirianni and the Philadelphia Eagles are outgunned and outmanned walking into London for a Week 5 showdown against the Jacksonville Jaguars. They are without eight starters going into Sunday . That's over a third of the team's starting lineup from Week 1.
As the Eagles offense tries to put pieces together, Sirianni is under pressure to try and get things right across the board. Going into Week 5, though, the Eagles should make three roster moves ahead of kickoff.
Philadelphia hasn't gotten the kind of quality play at safety compared to the last several years. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has said he doesn't want to move nickel corner Cooper DeJean to safety, but the Eagles do have a contingency plan in place to make that happen. Kenny Moore was one of the better cornerbacks in the slot for a very long time.
If he is up to the task, he could shift to nickel, and that would allow DeJean to roam around the defense and secure the backend of Philadelphia's secondary. There has been precedent as well. Kyle Hamilton is considered the best safety in the league but actually played in the slot for several years to try and help Baltimore's secondary.
DeJean isn't a natural safety, but his skill set and versatility could put him in that same boat.
Philadelphia is operating out of 11 personnel (or one tight end on the field) over 70% of the time this season. That needs to be even higher going forward. The Eagles are better at giving their offensive line space to operate in 11 personnel compared to the condensed look that comes with a second tight end on the field.
With so many backups now starting this season, Philadelphia needs to be able to run the ball effectively. Shortening the field has done nothing for them over the last few seasons.
They need to get their best players out in space. On Sunday, that's exactly how they can move the ball.
The jury is out. The Eagles have struggled mightily against the blitz all season far. A big part of that is due to the fact that the team has struggled with their offensive line's health for most of the start of the season.
The best remedy to any blitz is to get the ball out quickly. It's also something that the Eagles and Hurts have struggled to do over the last few years. In last week's loss to the Rams, Philadelphia saw several short throws batted at the line of scrimmage.
Against a Jaguars defense that is among the most opportunistic units in the league, the Eagles need Hurts to get the ball out quick and let their receivers start making plays after the catch.

title: Eagles' Injury Analysis: Banged-Up Offense Faces Tough Test vs. Jaguars
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — The Eagles leave for London Friday night for Sunday’s Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars without arguably their two best offensive players.
Friday’s final injury report made the absences of running back Saquon Barkley and receiver DeVonta Smith, who are both dealing with hamstring injuries.
Barkley missed every practice this week after being limited to four snaps in last week’s loss to the Los Angeles Rams. The RB1’s absence is further amplified by backup Tank Bigsby’s core muscle surgery forcing a stint on injured reserve.
To deal with that, the Eagles promoted Dameon Pierce from the practice squad earlier in the week, and made the same decision with Carson Steele on Friday.
Pierce and Steele provide support for Will Shipley with Pierce likely serving as the main complement to Shipley on offense, and Steele helping to handle some of Shipley’s typical work on special teams.
Smith was ruled out for a second consecutive game. There is some good news with Dontayvion Wicks practicing Friday and not being given a game status despite failing to finish Thursday’s practice with his own hamstring issue. That likely means the WRs in 11 personnel will again be Wicks, Makai Lemon, and Darius Cooper, although it’s conceivable Wicks’ workload will be lessened.
The other major issue is center Drew Kendall, who was unable to practice this week with a knee injury and officially ruled out Friday. Jake Majors, was promoted from the practice squad Friday, and is expected to handle the pivot against the Jags.
A natural center, Majors started a program record 56 games at the University of Texas, all of them at OC. The line from left to right is set to be Jordan Mailata, Willie Lampkin, Majors, Tyler Steen and Markel Bell. If that holds it will be the first NFL starts for Lampkin and Majors and just the second for Bell, the rookie third-round pick tasked with replacing Lane Johnson.
That complicates matters for quarterback Jalen Hurts, who popped up on the practice report with a calf injury, although the QB1 was a full participant and given no game status. It’s fair to question whether Hurts will have his typical mobility in game where he will need it, however.
WR Hollywood Brown (ankle) and safety Marcus Epps (groin) are also ruled out for the Eagles.
Edge defender Jonathan Greenard was unable to practice this week with an ankle injury but was listed as questionable, an indication the veteran will make the trip to London with the idea of being a game-time decision.
There was better news elsewhere. Tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) is off the report after missing the last two games and is available, which should help offensive coordinator Sean Mannion better vary his personnel groupings.
Also, linebackers Zack Baun (concussion) and Jihaad Campbell (knee), cornerback Quinyon Mitchell (knee), offensive tackle Fred Johnson (knee) and tight end E.J. Jenkins (toe) are all cleared to play.
Philadelphia’s offense is already in a slide. Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 93 yards and took four sacks against the Rams, and he has averaged 4.7 yards per attempt since Week 3.
Sunday’s plan now runs through Shipley and Pierce on early downs, Goedert as the reliable target, and a patchwork line that lost Johnson to retirement and Cam Jurgens in a trade to Baltimore earlier this week.
The Jaguars are one of the better run defenses in the league, so the short-yardage and play-action game will be under stress.
Defensively, Baun and Mitchell have been the two best defenders this season so that bolsters things while Epps would likely be losing playing time to Michael Carter is he was healthy.
Having Greenard on the edge is key because Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith have failed to generate consistent pressure.

title: Why Eagles Howie Roseman Isn't Punting on 2026 Season by Trading Cam Jurgens
full_text:
Howie Roseman isn’t punting on the season. He leaves those duties to his punter, Braden Mann, on fourth down.
So, while it may appear the Eagles’ general manager is facing a fourth-and-long this season, especially after Lane Johnson retired and trading away his two-time Pro Bowl center, Cam Jurgens , to the Ravens, he isn’t in the business of giving away seasons.
In the last nine years, the GM has constructed three Super Bowl rosters, has won two Lombardi Trophies, and has gone to the playoffs in eight of those seasons, including a run of five straight postseason berths.
“As good as anyone in the National Football League,” Roseman told reporters earlier in the week. “I think that it's easy to just go to the negative, and I think that the reality of it is, is that we've had an unbelievable run of success, and we're planning to have another unbelievable run of success. And so, I think there is a little bit of a benefit of the doubt that we didn't all just lose our minds and forget how to do our jobs.”
As tough as it was, and will be, moving on from Jurgens along with a seventh-round pick in 2027, the GM made the right call.
It was all about the value he got back, which included a fifth-rounder next year and an all-important second-rounder in 2028. That gives the Eagles two first-round picks in 2028, including their own and the Patriots’ first-rounder in the trade of A.J. Brown , and two second-rounders, their own and now the Ravens’.
“We're trying to win every year, and we're always trying to retool and get better, and again, it's hard to get first- and second-round picks,” Roseman said. “They give you a lot of options. You can certainly use those on players and picks. You can trade up in drafts with those picks. You can use them for players, and we've done all those things. And I think one of the things that it gives us is flexibility.”
Jurgens was never the same player he was before his back surgery in the 2025 offseason. He may never be that player again.
For the Eagles, it’s easy to begin salivating now for the future.
The next two years are big for them in terms of expiring contracts. Having four picks in 2028 is huge because of the number of players who have expiring deals after that season, including:
Presumably, some of them will get extended. Others will not. New talent must be identified.
Again, some will be extended. Others won’t. The Eagles have seven picks in 2027, including a likely third-round compensatory pick for losing Jaelan Phillips this past offseason and the fifth-rounder they got from the Ravens in the Jurgens trade.
Roseman still has a month before the trade deadline to assess this year’s team, which faces a pivotal stretch of games coming up. After playing the Jaguars in London on Sunday, the Eagles will be home for three of their next four games, the final one of which is against the Giants at Lincoln Financial Field two days before the trade deadline.
If the Eagles haven’t shown any signs of life after that stretch, or some of the young players are slow to develop, then it might be time for Roseman to punt.
“I think nothing has changed in terms of our goals and when we're trying to win this year,” he said. “From my perspective, just looking at what is the ultimate goal, which is to win the last game of the year, and then to have a run like we've had. … you wanna have an extended run. My job is to look at how we can have sustained success for a long period of time.”

title: Next Man Up: Jake Majors Poised for First NFL Start as Musical Chairs on Eagles’ Offensive Line Continues
full_text:
For the third time this season, the Eagles are expected to have a different center. Jake Majors is set to make his first NFL start Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.
Majors, promoted to the 53-man roster from the practice squad on Friday, is the latest change on a depleted offensive line amid a cascade of injuries, a retirement, and a trade.
The Eagles (2-2) enter the Week 5 matchup after a turbulent week . All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired, Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens, and left guard Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve. Meanwhile, Drew Kendall, who took over OC duties from Jurgens in Week 3, was ruled out Friday after missing practice all week with a knee injury.
In the small portion of Thursday’s practice in South Philadelphia open to reporters, the makeshift O-Line from left to right was Jordan Mailata, Willie Lampkin, Majors, Tyler Steen and Markel Bell.
If that holds against the Jags, both Lampkin and Majors will be making their first NFL starts, and Bell will be in line for No. 2 after Johnson was a late scratch last week before informing the organization of his retirement decision early this week.
It’s been 82 years since the Eagles started three offensive linemen with one or fewer career starts.
Majors, a 24-year-old undrafted free agent originally signed by Tampa Bay out of Texas in 2025, spent most of his rookie season on the Eagles’ practice squad after a brief stint with the Bucs. He described that initial year as “rocky,” citing the steep leap from college to the NFL.
“Last year was rocky for me, for sure,” Majors said. “But to have confidence from the organization, they didn’t really know much of me, and they brought me in, and they were like, ‘Hey, listen, we want to see you develop.’"
“And now I’m here today having the opportunity to play. Like, it’s pretty cool. It’s a great experience. Very blessed.”
Majors credited the Eagles’ well-regarded developmental program, which is led by Connor Barwin, the former star edge rusher who is a rising star in the organization as the head of football development and strategy, as well as assistant offensive line coach Greg Austin.
“This program does a good job of the development, and I owe a credit to Connor Barwin and Greg Austin, guys that have been in my ear since I’ve gotten here and just instilling confidence into me,” Majors said. “Just keep showing up every day and getting better. And I think that’s allowed me to be in the position I am right now.”
Asked by Eagles On SI what was “rocky” about his intro to the NFL, Majors, who started a Longhorns program record 56 games, highlighted the intensity of facing professionals on every snap.
“Everybody you go against, whether it’s practice or games, preseason games that I’ve had so far, everybody’s there for a reason,” Majors explained. “They’re professionals. And so, just the mindset of there’s no plays off. Like, every play, someone’s out there to beat you, and it’s your job to protect your livelihood and make sure you get to stay here.”
Majors has prepared every week as if he were the starter, a habit that has not changed with the sudden opportunity.
His durability at Texas has been a foundation to his psyche as a player.
“Yeah, it just kind of shows my dependability and durability. Fifty-six games is a lot,” he said. “I know there’s people that have played in this league for longer, like Jordan Mailata, so, but to say that I’ve been able to do that and still be around and still continue to get better and having no complacency, I’m very proud of that.”
Mailata has served as a stabilizing force amid the upheaval this week.
“He’s been our anchor, man. He’s been the guy that’s kind of kept everybody in homeostasis and just like, ‘Hey, listen, like, this is what we have right now, and this is what we got to deal with, so how are we gonna react? How are we gonna respond?’” Majors said.
“And I think he’s been a great leader and just kind of, like I said, being our anchor and just keeping us still and being present in the moment.”

title: Eagles vs. Jaguars: Who Wins and Why in Week 5
full_text:
The Eagles have lost two in a row and sit at 2-2 as they get ready for a Week 5 game in London. It’s a long way to go to right the season. Adding to the difficulty are the Jacksonville Jaguars, who lead the AFC South at 3-1.
“We're early on in this season, and our job is to continue to find out what we do best, what we don't do quite as good, and try to attack that way,” said head coach Nick Sirianni. “…Our job in situations is not to panic; it's to find solutions. In those situations, the rest of the world could be panicking. We have to be able to look and find solutions.”
Here's a deeper look into Sunday's international matchup, and if the Eagles have what it takes to win.
Philly is a battered bunch, and it starts at receiver, where they could be without DeVonta Smith, Tay Wicks, and Hollywood Brown, and that won’t help them going against the Jags' 31st-ranked pass defense.
Jacksonville is second in the NFL at stopping the run, and the Eagles aren’t expected to have running backs Saquon Barkley or top backup Tank Bigsby, who was put on injured reserve earlier in the week. That leaves Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce.
The RB backups will be only as good as the offensive line, and that is in shambles after the stunning retirement of Lane Johnson and the surprising trade of Cam Jurgens .
The Eagles will likely have two players make their first NFL starts—Willie Lampkin at guard and Jake Majors at center, depending on the health of center/guard Drew Kendall, who is battling a knee injury. Even Kendall, however, has just four career starts. Rookie right tackle Markel Bell is expected to make just his second career start .
Vic Fangio’s defense played 83 snaps last week and 72 the week before, and now faces quarterback Trevor Lawrence, who is third in passer rating this season at 111.2, seventh in completion percentage at 69.2, and has eight touchdowns to just two interceptions.
“It has an effect,” said the DC, about the high number of snaps, “but we got to find a way to finish.”
The Eagles decided to wait until Friday to fly to the U.K. That doesn’t give them much time to adjust to the time change. The Jaguars are much more in tune with playing in London, since they do it every year; they left on Thursday.
It’s been eight years since the Eagles played a game in London. They beat the Jaguars that year, 24-16, at Wembley Stadium, but their top cornerback, Jalen Mills, suffered an injury and was lost for the rest of that season. Sunday’s game will be at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
Players have criticized the surface quality, pointing out issues such as deep dips or seams along the numbers and turf connections. Former Eagles practice squad player Lewis Cine tried to keep his career going after a compound fracture in his leg on that field, and the one-time first-round pick of the Vikings was never the same player.
Jacksonville has the league’s third- best third-down conversion rate, turning third downs into first downs 51.1 percent of the time. The Eagles’ defense is middle of the pack at stopping offenses on third down, getting stops just 40 percent of the time.
On offense, the Eagles didn’t convert a third down in 12 tries last week and are 0-for-17 dating back to a Monday night loss in Chicago. The Jaguars are a difficult third-down defense for the Eagles to get well against, ranking fifth in the league.

title: Steelers Need to Sign a WR
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need wide receiver help. Only a day ago, everyone was talking about this team not needing to look at the wide receiver trade market because of their young talent. Today, the group is depleted, and they desperately need help.
With the news that Roman Wilson is set to miss multiple weeks with a finger injury, the Steelers are left with DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard as their starters. Michael Pittman Jr. is on Injured Reserve with a foot injury, and Ben Skowronek also left Week 5 against the Indianapolis Colts, dealing with a calf injury.
So, right now, Pittsburgh's room is Metcalf, Bernard and rookie Kaden Wetjen. Wetjen is primarily a returner and hasn't played an offensive snap yet.
The team will likely call up Brandon Smith from the practice squad. Smith didn't record a catch against the Colts but was a training camp standout and a player Aaron Rodgers has shared his faith in multiple times.
"Well, B-Smith hasn't taken a ton of offensive reps. I've been around him for a few years. He was with us in New York, and always enjoyed him being on the fieldand his ability. I think he's a talented guy," Rodgers said after the Colts game.
"But we can play in 12 all day long, and if we need to, we will. But I was really proud of Germ the way he stepped in. There were a couple of plays with B-Smith. Like we had this play we're running inside zone, and we have this short motion to block the safety. Just by the end of the week it was just assumed that motion. I wasn't even calling it.
"I looked over, and I was, like, Oh, B has probably never done this. I was, like, Hey. He didn't know what I was thinking.
"So we were kind of making it up a little bit as we went there, but I'm proud of B-Smith. He's a smart guy and knows his stuff, and he'll be ready to take on a bigger role this week, I’m sure."
The team will likely need to explore their outside options, though. The name everyone will immediately think of is Tyreek Hill, but he's not the only veteran on the market. Two even have ties to the Steelers. And it'll come down to how big of a role the coaching staff is looking to fill with a signing.
If Mike McCarthy wants another starter-level player in the mix, Hill is the name to watch out for. The six-time All-Pro is 32-years-old and looking to play this season after suffering a dislocated knee in 2025. But he claims he's healthy, and if he is, he's easily the biggest name on the market.
If the Steelers are simply looking for a contributor to play behind Metcalf and Bernard , and in the mix with Smith, Skowronek and Wetjen, there are other names.
JuJu Smith-Schuster hasn't played in Pittsburgh since 2021, but spent the first five years of his career wearing the black and gold. The physical receiver is mostly a slot option at this point in his career, but could be a reliable set of hands for short-yardage situations and over the middle passes.
Gabe Davis is recovering from an ACL and may not be ready to play. But at 27 years old, he may be worth making a phone call to to check on his health heading into Week 6.
And then there are others; Ray-Ray McCloud is a player the Steelers' organization knows well. Curtis Samuel is somewhat of a mystery free agent, and maybe the biggest surprise to not be on a roster or practice squad somewhere. Mecole Hardman, Justin Watson, Josh Reynolds and others are still available as well.
It'll come down to Pittsburgh's perference. Whether or not they're looking for a bigger name or a fill-in while they wait for Wilson and Pittman Jr. How long they truly expect both to be out could play a significant role in their decision.
We don't know who yet, but expect someone. The Steelers certainly need another wide receiver before Week 6.

title: Steelers Bringing Back Hard-Hitting LB
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are set to bring in veteran linebacker Elandon Roberts with the intention of re-signing the 32-year-old, according to Steelers Now's Alan Saunders.
Roberts spent the end of training camp with the Steelers, rejoining the defense and defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, who coached him with the Las Vegas Raiders the year prior. He was the biggest surprise release of the final 53-man roster, being surpassed by Patrick Queen, Payton Wilson, Cole Holcomb and Carson Bruener in the final cuts.
Now, Roberts is set to return to the Steelers, where his presence is needed. Both Queen and Wilson have been under heavy criticism throughout the season for failing to be reliable inside linebacker options. Their struggles have shown the most in run support, which is where Roberts thrives.
It's unknown if Roberts will sign to the active roster or practice squad when he does ink a deal with the Steelers. Chances are, even if he does sign with the practice squad initially, the intention will be to bring him up to the active roster at some point.
Roberts is entering his 11th NFL season, starting 121 games and recording 694 tackles, 14.5 sacks and 60 tackles for loss.
The Steelers defense is trying to figure out their flaws as they approach the midway point of the season, but it's becoming more and more clear that their lack of talent at the inside linebacker room can't be solved without adding to the group. Queen and Wilson have spurts of quality play, but overall, both have struggled more than they've succeeded for the Steelers.
Meanwhile, Cole Holcomb hasn't been a reliable backup and has become more of a special teams contributor than defensive help.
Roberts should be able to come into the Steelers' lineup and help immediately. Whether he joins the starting group or not, his presence in the run game is something Pittsburgh desperately needs. His drive as a starter will also help, and his leadership is also something they can utilize as they try to keep things on track.
How the Steelers create a roster spot for Roberts is up in the air. Bruener is a key special teams contributor and will likely remain in that role for his second season. Holcomb could be a bubble player if the Steelers chose to replace their depth.
If not, Queen and Wilson are the names to watch. And with a starter-level player joining the group, anything is on the table.

title: Steelers Get Bad News on Roman Wilson's Injury
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers look like they're about to lose another one of their top wide receivers for a sustained period of time.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, Roman Wilson is expected to be out for a few weeks after suffering a finger injury at the end of the first half of the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
"Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a couple of weeks due to a finger injury suffered Sunday, per source," Fowler wrote on X . "He’s still gathering info and seeking a second opinion."
Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a couple of weeks due to a finger injury suffered Sunday, per source. He’s still gathering info and seeking a second opinion.
Pittsburgh is dealing with significant injury concerns across the board at wide receiver.
Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on the reserve/injured list on October 10 after aggravating his foot injury last week. The 29-year-old, who originally missed the team's Week 2 game against the New England Patriots, is dealing with plantar fasciitis and won't be back on the field until Week 10 at the absolute earliest.
Alongside Wilson, Ben Skowronek sustained a calf injury in the first half against Indianapolis and missed the rest of the contest from that point forward.
DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen are the only healthy receivers remaining on the 53-man roster. Brandon Smith was also active against the Colts, though he was a practice squad elevation .
The obvious short-term solution for the Steelers is to sign Smith to the 53-man roster.
The 27-year-old training camp standout played 16 snaps on offense vs. Indianapolis and has two practice squad elevations left, but there's now an opening for him on the 53-man roster.
Wetjen is strictly a kick returner and has yet to see the field on offense as a rookie, though, so Pittsburgh will have to make another move or two at receiver now that Wilson seems set to miss multiple games.
Bernard proved that he can start next to Metcalf by posting 80 yards on six catches against the Colts, and the Steelers have the luxury of being able to run a ton of 12 personnel with Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington at tight end, but they still need another real option at receiver.
Whether it's making an early trade nearly a month before the November 10 trade deadline or bringing in a veteran free agent, Pittsburgh has to get aggressive and be extremely diligent in filling its hole at receiver in the coming days.

title: 7 Winners, 3 Losers From Steelers Win Over Colts
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are back in the win column .
At Acrisure Stadium, the Steelers came away with a 34-22 victory over the Indianapolis Colts that moves them to 3-2 on the season heading into a Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Here are seven winners and three losers for Pittsburgh in its first two-score win of the season.
On a day where their wide receiver depth was greatly tested , Freiermuth really stepped up as a weapon in the passing game for Rodgers.
After having just 17 yards and a touchdown in Week 4 against the Cleveland Browns, Freiermuth finished with two scores and 44 yards on five catches in Pittsburgh's win over the Colts.
It was his first multi-touchdown performance since Week 7 last season against the Cincinnati Bengals.
With Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) having been placed on the reserve/injured list while Roman Wilson (hand) and Ben Skowronek (calf) each didn't play in the second half with their injuries, the Steelers needed Bernard more than ever in this contest.
The second-round pick more than held up his end of the bargain, posting six catches for 80 yards and being a constant force in the middle of the field.
Frazier had been the bright spot of the Steelers' offensive line coming into this week, but he had an uneven showing vs. Indianapolis.
Frazier gave up a sack, which was his first of the season according to Pro Football Focus , and he was also called for a holding penalty on what would've been a first-down catch by Brandon Smith in the third quarter.
In his third-straight game commanding nearly all of the touches out of the backfield with Rico Dowdle out due to a toe injury, Warren continued his run of dominance this week.
His first touchdown went for 80 yards on a reception on Pittsburgh's second drive of the day in the first quarter, and he later broke off a 50-yard rushing touchdown in the third quarter.
When it was all said and done, Warren logged 101 yards on 15 carries to go with six receptions for 87 yards in the win.
There was some hope that Metcalf was trending in the right direction after putting up 115 yards vs. Cleveland last week.
Against the Colts, however, he was extremely quiet. Metcalf had only three catches for 12 yards, which was his lowest single-game output in the latter category since the Steelers' win over Indianapolis in Week 9 last season.
Rodgers was not sharp in the Steelers' Week 4 loss to the Browns, though he bounced back against the Colts.
The 42-year-old opened the game 11-of-11 for 116 yards and two touchdowns, and he closed the day with 235 yards and three touchdowns on 22-of-31 passing.
Rodgers was in command the entire way through, and it helped lead to Pittsburgh's highest point total in a single game since Week 11 of the 2025 campaign.
The Steelers had just one sack in this game, which belonged to Cam Heyward.
That doesn't mean Highsmith wasn't giving Colts left tackle Bernhard Raimann fits though, as he finished with a season-high four pressures (per Pro Football Focus ).
Queen has been a liability all year long for Pittsburgh at inside linebacker, and that didn't change in this contest.
According to SumerSports, Queen allowed three receptions on three targets in coverage for 36 yards while also missing a tackle ( per PFF ) and not contributing much against the run.
Samuel Jr. turned in what was arguably his best game for Pittsburgh up to this point.
Down Jamel Dean, who was inactive due to an ankle injury, Samuel Jr. posted four pass breakups (including multiple in the end zone) while allowing only 36 yards and three catches on 11 targets in coverage (per SumerSports ).

title: Steelers' Aaron Rodgers Honors Mike Tomlin After Win Over Colts
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers made sure to shout out his former head coach after the team's 34-22 Week 5 victory over the Indianapolis Colts .
In his postgame press conference , Rodgers was wearing a shirt that read "DGBTTF", which means "don't get beat to the flat."
The future Hall of Famer was asked whether that was a coincidence or a warning to the Colts' defense, and Rodgers explained that it was "an ode" to Tomlin since he often used that phrase.
"No it's not a warning," Rodgers said. "It's an ode to Mike T. He used to always say, 'don't get beat to the flat.'"
Rodgers has been rather hold and cold for the Steelers in his final season before retirement.
The 42-year-old was really solid against the Atlanta Falcons and Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1 and 3, respectively, while going through some struggles in Weeks 2 and 4 vs. the New England Patriots and Cleveland Browns, respectively.
The common denominator for a strong outing from Rodgers has been good pass protection up front from Pittsburgh's offensive line. He was sacked five times against the Browns and didn't have much time to operate, which played a big role in how inconsistent he was, but the unit really clutched up vs. Indianapolis.
Rodgers was sacked just one time, and he had plenty of time to sit around in the pocket and find his receivers all throughout the contest.
He started the day 11-of-11, and he finished the game with 235 yards on 22-of-31 passing for three touchdowns and no interceptions.
As a result, Rodgers helped lead the Steelers to their first two-score victory of the season and their first since Week 15 of the 2025 campaign.
Without Michael Pittman Jr., who was placed on IR with his foot injury ahead of this contest, while both Roman Wilson (hand) and Ben Skowronek (calf) didn't play in the second half due to their injuries, Pittsburgh needed a collective effort on offense in order to come out with a win over the Colts.
From Rodgers being sharp to the likes of Jaylen Warren, Pat Freiermuth and Germie Bernard all having banner days as the offensive line won most of their battles against Indianapolis' defensive front, the Steelers got perhaps their most complete performance of the year across the board in this one.
They'll have to keep it up moving forward if they want to remain in the hunt for another AFC North title or a Wild Card spot, but it's certainly a huge step in the right direction.
