title: Steelers vs. Colts Takeaways: Offense Just Exploded
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers move to 3-2 on the season and regroup in a big way after a loss to the Cleveland Browns. Leaving Acrisure Stadium for the third time in 2026, the Steelers defeat the Indianapolis Colts 34-22, moving to 3-0 at home this year.
The game wasn't the smoothest victory for the Steelers, but they seemed to be in control from start to finish. Jaylen Warren put the team on his back from start to finish, just like he has throughout the season. Aaron Rodgers helped, though, adding three touchdowns of his own.
This team remains a mixed bag, but one with a winning record. They'll take it.
Opening up the notebook afterward, there are plenty of takeaways that stand out. Let's dive into them.
How many times do these takeaways need to include Jaylen Warren before it becomes too normal for him to play the way he has been. Warren may not just be the best player on the Steelers' offense this season, but the best player on their team.
Warren got things started for the Steelers with an 80-yard touchdown catch-and-run on the opening play of the offense's second drive. Aaron Rodgers got drilled as he dumped it off to Warren, who took it to the outside, beat the defense and took off down the sideline.
In the second half, he got things moving with a 50-yard touchdown run up the middle to give Pittsburgh a 24-16 lead.
He's the first player in the NFL to have an 80-yard touchdown reception and a 50-yard touchdown run in the same game since Herschel Walker did it for the Dallas Cowboys in Week 15 of the 1986 season.
Warren finished the first half with 81 receiving yards and 13 rushing yards on four carries. He finished the day with 101 rushing yards, 87 receiving yards and two touchdowns.
Warren remains one of the best running backs in the NFL and continues to climb up that list. He's playing at an All-Pro level and is keeping Pittsburgh's offense alive in crucial moments. Whether it's being a reliable checkdown or the player who needs to carry the offense through the ground, he's there to be a force.
The Steelers need this to continue, but they also need to be cautious about keeping him healthy. When you have a player as impactful as Warren is, you need to treat them like the superstar they are - and the key piece to the team's success that he is.
Side note: Rodgers' pass to Warren was also history. He tied Ben Roethlisberger for the most career touchdown passes of 80 yards or more with nine.
Jaylen Warren is on a whole other level this season pic.twitter.com/DZ9YDmnLPG
The Steelers need to fix their special teams. Kaden Wetjen isn't exciting but was selected in the fourth round to be a star kick returner. Chris Boswell is missing field goals, including a few before the game, which brought just as much concern as missing them in-game. And somehow, coverage for kickoffs and punts has gotten worse by the week.
The special teams unit as a whole is bad, right now.
It's hard to identify where the changes need to be made, and what's more concerning that is there are some big names within this group in terms of special teams recognition. Ben Skowronek, Jack Sawyer, Travis Homer, Brandin Echols and Cole Holcomb are players known around the league for their special teams play. This season, they aren't getting it done, most of the time.
This group needs to improve or they're going to cost this team games. And Danny Crossman should be feeling the pressure for how poorly his group has performed.
Side note again: This is all outside of Cameron Johnston, who has been phenomenal all season. He's playing like the punter the Steelers have been trying to find for the last 20 years.
Sometimes, Aaron Rodgers is Aaron Rodgers. He did it in the first game of the season, putting on a show against the Atlanta Falcons. He did it again against the Indianapolis Colts, and it's always fun to watch.
At 42-years-old, Rodgers was more mobile than he's been in a while and on multiple occassions extended the play with his legs, finding open receivers after leaving the pocket and keeping his eyes down field.
He was accurate, collected and outside of one missed pass to Pat Freiermuth, there weren't many moments when you were thinking he made a poor play or poor decision.
Hoopin' @AaronRodgers12 | @oti_germie pic.twitter.com/7qWJG3k5hi
It was a nice reminder that the Steelers do have a legendary quarterback running the show. He doesn't always have the ability to win with his physical traits, but whenever he's feeling good, he can do some magical things.
This was one of those games where the Steelers know if he plays this well, they have a good shot to win.
The Steelers haven't fixed anything in their secondary despite changing, well, nothing. This team tried to give Asante Samuel Jr. another chance, and maybe they plan on giving him more, but he may not be the answer. Right now, he can't stop anyone or any route. He's the biggest liability on the field for the Steelers, but he's not the only one.
Everyone outside of Jalen Ramsey wasn't on their A-game against the Colts. Daylen Everette didn't play terribly, but he couldn't keep up on every route. Jaquan Brisker continues to go backward instead of forward, and the team has lost so much faith in Rayshawn Jenkins that he didn't play - and Robert Spears-Jennings barely took any snaps to replace him.
When he was on the field, he spent a lot of time pre-snap telling people where to be. That's a seventh-round rookie telling veterans where to be.
It's time for the Steelers to listen to Jalen Ramsey and get Sean Murphy-Bunting on the field. Brandin Echols should also be an option, and it's pretty surprising that he hasn't been. This team needs to find a solution to the opposite side of Everrette/Jamel Dean.
They also need to figure out Brisker, though. The local star has been a liability in coverage over the last few weeks and is seemingly getting further behind by the game. Maybe he just needs DeShon Elliott back to support him, but something needs to be figured out.
The Steelers lost Roman Wilson right at the end of the first half after he suffered a hand injury. How quickly the team ruled him out for the game raises concerns, and if Wilson is set to miss time because of the injury, he leaves Pittsburgh with two starters - DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.
He wasn't alone, though. Ben Skowronek left the game with a calf injury and was unable to return. It's unknown what he's exactly dealing with and if he'll miss time as well.
That leaves the Steelers with Metcalf, Bernard and Kaden Wetjen. That's their only three healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Brandon Smith is expected to be called up to help off of the practice squad.
That's not enough, even with Smith. This team needs to add help immediately. Maybe they start by seeing if Wetjen can be part of the offense and if Smith is good enough to contribute consistently. Brandon Johnson is another veteran on their practice squad they can utilize.
Names like Tyreek Hill, JuJu Smith-Schuster and Gabe Davis may need to be on their radar leaving this game, though.

title: Steelers WR Situation Gets Worse After Roman Wilson Injury
full_text:
One of the Pittsburgh Steelers ' top wide receivers suffered an injury at the end of the first half that will keep him out for the remainder of the team's Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts.
On one of the final plays of the second quarter, Aaron Rodgers attempted an 11-yard pass to Roman Wilson that was initially ruled complete at Indianapolis' 19-yard line.
It was subsequently reviewed and overturned to incomplete, though that wasn't the most important development to come out of the play for the Steelers.
Wilson has seen grabbing his wrist/hand as he headed to the sideline, and he was later ruled out for the remainder of the contest with a hand injury.
Before departing the game, Wilson had not recorded a catch, and the play on which he got hurt was his only target as well.
With Ben Skowronek also having been ruled out due to a calf injury while Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on the reserve/injured list with his foot injury on October 10, the Steelers now have a complete lack of depth at wide receiver.
DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard will have to do most of the heavylifting for Pittsburgh the rest of the way against the Colts.
The Steelers will likely also lean quite a bit on 12-personnel packages in which Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington are on the field at the same time as a means of making up for their deficiency at receiver.
Pittsburgh elevated training camp standout Brandon Smith from its practice squad after placing Pittman Jr. on IR, though Kaden Wetjen is the only other healthy receiver on the team's 53-man roster.
While the Steelers can get through the rest of their matchup vs. the Colts without much of a depth chart at receiver, their long-term standing at the position depends on the severity of Wilson and Skowronek's injuries.
Because Pittman Jr. will be forced to miss at least three more contests beyond this week, Pittsburgh was already in the market to make a move at receiver.
If Wilson and Skowronek have to miss any additional time with their injuries, the team would then be further incentivized to make an addition.
Perhaps Smith could sign to the 53-man roster if that ends up being the case, though there could also be more transactions on the horizon.

title: Steelers' T.J. Watt Injured After Getting Hit in Face vs. Colts
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers battled the Indianapolis Colts on a rainy afternoon, as two 2-2 squads battled for momentum in the early part of the regular season. Despite the bad weather, the two teams played surprisingly clean football through the opening half.
With those sloppy conditions, injuries were on the minds of both the Colts and the Steelers. Lower-body injuries are where the mind immediately goes, but the first ailment the Steelers faced in Week 5 was a scary one that had nothing to do with the playing conditions at Acrisure Stadium.
During the second quarter of the contest, star edge rusher T.J. Watt went one-on-one with Colts offensive lineman Jalen Travis when the Indianapolis tackle shot his hands up to block him, Travis's hands hit Watt up high, and it appeared that his fingers may have gone through Watt's facemask and poked him in the eye. ESPN's Brooke Pryor shared a clip of the play via her X account. In the replay, you can see Watt react to the accidental eye-gouging immediately after breaking off of the block.
ouch. TJ Watt still in the medical tent after this eye poke. pic.twitter.com/QXowRWRTcg
After being examined in the blue medical tent, Watt returned to the team's bench. He was shown on the television broadcast icing his right eye. NFL Network's Tracy Wolfson shared while reporting from the sidelines that Watt was questionable to return and the Steelers had added a visor to his facemask for added protection.
Losing T.J. Watt is the last thing the Steelers want to see happen, but of all positions on the defense, edge rusher is one they can afford a hit or two.
The Steelers have one of the deepest outside linebacker rooms in the NFL, and that comes in handy when your leader and top player goes down. Behind Watt, the Steelers have another Pro Bowl level player in Alex Highsmith and a quality starter in Nick Herbig. Throw in second-year rotational player Jack Sawyer, and there is a high level of comfort moving forward.
Should Watt miss time, Highsmith and Herbig would assume the majority of the snaps on the edge. The trio has split time over the first five weeks, but they can.
It's only Week 5, but an early race is emerging for the Defensive Player of the Year award. Once again. Watt is at the center of those conversations. He's been an absolute game-wrecker in 2026, posting 4.5 sacks in four contests, a forced fumble, and two passes defended.
Watt has seemingly reverted to his vintage self, and that would be cemented by winning the second DPOY of his storied NFL career.

title: Steelers Out of Marvin Harrison Jr. Race
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will not be the landing spot for a former top pick.
According to insider Mark Kaboly, Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is not heading to the Steelers, though he is expected to be officially traded in the near future.
"Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade will become official either later today or on Monday. Harrison is NOT coming to the Steelers, I've been told," Kaboly wrote on X.
Marvin Harrison Jr.'s trade will become official either later today or on Monday. Harrison is NOT coming to the Steelers, I've been told. #NoYeet
On October 10, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Cardinals were finalizing a deal involving Harrison Jr., and that the former No. 4 overall pick was told that he would be inactive for the team's Week 5 game against the Detroit Lions as all of the details were finalized.
No destination was announced at the time, which left the door open for plenty of speculation about Harrison Jr.'s landing spot.
As such, there was at least a possibility that Pittsburgh was among the suitors for Harrison Jr. The team already could've used another receiver before Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on the reserve/injured list after aggravating his foot injury, and the fact that he will now miss at least four games further exacerbated that need.
Now that Kaboly has noted that the Steelers won't be the team to strike a deal with Arizona for Harrison Jr., however, they'll have to look elsewhere if they plan on adding a receiver ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
Harrison Jr. would've been an intriguing add for Pittsburgh considering he was largely considered a generational prospect out of Ohio State in the 2024 NFL Draft who hasn't lived up to expectations with the Cardinals.
Schefter also reported that Arizona had been searching for "first-round value" in exchange for Harrison Jr., though, which may have been far out of the range of the Steelers' comfort zone.
It remains to be seen what the Cardinals ultimately get for Harrison Jr. wherever they end up trading him. There are better uses of Day 1 and 2 picks in Pittsburgh's situation, and missing out isn't the worst outcome in the world.
The Steelers will count on DK Metcalf, Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard for as long as Pittman Jr. is out. That's a pretty solid group, but there is room for another mid-tier addition or so if the organization finds a move worth making.
There are other position groups around Pittsburgh's roster in more need of reinforcements, though, so it's no guarantee that the front office will supplement its receiving corps.

title: Three Reasons Steelers Beat Colts in Week 5
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers will be back home at Acrisure Stadium in Week 5 for a matchup with the Indianapolis Colts.
This game will mark the fifth-straight season in which the two teams have faced one another. The Steelers won the latest bout, defeating the Colts by a score of 27-20 in Week 9 last year.
Here are three reasons why Pittsburgh could defeat Indianapolis once again and move to 3-2 on the season.
Indianapolis' defense has been one of the worst in the league up to this point in the season. It is allowing the third-most yards per game (392.3), and the unit has struggled significantly to generate consistent pressure.
According to SumerSports , the Colts' pressure rate of 32.0 percent is the third-worst mark in the NFL.
Pittsburgh's offensive line hasn't done a good job of keeping Aaron Rodgers upright, evidenced by the fact that it allowed five sacks in a Week 4 loss to the Cleveland Browns to go with the unit's allowed pressure rate of 42.1 percent on the year (ninth-worst in league, per SumerSports ).
In the Steelers' best game of the season from a pass protection standpoint thus far in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals, however, Rodgers threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns in what was one of his best performances for the black and gold.
The blueprint is there for a similar outing against Indianapolis, even with Michael Pittman Jr. out after aggravating his foot injury, given that Indianapolis' pass rush is well below-average.
T.J. Watt has completely bounced back from a disappointing 2025 campaign, as he's tied for the third-most sacks in the league with 4.5 while also having a forced fumble (and recovery) as well as a pick-six to his name.
Alex Highsmith isn't far behind Watt with 3.0 sacks, and while Nick Herbig doesn't have any sacks after signing a four-year, $100 million extension in the offseason, his 20.5 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) suggests he's due for some production on that front.
Colts starting left tackle Bernhard Raimann and right tackle Jalen Travis, meanwhile, are allowing pressure rates of 8.5 percent (12th-worst among offensive linemen with at least 100 snaps) and 10.3 percent (fourth-worst), respectively.
Watt, Highsmith and Herbig should all be able to feast as a result, and they could help shut down Indianapolis' passing attack while constantly getting to Daniel Jones in the pocket.
So far this season, Pittsburgh's defense has recorded four interceptions and recovered four fumbles while having a turnover margin of +2.
The Colts, meanwhile, currently own the worst turnover margin in the league at -6. They've thrown four interceptions and lost four fumbles while having forced just a single interception and recovered one fumble thus far on defense.
Though the Steelers will play without several key pieces on defense, including Derrick Harmon (placed on IR with foot injury) and Jamel Dean (ankle) while DeShon Elliott remains on IR after having his 21-day practice window opened this week , they still have an advantage when it comes to winning the turnover battle, and doing so is paramount to coming away with a victory.

title: Leonard Williams Ankle Injury Update: How Seahawks DT Played Through Scare vs. 49ers
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks defensive tackle Leonard Williams had an injury scare during the team's 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers last week. It didn't prevent him from appearing against the San Francisco in a 32-29 loss at Lumen Field on Sunday afternoon.
The ankle injury may have slowed Williams down against the Niners, though. Williams had one assisted tackle and a quarterback hit on Brock Purdy.
As Williams had described before the game, he "heard a little bit of crunchiness" while he was walking off the field during the Chargers game.
"I think at first, just when it first happens and you're out there on the field, the adrenaline's pumping and you hear a little bit of crunchiness or something like that, you always think worst-case scenario. But then once you calm down, go in the training room and they start doing tests on you, you start realizing it's not as bad as you thought," Williams said .
After struggling against San Francisco, you have to wonder if Williams rushed back to the field too quickly.
Williams doesn't have the best luck in his injury recovery.
After electing to play against the Niners, Williams may now have to turn around and play against the Denver Broncos on just four days rest. The two teams clash in the Mile High City as part of Thursday Night Football this week.
Denver possesses one of the toughest interior offensive lines in the league. Even if Williams does play, he'll face a stiff test in the middle of the Broncos' protection.
Williams suffered what was believed to be a low ankle sprain against Los Angeles during a goal-line play.
Very few details were revealed publicly about the injury.
A Grade 1 ankle sprain typically takes at least a week, but up to a month of recovery time. That's the likeliest injury Williams went down with last week.
There's a few ways to get around Williams' injury, whether he sits or suits up against Denver this Thursday.
Seahawks head coach and defensive play-caller Mike Macdonald could get creative with disguised blitz packages to compensate for the hobbled tackle having limited mobility.
Macdonald may want to consider that anyway. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix struggles against heavy pressure.
Macdonald could also lean on Byron Murphy II opposite Jarran Reed as the primary interior pass-rusher.
Murphy had a pair of sacks, three TFLs, and three quarterback hits on Purdy this past Sunday.
Whether Williams sits or plays, Macdonald has good options to hedge with. We'll see what hand he plays in a few days.

title: 3 Observations After Seahawks Loss vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are back in the loss column after falling to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 5 by a score of 32-29.
The Seahawks held a lead going into the fourth quarter, but they surrendered two scores, which ultimately cost them the win at home . Here are three key observations from the game.
With the Seahawks' run game in disarray, Sam Darnold has to play flawlessly as the team's starting quarterback. In the last three weeks, he hasn't really done that. Darnold threw an interception for the third straight game, marking five in the first five weeks. His two turnovers were a big catalyst behind the team's loss.
What made Darnold so successful in the Seahawks' playoff run last season was that he was able to take care of the football. If he is able to do that, the Seahawks' defense should be able to do enough to carry them to victory.
Unfortunately, his interceptions came at inopportune moments, which gave San Francisco short fields. One of them came in the first quarter, which opened up the scoring for the game. Emanuel Wilson fumbled in the second quarter, which also led to a quick touchdown for the Niners. It isn't just on Darnold, but as the quarterback, he is going to shoulder the bulk of the responsibility.
In brighter news, third-year defensive tackle Byron Murphy II sacked San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy twice and established his dominance throughout the game. Players like Murphy are going to make the Seahawks defense incredibly difficult to go up against week in and week out.
As the season goes along and offenses begin to deteriorate due to injury and fatigue, defenses will grow stronger. Murphy will be a big reason why if he can stay healthy.
While it's easy to look at this loss as a massive disappointment because the Seahawks aren't accustomed to losing very often, there is a grain of salt to be had. That's because they did play the 49ers, who are one of just two teams that have accumulated five wins in the first five weeks.
This is one of their tougher games on the schedule, and when the Niners came to Seattle last season, they also took the loss. The Seahawks learned from their mistakes and were able to come back and win in Week 18 in a must-win situation and again in the playoffs.
This won't be the last time they face off against the Niners. They'll get one more shot at them at the end of November, right after Thanksgiving, in a game they should be well prepared to win and get revenge.

title: Seahawks WR Cooper Kupp Weighs in on Controversial Final Play vs. 49ers
full_text:
If not for a Jaxon Smith-Njigba drop on third down, the Seattle Seahawks wouldn’t have had to rely on a miracle fourth-down conversion to Cooper Kupp to try and save their eventual 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
But the Seahawks needed that final play to go in their favor, and without a camera angle that could conclusively see whether Kupp extended the ball beyond the first-down marker before going out of bounds, it didn’t.
The ruling on the field was that Kupp was short, and they didn’t have enough evidence to overturn it.
“I knew it was close, but yeah, clearly it was short,” Kupp said after the game . “So, just not enough there, and you’ve got to find a way to get that fourth down.”
Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold found Kupp about four yards away from the first-down marker. Kupp slipped a tackle and accelerated to the line to gain, where he was met by multiple 49ers defenders.
Kupp slid towards the sideline and tried to extend the football, but all the horizontal angles of the play made it difficult to tell if the ball crossed the marker before or after it was over the sideline.
Cooper Kupp is short and the @49ers take over! @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/k9426I2gFe
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was asked about his thoughts on the play, and he was brief.
“I don’t know,” Macdonald said. “They said he was short, so you’ve got to live with it.”
The 49ers took over on downs, and they were able to kneel it out from there. The Seahawks only had one timeout remaining, and the game clock was under 50 seconds.
It’s a play that will undoubtedly live in infamy in the storied Seahawks-49ers rivalry that has already brought heaps of wild games. Seattle won the big ones that mattered last season, and San Francisco has once again won the first matchup of the season between the two teams.
The Seahawks fell to 3-2, losing two of their last three games. San Francisco advanced to 5-0, and they currently lead a tightly contested NFC West that also houses the Los Angeles Rams (2-2).
Week 6 will be critical for the Seahawks, as they’re on a short week before facing the Denver Broncos (3-2) on Thursday, Oct. 15. Seattle will have to quickly recover emotionally from a difficult, close loss.

title: 3 Winners & 3 Losers From Seahawks Heartbreaking Week 5 Loss to 49ers
full_text:
It was a sloppy game on Sunday as the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers combined for seven turnovers. Each team continually capitalized on those mistakes, with 35 points being scored on those takeaways.
Unsurprisingly, that led to a back-and-forth contest as well, with four lead changes in the close contest. In the end, the 49ers escaped with a 32-29 win as Cooper Kupp came up just inches short of a first-down conversion on their final fourth-down play of the game.
Following the upsetting loss, here's a look back at which Seahawks players stood out as both winners and losers.
Seattle had a 10-7 lead in the second quarter and forced a punt right after taking the lead. They were backed up, but still could have tried to add to their lead. That didn't happen with Emanuel Wilson fumbling the ball away. San Francisco recovered the loss ball at the Seahawks' 11-yard line, which allowed them to score quickly and take the lead, 14-10. Wilson had the short touchdown early in the game but the fumble was a gut-punch that gave the 49ers plenty of momentum.
Seattle needed a big play to take back momentum and Nehemiah Pritchett delivered. With the Seahawks trailing 21-16, Pritchett picked off a pass from Brock Purdy, giving his offense a short field. They covered 23 yards on three plays, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba scoring on a 16-yard touchdown to take the lead back.
After Wilson's fumble, George Holani had a chance to steal some of his snaps and made two critical errors in the second quarter. His first was a fumble after gaining eight yards on a pass from Sam Darnold. He recovered the ball, but might have had a chance to score with a ton of open field in front of him. Instead, the drive stalled and they settled for a field goal.
Holani was given a chance to make up for his mistake, but made an even worse one to close out the half. The defense forced a punt with under 20 seconds to play, ending the 49ers chance to score before the half. Or so it seemed.
The Niners still scored as Holani fumbled in the end zone, with Gracen Holten recovering for a defensive touchdown. That sent the Seahawks into the half trailing 21-13.
49ERS RECOVER THE FUMBLE IN THE END ZONE @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/lwDIn52XVj
There's no shortage of talent on the Seattle defensive line, but there's no denying that Byron Murphy is their most impactful player. He's coming off a breakout season that saw him record 62 tackles and seven sacks, and he just had his best game of the 2026 campaign.
Murphy was bullying his way into the offensive backfield, recording two sacks in the first half alone. Each of his sacks helped lead to a punt, allowing the Seahawks to stay in the game despite multiple mistakes in the first half.
He was also able to come up with a huge play near the end of the game. With things tied at 29, the 49ers were driving to take the lead with just over two minutes to play. Murphy stepped up and stopped Kaelon Black for a one-yard loss on third-and-one, forcing the Niners to settle for a field goal.
The Seahawks had a terrible start to the game, with Sam Darnold throwing an interception on third-and-10, giving the 49ers the ball in the red zone. That set them up for their opening touchdown, allowing them to go up 7-0.
In the second half, Darnold again gave the ball away quickly. This time, he was picked off at the SanFrancisco 44, but they were given even better field position when Elijah Arroyo was called for unneccesary roughness on the return. The 49ers missed their field goal, which bailed Darnold out, but these are mistakes he simply can't make.
Darnold did all he could to fight back in this one, but fell just short. One reason was a pass to a wide-open Jaxon Smith-Njigba that was thrown slightly behind JSN, who couldn't come down with the ball.
Seattle's offense was sloppy for much of the first three quarters, with four turnovers allowing the 49ers to take a 21-13 lead. The Seahawks fought back, however, thanks in large part to Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year continued to provide the fireworks, including a 16-yard touchdown with just under six minutes to play in the third quarter. JSN, who suffered an ankle injury earlier in the game, made a beautiful move after catching a short pass from Darnold to find the opening he needed to get into the end zone.
What a move by the reigning OPOY @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GoZnRMz3om
Smith-Njigba finished with 102 yards on five receptions, but he's only going to remember the one he couldn't haul in, the final third-down play that was thrown behind him, but JSN nearly hauled in.

title: Drake Thomas Injury Update: Seahawks Starting Linebacker Leaves Game In Second Quarter
full_text:
A few minutes after San Francisco 49ers starting linebacker Dre Greenlaw was ejected for some extracurricular activity on the sideline, the Seattle Seahawks may have lost their own. Drake Thomas, on an intermediate pass to Mike Evans (where Evans also momentarily left the game). He went to the blue tent and may not return to the game this half.
With less than two minutes to go before halftime, and Tyrice Knight having been a stud in training camp and preseason to sub in, I imagine Thomas gets at least that much time to get himself back together. Thomas has had a strong start to the season, and would obviously be missed if he can’t return. The injury seemed to be in the leg/ankle region.
We don’t yet have more information than that. With the 49ers about to punt the ball away with less than 30 seconds left in the first half, there should be no need to make an immediate decision on his availability. The Seahawks defense has played excellent to this point, with the 49ers scoring touchdowns on drives that started in the red zone.
The Seattle Seahawks had a disasterous end to the first half, with George Holani fumbling for the second time of the game at the goal line with almost no time left to give the San Francisco 49ers a touchdown to take an 8 point lead into halftime. Amid that mess was an announcement that Thomas had an ankle injury, and his return is questionable.
This does present a good opportunity for Tyrice Knight, who as said before, was a stud in preseason and training camp. But this team does prefer Thomas out there. Of course, the defense is the least of their problems right now, as San Francisco has just 112 offensive yards in the first half. All 21 points have come with minimal or no work from the offense.
If Seattle's offense can't figure something out, then the defense is going to have to pull out something superhuman to win this game. The offense has failed them repeatedly, and is putting them in terrible situations. That they've held San Francisco to 21 points, as off as that may sound, is credit to their play. But there's a full half of football remaining for the Seahawks to rewrite this script.

title: Seahawks Confidence Meter: Leonard Williams an X-Factor vs 49ers
full_text:
The injury bug hasn’t been kind to the Seattle Seahawks (3-1). The Seahawks are seeing the biggest injuries in their secondary, mostly in their safeties, and their rookie starting running back Jadarian Price is on IR. Late in the Week 4 home win over the Los Angeles Chargers, veteran Leonard Williams was down with an ankle injury.
​There were real concerns that Williams would miss the critical Week 5 home game versus the San Francisco 49ers (4-0). He missed Thursday’s practice after being limited on Wednesday’s practice. It was revealed on Friday that he would play on Sunday, which should be a huge sign of relief for the Seahawks. Williams might be Seattle’s most crucial player on Sunday.
​Williams is arguably one of the Seahawks’ most important defenders , along with linebacker Ernest Jones IV and cornerback Devon Witherspoon. Not only is he the leader on the defensive line, but he sets up the tempo and the intensity for the Dark Side Defense.
​In Week 1 of the game versus the 49ers last season, Williams accounted for a season-high seven total tackles, a tackle for loss and a quarterback hit. In the regular-season finale in Week 18 last season, the 49ers' offense focused their attention on Williams at the line of scrimmage. This allowed the rest of the Seahawks' defense to crash the line of scrimmage. Finally, in the 41-6 Divisional Round win, Williams accounted for two total tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss and two quarterback hits.
Williams is one of the key reasons why 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey is averaging only 3.2 yards or less versus the three games versus Seattle. The Seahawks haven't allowed McCaffrey to account for a rushing or receiving touchdown in the last five games. Williams has also been key in suppressing 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy by pressuring him, sacking him or keeping him from rushing for more yards in RPO.
The 49ers will be the Seahawks’ biggest test so far this season. San Francisco’s offensive line hasn’t allowed a sack in any of the four games this season and it faced the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos. One good reason is Purdy’s ability to escape the pocket and evade pressure. Purdy has played like one of the league’s best players, but he now faces Williams and the Dark Side Defense.
​The Seahawks will be the 49ers’ biggest test yet this season . Seattle ranks in the top five in most defensive categories through the first four games of the season. Seattle ranks first in the league in passing yards allowed per game, total yards allowed per game and tackles for loss. Williams is a big reason for that.
​He accounted for 13 total tackles, nine solo tackles, six quarterback hits, five tackles for loss and three sacks. If he isn't limited against the 49ers, there is a great chance it will be a battle every yard, every play. The Seahawks need Williams to be the X-Factor, even if he isn't 100%.

title: Trevon Diggs Gets More Opportunities With Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
This 2026 NFL Season has been tough for the Seattle Seahawks (3-1) as they’ve been dealing with tough injuries and bad news. The Seahawks have seen injuries at the secondary, with a good portion of their young players on injured reserve. Not only is rookie cornerback Julian Neal on IR , but there is serious doubt that Terrion Arnold will play down for Seattle for a few more months, if able to.
​With Neal and Arnold out of the picture for the Seahawks, it gives veteran cornerback Trevon Diggs a chance to make his presence known with the team. Seattle signed Diggs off the practice squad ahead of the Week 5 home game versus the San Francisco 49ers (4-0). Diggs might get more chances with the Seahawks this season after making his first appearance last week in the 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
​The Seahawks believed their great talent and depth at the secondary would be an asset going into the season. Seattle, however, lost rookie safety Bud Clark for the season with a broken ankle during the preseason.
​Starting safety Ty Okada missed the first four games of the season with a hamstring injury. Their other starting safety Julian Love missed a key game in the road loss to the Washington Commanders. Finally, Neal is on IR with a hamstring injury.
​Arnold, meanwhile, is scheduled to have a court hearing for his eight felonies on Dec. 16. He isn’t likely to play a down for the Seahawks and remains on the commissioner’s exempt list while the legal process continues. The Seahawks haven’t devoted a lot of resources to having Arnold be on the field early, but they would’ve liked for him to be a top-tier coverage corner.
​The good news for Seattle is that it still has Diggs, who made his first appearance for the Seahawks in Week 4. Diggs participated in meaningful snaps for the Seahawks against the Chargers’ defense last week. He didn’t account for a tackle or a pass breakup, but he also didn’t allow a reception in the game.
​The Seahawks have been determined to keep developing their role players to help build depth. Diggs is now one of the only cornerbacks on the roster Seattle can turn to outside of Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe and Nehemiah Pritchett. The Seahawks could also turn to rookie Avery Smith, an undrafted free agent the Seahawks traded for right after training camp ended. Smith didn’t play in the last two games as a healthy scratch.
​Diggs is at his healthiest he has been in the last few seasons and he possesses great experience . The Seahawks might utilize him on the same level as Pritchett, who has been one of Seattle’s ascending coverage players.

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 5 Clash vs. 49ers
full_text:
Dating back to 2022, the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers have met a total of 10 times in four seasons. There were playoff clashes in 2022, won by the Niners, and this past season— a 41-6 victory in the divisional round that propelled Mike Macdonald’s club to an eventual victory in Super Bowl LX.
Including that postseason clash, the Seahawks have won three of the last four meetings. Can Macdonald make it four out of five as he renews acquaintances with Kyle Shanahan? These three encounters could tell the story.
Seattle’s offensive front has been solid this season. Entering Week 5, they were the 10th-ranked unit by Pro Football Focus , up two spots from a week ago. The ‘Hawks have given up just six sacks in four games. Running back Jadarian Price is currently on injured reserve and it’s been backfield by committee, but the Seahawks are still averaging a respectable 110.3 yards per game on the ground.
Center Jalen Sundell has been solid at the pivot, but he faces an enormous challenge in four-time Pro Bowler and four-time First Team All-Pro Fred Warner. He was lost after six games this past season, but four weeks into 2026 and he leads the club with 40 tackles, two QB hits, three passes defensed, and a pair of forced fumbles.
56 YARD TOUCHDOWN FOR THE PEOPLES TIGHT END GEORGE KITTLE! #NFL #Broncos #BroncosCountry #49ers #FTTB #DENvsSF pic.twitter.com/qq3V6QdKZZ
While veteran newcomer Mike Evans actually leads Shanahan’s team with 17 receptions, running back Christian McCaffrey and tight end George Kittle are right on the former Buccaneer’s heels with 16 grabs. However, the latter has a club-high 244 receiving yards, and a team-best four touchdown receptions are the most by a tight end in the league this season to date.
Perhaps it’s no coincidence that the Seahawks’ lone loss this season at Washington in Week 3 was the one game safety Julian Love missed. In his three appearances, he’s fifth on the team with 14 tackles. He leads the club with two interceptions and four passes defensed. Seattle has given up a combined 40 points and four offensive TDs in its three victories while allowing three offensive touchdowns in the 33-31 loss to the Commanders.
Uchenna Nwosu! Derick Hall! Seahawks win! pic.twitter.com/pLfnlsWN0x
Seattle’s pass rush, led by defensive tackle Leonard Williams and edge Derick Hall, has produced 11.0 sacks in four games. Williams (3.0) and Hall (2.0) have combined for nearly half of those quarterback traps. The latter has played in all four games and made just one start, but has nine tackles (2 for losses), one fumble recovery, and is tied with Williams for the team lead with six quarterback hits.
Hall and veteran DeMarcus Lawrence will have to contend with ageless left tackle Trent Williams, who in his 16th NFL season (seventh with the 49ers) is Pro Football Focus’s fourth-best player at his position —including ninth in pass blocking.

title: 5 49ers Who Stepped Up in Seahawks Win
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers won their most impressive performance of the season, beating the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. It took strong performances from a lot of unexpected names to get the job done. Who stepped up the most?
Evans has been excellent for the 49ers this year. However, whether it be blowouts or injuries, he has not put in a full effort yet. Sunday, we saw the entire skill set of Evans. The All-Pro receiver had seven catches for 114 yards and a touchdown. Evans dominated and averaged 4.35 yards per route run. His season total is 3.05. Anything above two is considered extremely good, which speaks to how well Evans has played. The 49ers made a great addition.
It is almost every week that Halton is being discussed as a player on the rise. The rookie from Oklahoma had three pressures and a forced fumble that he recovered for a touchdown. He is playing more than expected due to injuries around him, and he is taking advantage. You can call him a starter moving forward.
Green has consistently been asked to step up this year, and every time the team calls on him, he delivers. He allowed two receptions for five yards in coverage, and star receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was 1-for-3 when he saw a pass with Green defending him. Green had a pick on one of those targets and added a second interception in the game. He has been a stock-up player all season.
With Marques Sigle on the sidelines, the team called on their former starter Malik Mustapha to jump into the lineup. Considering he was a former starter, the expectations were higher than for most backups. Still, Mustapha lived up to them and then some. Whether he is boosting his trade stock or competing to get back into the lineup, Mustapha made a strong case today.
Dugger has been the 49ers' third linebacker the entire season. So, when Dre Greenlaw was tossed from the game early, the team threw even more responsibility on the rookie linebacker. Dugger lived up to the hype so far. He added six tackles and a sack. For a fifth-round rookie who is new to the position, there is a lot to like in his progression so far this season.

title: 49ers Grades After 32-29 Win Over Seahawks: Mike Evans Dominates Seattle
full_text:
SEATTLE -- The 49ers just beat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. Here are the 49ers' grades for this performance.
Brock Purdy was clutch against an elite defense, and he gets credit for that. When the game was tight in the fourth quarter, Purdy played his best because he threw repeatedly to Mike Evans, his only good wide receiver. That was smart. Earlier in the game, Purdy got intercepted because he forced a pass to his worst wide receiver, Jacob Cowing. That was not smart. Overall, Purdy did the best he could with a depleted supporting cast, and eventually found the Seahawks' weakest link -- cornerback Josh Jobe. As opposed to Sam Darnold, who essentially lost the game for the Seahawks with his two turnovers. Purdy didn't have to win this game -- he just had to let the Seahawks lose it, and they did.
Kaelon Black continued to struggle, but Christian McCaffrey averaged a whopping 6.2 yards per carry without Kyle Juszczyk leading the way. It's almost as if Juszczyk's impact on the offense is extremely overstated. The 49ers didn't miss him at all in this game.
The 49ers had just one quality wide receiver -- Mike Evans -- but he was all they needed. He finished the game with 7 catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. And when the 49ers needed to put together their first long touchdown drive of the game, they called his number repeatedly and he came through. As long as Evans stays healthy, the 49ers offense will be extremely difficult to stop unless the opposing team has three outstanding cornerbacks. Still, Deebo Samuel left the game with a hamstring injury that could sideline him for a few weeks, which means the 49ers desperately need to trade for a wide receiver, preferably a young, fast one who can replace Jacob Cowing in three-receiver formations and on special teams.
George Kittle came down with flu-like symptoms last night and struggled as a receiver in this game -- just 24 receiving yards on five catches. But he and Luke Farrell were a big reason that McCaffrey was so successful running the ball. Unfortunately for the 49ers, Farrell is a horrendous receiver.
I guess this group isn't the best offensive line in the league. Today, they faced their first real test, and gave up three sacks. Left guard Connor Colby in particular gave up two. He remains the weakest link on this line. Still, this group more than held its own in the run game.
This group is playing so much better than it has any business playing. Gracen Halton forced a fumble at the goal line and recovered it in the end zone for a touchdown. He looks like he's going to be a great player one day. Osa Odighizuwa, Sebastian Valdez, Keion White and Mykel Williams played well, too. Suddenly, the defensive line doesn't look like the position the 49ers need to upgrade before the trade deadline, particularly if Nick Bosa comes back. They need a wide receiver instead.
Draymond Greenlaw got ejected after hitting Sam Darnold out of bounds and then head-butting a Seahawks player who wasn't wearing his helmet. Greenlaw is entirely too old to continue making that same mistake. He really is the 49ers' version of Draymond Green. He might get suspended for next week's game against the Commanders. And if he can't play, the 49ers will still win, because they have Fred Warner, one of the best linebackers of all time. Of course, he recorded 10 tackles and a forced fumble in this game. Just another day at the office for him.
Renardo Green is becoming an All-Pro cornerback. Today, he intercepted two passes and broke up three. No wonder the 49ers don't have Deommodore Lenoir shadow the other team's best receiver -- he's the second-best cornerback on the team. No disrespect to him, but Green is better. Lenoir gave up a long catch to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the first half. And despite how well this group played, the Seahawks were one dopped Smith-Njigba pass on the final drive away from tying the game. These teams are so evenly matched.
The 49ers need a new punt returner. Jacob Cowing muffed a punt and the Seahawks recovered it, which kept them in the game. The 49ers might also need a new kicker. Eddy Pineiro missed another kick today, and now has missed five this season. He's becoming the new Jake Moody.
Raheem Morris' defense won the game. It forced four turnovers, held the Seahawks to five field goals, and got the game-winning stop at the end when it pushed Cooper Kupp out of bounds an inch before the first-down marker on fourth-and-10. To be fair, the defense got to face two of the worst running backs you'll ever see in the NFL because the Seahawks arrogantly thought they could replace Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker. Still, Raheem Morris has been an outstanding hire, and he's a huge reason the 49ers remain undefeated. In hindsight, he was one of the best hires of the offseason for any team.
Kyle Shanahan's offense was another story. It had just two drives of 25 or more yards. They had touchdown drives of 18 and 11 yards. Their defense scored a touchdown. Their run game worked when Christian McCaffrey got the ball but Shanahan didn't stick with him. Other than that, nothing Shanahan called worked particularly well until he put Evans on Jobe in the fourth quarter. That was the game-winning matchup for the 49ers. Give Shanahan credit for finding it eventually. In the future, he needs to do a better job of using Purdy's legs and getting him out of the pocket and establishing someone other than Evans as a threat in the passing game. Still, it's been two weeks in a row that Shanahan has saved his best for the end of the game. That's clutch. His team clearly is the best one in the NFC.

title: 7 Biggest Takeaways From 49ers' Week 5 Win Over Seahawks
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers went into Lumen Field to defeat the Seattle Seahawks 32-29. There were a lot of highs and lows for both teams in this contest.
But it had everything you'd expect from a divisional game between the two best teams in the NFL. Let's unpack the biggest takeaways from the 49ers' Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
It was for games like this. The 49ers were desperately missing a true No. 1 receiver in their last two games against the Seahawks. Mike Evans was a massive difference-maker in this game.
He reeled in seven catches for 113 yards, one touchdown, and a two-point conversion. Every time Brock Purdy targeted him, he almost always came down with the ball.
Their connection is insane, especially on the first two throws from Purdy, which were dimes. Evans was Mr. Reliable today. He carried the 49ers' offense, and with fractured ribs. What a monster.
Ever since Nick Bosa was put on the shelf with a calf injury, the 49ers haven't been able to rush the passer effectively. That all changed in this game, as it was very well alive.
Sam Darnold was sacked a whopping five times. He was pressured on a bunch of drop backs, causing him to make mistakes. Osa Odighizuwa, Keion White, and Sebastian Valdez all stood out today. They played a key role in today's win.
And so did rookie Gracen Halton. He deserves his own recognition for this game. The rookie had a dream breakout game. Not only did he register a sack, but he forced a fumble and recovered it in Seattle's end zone.
He caused the biggest turning point in the game right before halftime. Halton has been showing a ton of promise all year, and after a performance like that, he's officially arrived as an impactful player the 49ers rely on.
As great as Dre Greenlaw's energy and emotion are, he can sometimes be his own worst enemy. Greenlaw was ejected after headbutting Ernest Jones, who didn't have his helmet on, while on Seattle's sideline.
The NFL might suspend Greenlaw for that. I'd be surprised if they don't. The league can't let a player helmet-headbutt another without their own. It's insanely reckless, so I fully expect Greenlaw to be suspended for at least one game.
Injuries continue to stack up for the 49ers, with Deebo Samuel as the latest injury. He hurt his hamstring in the third quarter on the play where he fumbled the ball.
The 49ers ruled Samuel out of the game immediately. Given how quickly he was ruled out, you could probably expect Samuel to be out for weeks. He might've torn it. Either way, hamstring injuries take time and are very tricky. Expect him to miss time.
What's wrong with Eddy Pineiro ? First, he was struggling to connect on easy extra-point attempts. Now, he's missing field goals that he'd casually make last year in a pivotal game.
It's time to be concerned about him. Thankfully, he made the game-winning field goal to force Seattle's offense to respond in the final two minutes. If he had missed that, he would've struggled to come back from it.
I think it's officially fair to ask this question now. Raheem Morris has the 49ers' secondary playing at a different level. Robert Saleh couldn't do much with them last year.
That is the biggest difference between the two, along with more trickery from Morris. His defense is not as easy to decipher as Saleh's. He forces quarterbacks to spend more time figuring out what's going on.
That's part of what led Darnold to get sacked and make mistakes. The crazy part is the 49ers don't have Bosa. Just imagine how unleashed it'll look with him back, especially if they add another pass rusher via trade.

title: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Describes Brock Purdy's Mentality During Games
full_text:
Kyle Shanahan's coaching makes it notoriously difficult to impress him during San Francisco 49ers games.
He's relentless in his approach , but rightly so. Football is all about situational awareness and having the ability to anticipate every possible scenario before it unfolds.
Everybody within the 49ers organization always talks highly of what it's like to play under his leadership. He sets high standards for himself and his players, demanding them to be at the very best of their game.
In a recent interview, Shanahan spoke at length about why Brock Purdy is "awesome" to coach, explaining that the quarterback perfectly embodies what he wants from the position.
“On our first touchdown vs Denver, he had an awesome drive. He scored throwing that ball to Deebo and did his little Dougie, but there were a few plays on that drive where I thought he did lose his patience, where he just gave up on things a little quick, didn’t have confidence in them and broke the pocket and didn’t sit there and play quarterback," shared Shanahan with NBC Sports Bay Area .
"Sometimes it’s good, sometimes it’s bad. I remember him coming off the field and we didn’t have any play on the one Deebo scored on. It was an off-schedule and Brock found him and it was awesome. I was like 'Dude, we scored because of you on that drive, but settle down some. There was a couple plays in there that I thought you were losing your patience and getting out too quick' and that’s why Brock’s awesome.
"He doesn’t get offended, he’s like 'I know, it was unlucky wasn’t it', it was two plays he did it on. So you can keep coaching him no matter what the game’s like and you keep it moving after that.”
Shanahan has had multiple quarterbacks in his time at San Francisco, but none are on the same level as Purdy.
This applies to both his ability and his coachability. Purdy's ability to remain composed under pressure is a key quality. The best example is the NFC Championship Game against the Detroit Lions.
Purdy is the ideal quarterback for Shanahan's system. Now, the challenge is to translate that into another Super Bowl appearance and, ultimately, win it all.
They've come close twice, so anything's possible if Purdy remains the quarterback. It's still incredible to think about the circumstances that led the franchise to get him.

title: The One Attribute That 49ers QB Brock Purdy Has Over Elite Quarterbacks
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is again making headlines in the mainstream media.
This time it's mostly praise, which is well deserved. Through four games, Purdy has thrown for 1,007 yards, 11 touchdowns, and just one interception. He's also posted a 126.2 passer rating and a league-leading 89.2 quarterback rating.
He's taken his game to another level, producing at an even higher level than before. Based on those numbers, Purdy has firmly put himself in the MVP conversation and, by most statistical measures, deserves to be considered a serious contender for this year's award.
Yet members of the media are still faltering at giving him his flowers, with LeSean McCoy stating on Speakeasy : “This is the thing nowadays, it can’t just be like he’s really really good. He’s really really good.
"It’s either gotta be great and elite or you’re terrible. There’s nothing in the middle. I think Brock Purdy today, it’s not the first time Brock Purdy has played MVP caliber football, I think Brock is a phenomenal quarterback. He’s really really good. He’s damn good…
"I have a lot of respect for Brock Purdy and if he wins an MVP I’ll have even more respect for him, but for me, being around this game and watching it, and playing in it, there’s no way I’m ever gonna put Brock Purdy in the same boat as Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson. It’s just never gonna happen. But you can’t say he’s not playing as good as them guys.”
Patrick Mahomes aside, given that he's the best quarterback in the league, bringing up Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson completely misses the point being made.
Jackson is 3–5 in the postseason, with 10 touchdown passes, seven interceptions and a passer rating of 84.6. Allen, meanwhile, is 8–7, with 29 touchdown passes and just six interceptions.
Purdy, however, is 5–3 in the postseason, having led the 49ers to both the NFC Championship Game and the Super Bowl. Neither Jackson nor Allen has reached the Super Bowl, despite always being mentioned as the league's elite quarterbacks.
You can make the argument that Allen is the better quarterback overall, despite his relatively underwhelming postseason record. But Purdy has already demonstrated that he can deliver on the biggest stage. That's the distinction being overlooked when the media repeatedly champions the likes of Allen, Jackson and Justin Herbert, who, at this point, has yet to win a playoff game.
Ultimately, the argument isn't necessarily about who has the greatest individual talent. It's about who has actually delivered when the stakes are highest. And Purdy has already done that.

title: 5 Matchups That Could Decide 49ers vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers Week 5 clash with the Seattle Seahawks could end up defining who wins the NFC West at the end of the season . If the 49ers want to win, they are going to need to dominate a few particular matchups.
Haynes has been struggling this year and has been splitting time with rookie Beau Stephens. They are unresolved at right guard. Mykel Williams will rush from the edge, but they love to slide him inside to get advantageous matchups.
Getting him matched up on Haynes is a good way to build his confidence early in the season.
The 49ers did not move Lenoir into the slot last year. So, the Seahawks were able to get Smith-Njigba in situations where he could dominate against weaker opponents. The 49ers have said that they do not plan on having Lenoir follow Smith-Njigba all game. However, in specific moments, they will not be afraid to stick Lenoir in the slot to have him shut down Smith-Njigba.
Smith-Njigba has 481 yards, and the next receiver has 114 yards. If they can shut down Smith-Njigba, the rest of the offense will stall.
The 49ers run defense has struggled this year, but they have been able to establish leads, and it has not been exposed. Meanwhile, Seattle does not have nearly the same rushing attack with Zach Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker out of the picture.
San Francisco cannot allow the Seahawks' unimpressive rushing attack to have the same success that other teams have had.
The 49ers interior offensive line has played over its head so far this season. However, the Seahawks interior defensive line is going to be one of the toughest competitions that this group will face all season. Is Puni really in for a career year, and did Connor Colby take a step forward? We will know for sure soon.
Shanahan is one of the best offensive minds in the NFL. However, he has not been good against McDonald. The Seahawks defense held the 49ers in check all three times they played last season. It is rare when Shanahan goes into a game as the lesser coaching option. This will be a big test.

title: 49ers Could Target Strong Vita Vea Alternative at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are going to need defensive line help at the NFL trade deadline. While the Tampa Bay Buccaneers saved their season with a Week 5 win against the Dallas Cowboys, the team is sitting at 1-4 right now. They could end up being sellers.
If the Bucs are selling, a name to watch for the 49ers that is not Vita Vea is veteran A’Shawn Robinson. Bradley Locker from PFF sees Robinson as a great fit for the 49ers.
“Robinson may not be the flashiest name on this list, but he’s likely to be dealt given his work on the ground, not to mention being a 2027 free agent,” wrote Locker.
The fit makes more sense than Vea from a cost perspective.
Robinson is entering his 11th season in the NFL. He has played eight playoff games and was on a Carolina Panthers defense that turned things around and made a run into the playoffs. In 2021, he was on the Los Angeles Rams when they won a Super Bowl.
Robinson also has 110 career NFL starts. His combination of experience in the playoffs and in an NFL locker room would be an accepted presence.
He is only on a one-year deal. His deal is cheap enough that the 49ers could easily afford to bring on the entirety of his salary. The combination of him not having team control and bringing cap relief to the Bucs makes him an easy target that would cost a late third-round pick.
For the 49ers, they do not need flash on defense as much as they need stability. Osa Odighizuwa is making plays, but is on pace for more snaps this year than any other in his career.
Gracen Halton can get in the backfield, but the rookie has already left a game with cramps . There is a chance he will be hitting the rookie wall with all of the snaps he is getting. The rest of the depth chart is filled out by practice squad call-ups and players who were signed in the weeks after the season started.
Robinson would come in and start right away. He would take blocks away from Odighizuwa and would allow them to keep Halton fresh all year. For a low cost, the fit makes sense. If the 49ers do not want to spend big on Vea, Robinson is a perfect fit.

title: Why 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan Tends Not to Draft Offensive Linemen Early
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' offensive line is one of the most surprising improvements on their roster this season.
It says a lot that, after the first four games - two of which were against teams that made the NFC and AFC Championship Games last season - not a single team has managed to sack quarterback Brock Purdy.
The position group has made a big improvement, whereas for the last few years, it was considered mediocre at best.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan has made only one Day 1 pick on the offensive line in the 10 years he's been in San Francisco. In the end, it was a wasted pick as Mike MCGlinchey wasn't elite and now he plays for the Denver Broncos.
Aside from Trent Williams , whom they traded from the Washington Redskins (now Commanders), the rest of the offensive line was selected in the third, fifth and seventh rounds, respectively. Jake Brendel came from free agency.
Now that the 49ers know that Williams' days are numbered due to him acknowledging he could retire after 2027, the front office opted not to use a Day 1 pick in this year's draft, which received some backlash.
It's all well and good that the unit is playing their best on the field, it doesn't change the fact that they should draft high on a Williams replacement.
Shanahan revealed more on his philosophy on drafting offensive linemen, stating to NBC Sports Bay Area : “By no means do we go into it and say it’s just our philosophy not to take those guys early, but we just don’t take them to take them.
"One thing I noticed a lot in this league, I think a lot of people take Olinemen just to take them. It’s one of safest things to do.
"If you take an Olineman, very rarely are you gonna get questioned. Very rarely does it turn into busts, even if they’re just an average guy.
"A guy who’s in the first round and plays like a fourth round guy, but still plays like a starter, there’s not that much difference.
"It’s hard to find starters, first round, fourth round, whatever, but there’s not that much of a difference until you find like a Pro Bowl type dude.”
It would be wise to find a left tackle to replace Williams before he retires. His eventual absence will be a huge loss to this roster.

title: Why the 49ers Will Beat the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5
full_text:
The Seahawks destroyed the 49ers the past two times these teams played each other, but both are decidedly different teams now.
Those 49ers had Jauan Jennings and Ricky Pearsall as their starting wide receivers. Pearsall had a PCL injury that rendered him practically useless -- not his fault, at least he played -- and Jennings got shut down both times. He caught six passes for 58 yards and no touchdowns total in both games.
This tandem's complete lack of speed allowed the Seahawks' defensive backs to attack the line of scrimmage and smother the short passes and the run game. This explains why the 49ers scored no touchdowns and reached the red zone only once in those two games against Seattle.
These 49ers have Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel as their starting wide receivers. Samuel seems completely rejuvenated, running harder than ever, he's still explosive and has scored three touchdowns in four games.
And Evans is a huge upgrade over Jennings. That's because Evans is a future Hall of Famer, and defenses must respect his size, catch radius, vertical ability and red-zone prowess. So, even when he's limited by a rib injury, as he is this week, he still alters coverages before the snap because defenses are scared of him. His mere presence on the field provides the 49ers with a schematic advantage.
Meanwhile, last season's Seahawks had Kenneth Walker, one of the best running backs in the NFL, and Klint Kubiak, one of the best offensive play callers in the league. This season's Seahawks don't have Walker anymore -- he's on the Chiefs. His replacements -- Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price -- both are injured, and neither will play on Sunday.
As a result, these Seahawks are one-dimensional on offense. And their new play caller, Brian Fleury, never has called plays before this season. And he's having trouble establishing anyone other than reigning Offensive Player of the Year Jaxon Smith-Njigba as a legitimate weapon. That's why the Seahawks offense stinks on third down this season.
Sam Darnold is a good quarterback when he can complement a strong running game, but he can't do that this season. Now, he's the focal point of Seattle's offense, and he's turnover-prone when he's under pressure.
That's why the 49ers will beat the Seahawks on Sunday. They have a better quarterback than Seattle, a better offensive play caller than Seattle, and a more balanced offense than Seattle. And while the Seahawks have a great defense, the 49ers' defense is really good in its own right.
This will be a grim, violent, low-scoring game that will come down to field goals.

title: Week 5 NFC South Update: Are the Buccaneers Still Last in the Division?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their big win in Week 5 out of the way early, beating the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 at AT&T Stadium.
They got to have the rest of the week off and sit back on Sunday while the rest of the league played its Sunday slate. Two other teams in the NFC South played their games, while the Carolina Panthers took the Sunday off too — they were on their bye week, though.
Here's how the Atlanta Falcons and the New Orleans Saints did, and where the Bucs sit in the division — their win changed some things around in the NFC South.
The Panthers technically lead the division because they did not play a game on Sunday, so they still sit at 2-2.
The Atlanta Falcons played a close overtime thriller with the Baltimore Ravens, but they lost 30-23 after a backbreaking Tua Tagovailoa interception late in overtime. As a result, they sit in second with the same amount of wins as Carolina but with an extra loss due to the bye-week discrepancy.
The New Orleans Saints lost their game against the Minnesota Vikings 23-13, which drops them to 1-4 on the year. That game propelled the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to third place in the division, not last, due to New Orleans' NFC South loss against the Falcons and their much poorer point differential.
The craziest thing? With Atlanta's loss on Sunday night, the Bucs are just one game back from the NFC South lead. It would be a surprising turn of events, but if Tampa Bay were to get something going here quickly, the division would still be very much in reach for the Bucs.
That turnaround continues next Sunday. The Bucs face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and they'll try to beat them in Raymond James Stadium to move to 2-4 on the year. A win would be great for Tampa Bay's upward projection, but a loss would plummet them to 1-5 and put most in the organization right back in the hot seat.

title: 3 Buccaneers Players Who Could Be Traded Before Deadline
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers may be coming off a win, but things still don't look great for them heading into the rest of the season. The team is 1-4, and if things go poorly, it could be staring at a rebuild next year with a new head coach.
If that's the case, general manager Jason Licht may want to get some new draft capital. Licht almost never trades midseason , but what if he did? And if he needed some draft picks, which Buccaneers players would he be willing to give up? Who would teams want?
We tried to answer all these questions with three potential Bucs players who could be moved before the deadline:
If the Bucs don't play well leading up to the deadline, they'd probably be down to get anything they could from Chris Godwin. Godwin is 30 years old and isn't getting a ton of use in Zac Robinson's scheme, and there are probably a few teams that wouldn't mind his veteran presence and experience at the position — and maybe a few that would utilize him just a bit more.
Godwin is currently playing on a $22 million deal this year after signing a three-year deal for that much on average. But his last deal is a team option, so any team that traded for Godwin could either extend him to the tune of $22 million more or simply let him walk. Godwin could be a rental for any team looking to take themselves over the line, and the Bucs could get a little capital on top.
Gainwell is another player the Bucs haven't been using much. He's only ran the ball 17 times for 44 yards, just 2.6 yards per carry — he's also only caught 11 passes for 54 yards and a touchdown.
RB-needy teams could easily call about Gainwell if needed. The Bucs have Sean Tucker available and Tucker has looked good in his limited snaps, so he could slide right into that RB2 postion (and he's be a lot cheaper). Any team that wants Gainwell would have to take on his two-year, $14 million contract, which he's currently in the first year of.
This one doesn't feel particularly likely, because the Bucs' pass rush hasn't been great. But if Tampa Bay really wants some capital back before what could be a rebuilding year next year, Diaby wouldn't be a bad player to move.
Diaby is on a contract year as it stands and will be a free agent in March. As a result, any team picking him up wouldn't have to worry about taking on a big contract and could instead watch him to see how he plays — if he pays well, they can extend him, and if not, he'd be a quick rental.
Diaby has five solo tackles and a pick without any sacks so far this season. The Bucs probably want to keep him around for now, but it might be wise to simply listen if a team comes calling.

title: Would Jason Licht Realistically Trade Any Buccaneers Players?
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is approaching. We're exactly one month away, and so any talks or significant developments on the trade market are beginning to fester as we approach Week 6 of the regular season and teams are more in-tune with what they need.
It's been a big week for trades, with center Cam Jurgens heading from Philidelphia to Baltimore and Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. allegedly headed... somewhere after Sunday's slate. More trades will be soon to come, and all 32 teams likely have players that could be dealt this season.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 1-4 heading into Week 6. Things looked particularly dire before the team's 24-16 win over the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, but with a win, the Bucs can seek to become the second team in NFL history to make the playoffs off a 0-4 start.
Do they need firepower to do that? Should general manager Jason Licht go all in and make a trade? Should the Bucs begin their rebuild early and try to get rid of some veterans for extra capital?
Almost certainly not. There are a few reasons, but we'll start with the biggest one — Licht isn't really a big trader.
He's only made one in-season trade during his entire tenure as Bucs GM, and that was when he gave the New York Jets a sixth-round pick in exchange for defensive tackle Steve McLendon in 2020. He's also not a huge fan of giving high value — the most he's ever exchanged for a player is a third-round pick when he traded for edge rusher Jason Pierre-Paul in 2018.
On the flip side, Licht has a bit more recent history dealing aging players to get capital, but never during the season — he flipped cornerback Carlton Davis to the Detroit Lions in 2024 before the season started to get a third-round pick back from them.
The Bucs have a few aging veterans on the team, but they tend to like all of them. Some options, like wideout Chris Godwin Jr., have a contract far greater than their ability, so other teams probably wouldn't bite on a trade for any of Tampa Bay's mainstays.
The Bucs also went into this season believing they were competitive, and even at a 0-4 start, they likely still believe that. The Bucs will try and turn things around from a disastrous start, and with that in mind, they're very likely to stay put at the trade deadline and try to make things work with the talent they have — and they aren't in the mindset of rebuilding.
The Bucs will try plenty of things over the next few weeks to try and get things going in Tampa Bay. Just don't expect trades to be one of them.

title: Why Todd Bowles Was Crouched In Pain After Buccaneers Sealed the Win
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulled off the improbable.
They went on the road as a 0-4 team in primetime with an undrafted rookie quarterback and won against one of the best offenses in the league, the Dallas Cowboys.
It was a thrilling game for the Bucs, who had to fight to the very end to make sure they were able to get their first win.
Once the Bucs sealed the victory with an interception by Alex Anzalone, head coach Todd Bowles could be seen kneeling down in some pain. That caused many to show concern, but we now know exactly what occurred and that Bowles will be okay.
According to ESPN's Jenna Laine, Bowles confirmed that it wasn't anything serious and that he just caught a helmet to the gut that caused him to go down to one knee.
I’m told that Todd Bowles is OK. Several of you asked. I was concerned as well. I’m not in Dallas but just heard back. He said he caught a celebration helmet to the gut but says he’ll be OK. That’s why he was crouched over like this. pic.twitter.com/cDwSSsAETj
For a moment, those who have been critical of Bowles forgot about the football side of things and hoped that he didn't suffer some type of medical emergency.
It's great to get some clarity on the situation, even though we knew Bowles was okay since he spoke with the media following the game.
Bowles coached his tail off in the matchup, showing signs of what this team could be if it all comes together.
The offense did what it was supposed to do by running the ball for a whopping 241 yards. And the defense, while still struggling to get pressure, was able to play CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens tight. The defense also showed up big time by winning the turnover battle with two interceptions and a fumble recovery on special teams.
While the win is big for how the team moves forward, it's impossible to ignore that they did this against one of the worst defenses in the league.
The road ahead doesn't get much easier for the Bucs, but if they are able to carry over this type of play and confidence as a team, they could find themselves right back in the mix of the NFC South.
The Bucs now have over a week until their next game, when they return home to Raymond James Stadium to face off against Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers.

title: Buccaneers Rookie Quarterback Makes NFL History With Cowboys Win
full_text:
It took awhile, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers finally have their first win of the season.
The Bucs defeated the Dallas Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday Night Football to move to 1-4 on the year. They did it with undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels under center, who is filling in for QB Baker Mayfield as Mayfield recovers from a dislocated thumb he suffered against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3.
Daniels played well against the Cowboys, completing 76% of his passes for 178 yards and a touchdown. But he also made history when he beat Dallas at AT&T Stadium, and it's a record that will never be broken.
Per FOX Sports' Greg Auman, Daniels is the only quarterback outside of the NFL's strike year in 1987 to ever defeat the Dallas Cowboys in a regular season football game.
Tampa Bay’s Jalon Daniels is the first undrafted rookie QB ever to beat the Cowboys, aside from a strike game with replacement players in 1987.
That stat makes sense — UDFA rookies rarely ever start football games anyway. Daniels is the first UDFA rookie to start for a team before Week 4 since the 1970 NFL-AFL merger. There have been just 10 UDFA rookie quarterbacks to start a game since 2013 — of those 10, one of them was Kendall Hinton, a wide receiver who had to play emergency QB.
Daniels has done a decent job filling in for Mayfield so far. Daniels has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions on 55 attempts for 337 yards, and on top of that, he's rushed for  87 yards on 16 carries.
Daniels is set to start another game two Sundays from now against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. With Mayfield already looking to come back from his dislocated thumb, Daniels will likely have one more week to show his worth and cement himself as Tampa Bay's backup for the foreseeable future when the Steelers come to Tampa Bay.
The Bucs and Daniels will play the Steelers on Oct. 18. The Bucs have alternated wins and losses against the Steelers since 2002, so maybe Daniels will help continue that trend two Sundays from now.
